places.name: Texas Hill Country Resort (View Cabins; also King Cabin and Ranch House)
places.town: Medina (23195 State Hwy 16 N, between Medina and Kerrville)
places.price_note: Campspot booking page, Sept 2026, before taxes and fees: View Cabin $120 (1 queen), $130 (1 king, tagged Accessible), $140 (2 queens, 7 units). Hideaway Cabin $175, Getaway Cabin $185, King Cabin $285 (sleeps 12, 2 units), Ranch House historic suites $399 (the listing does not say whether that is per suite or the whole house). Bunk Houses start at $85 but have NO bathroom. Official FAQ: free change or cancel up to 7 days before arrival, and booking direct on txhillcountryresort.com is said to be the lowest rate. Promo code WEDDING gives 10% off. No minimum-night rule or fee schedule is shown. Front desk is closed Mondays (Tue-Fri 10-6, Sat 9-7, Sun 8-5), so plan the check-in day around that.
places.group_note: 43 cabins plus a 3-suite Ranch House and 50 RV sites. View Cabins: about 9 units (7 with 2 queens, so about 4 people each, though Campspot does not state occupancy). King Cabins sleep up to 12 (2 bedrooms, futon, loft; 2 units). Getaway (5 units) and Hideaway (8 units) cabins have lofts. A family can book several View Cabins plus one King Cabin at once. Ask for adjacent units, because the listing does not say which ones sit side by side.
places.scenery_what: A hilltop resort on 90-100+ acres. Staff market the View Cabins as having the Hill Country view from the back porch. The grounds have an observation deck, an infinity pool with a hot tub, trails with caves, and dark starry skies. Other cabins and an RV section are also on the property, so there will be neighbors in sight.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The number of porch steps is not published. Cabins have a 'private porch'.
places.access_detail: Campspot lists every View Cabin with a 'full bath' plus 'Air Conditioning · Heat · Microwave · Mini Fridge'. It tags the View Cabin (1 King), King Cabin and Hideaway Cabins 'Accessible'. The King Cabin and Hideaways add a kitchen. Neither the official site nor Campspot confirms parking at the cabin door, and neither gives a step count. Call (830) 201-1895 and ask for the Accessible 1-King View Cabin and whether you can park beside it. The Campspot copy also mentions resort 'private bathhouses', and the Bunk Houses are listed as 'No Bathroom', so avoid those. Lofts in the King, Getaway and Hideaway cabins are for younger family members.
places.flood_note: Hilltop property off SH 16, not on a river. The official site and Campspot post no 2025 or 2026 flood impact. SH 16 between Kerrville and Medina is a winding road.
places.red_flags: A June 2025 Campspot reviewer (RV guest) said 'The place does not have cellular service' and called the access road 'extremely dangerous', with potholes in the asphalt. Campendium (Apr 2024) says 'Twisting road from Kerrville. Take your time.' Having no cell signal matters with an elderly guest, so confirm Wi-Fi or a landline. The resort hosts weddings and live music, so weekend noise is possible. The View Cabins have a mini fridge and microwave only, no kitchen.
places.review_signal: Campspot 3.0/5 from 2 verified reviews: Nov 2025 'Beautiful place, Quiet and Peaceful'; Jun 2025 complaints about cell service, the road and power. Campendium 4.0/5 from 6 reviews (2015-2024): 'Beautiful country side, very peaceful', 'park seems mostly renovated' (Apr 2024). Tripadvisor and Google were not reachable.
highlights: Cheapest private-bath, AC unit on the list at $120-140/night for a View Cabin
'Accessible'-tagged 1-King View Cabin for grandma, with the rest of the family in 2-queen View Cabins or a 12-sleeper King Cabin
Infinity pool and hot tub, on-site pizza and beer, camp store, observation deck, dark-sky stargazing
Free cancellation up to 7 days out

places.name: Tapatio Springs Hill Country Resort
places.price_note: The official site shows no rates. A third-party booking site (h-rez) says 'Rates from USD146'. The $268 upper figure came from the finder's third-party listings, and I could not re-verify it because Tripadvisor, Expedia and Hotels.com blocked access. Official FAQ: a $24/night resort fee (pools, fitness, disc golf, range, weekend live music, parking, Wi-Fi) plus tax. Pets: $75 per pet the first night, $25 after, $150 cap. Official offers: 'Gather the Family Package' ($75 daily dining credit plus a nightly s'mores kit); save up to 18% on 2 nights and 20% on 3 nights; a Road Trip package with a 2-night minimum. Check-in 4 PM, check-out 11 AM, at the Clubhouse desk. The site mentions group buyouts, price unknown.
places.group_note: A standard resort hotel. Room types: King Guest Room, Double Queen Guest Room ('ideal for families or friends'), King Suite, and 4 ADA King Rooms. The site does not state occupancy or total room count. Book one ADA King for grandma plus Double Queens for the rest of the family. A meetings/buyouts page exists for large groups.
places.scenery_what: Every room has a private balcony or patio with 'Hill Country and Resort views': a golf course in a valley, rolling hills, limestone bluffs and big live oaks. It is pretty resort grounds rather than a wild vista, and other rooms and golfers are in sight. The ADA rooms are on the first floor, so their view is probably the patio-level grounds (unconfirmed).
places.steps_to_enter: Zero steps for the ADA Kings: 'a stair-free entrance to the guest room', first floor.
places.access_detail: Official accessible-rooms page: 'The resort features 4 ADA King Rooms with accessible parking spaces and a stair-free entrance to the guest room. Located on the first floor... The bathrooms are accessible with grab bars and shower bench. Two of the four ADA rooms have a wheelchair-accessible shower instead of a tub (based on availability).' Official FAQ: 'Complimentary parking is available in lots adjacent to our lodging buildings.' A third-party listing confirms 'air conditioning with climate control'. I did not confirm an elevator for upper-floor rooms. Book early and ask for one of the two roll-in-shower ADA Kings.
places.flood_note: Valley resort near Frederick Creek (a venue on site is named after it). It is not on the Guadalupe or any other flagged river. No flood notices on the official site.
places.red_flags: The $24/night resort fee is on top of the rate. Only 4 ADA rooms exist, and just 2 have roll-in showers, so they can sell out. Old third-party reviews (2014) describe rooms as 'dated but clean' and 'Rooms were noisy'. Rooms may have been renovated since (the site now says 'rustic-chic'). Pet-friendly rooms may matter for anyone with allergies.
places.review_signal: Tripadvisor, Expedia and Yelp blocked access (403/429). The h-rez aggregator shows 8.6/10 from 4 old votes (2013-2014): 'Beautiful setting', 'dated but clean', 'Rooms were noisy'. The official FAQ page was updated April 2026.
highlights: Best verified grandma setup: ADA King with accessible parking, zero-step entry, grab bars, shower bench, 2 roll-in showers
Closest to San Antonio (about 45 min from downtown)
On-site restaurant La Cascada, 2 pools, fire pits, weekend live music, walking paths
Family Package with a $75/day dining credit and s'mores

skeptic.name: Tapatio Springs Hill Country Resort
skeptic.evidence: The official Accessible Rooms page confirms: 'The resort features 4 ADA King Rooms, with accessible parking spaces and a stair-free entrance to the guest room. Located on the first floor', 'grab bars and shower bench', and 'Two of the four ADA rooms have a wheelchair-accessible shower instead of a tub (based on availability).' So two of the four have a step-in tub with a bench; request a roll-in room in writing. The official FAQ says 'Complimentary parking is available in lots adjacent to our lodging buildings and Clubhouse' and 'Our rooms and suites feature a private balcony or patio' with 'resort or Hill Country views'. The Accessibility Advice page lists an 'Accessible route from hotel entrance to accessible guest rooms' and routes to the restaurant and pool. AC is confirmed by the H-REZ room list ('Air conditioning'). Price: H-REZ shows 'Rates from USD146'. The $268 top is unverified, and there is a $24/night resort fee on top. CAVEATS: check-in is at the Clubhouse Front Desk, separate from the lodging buildings, so she has a short drive between them. No elevator is mentioned for upper floors (irrelevant for the first-floor ADA rooms). The view from the ground-floor ADA patios is not described. It is a golf and wedding resort, so expect other guests and events. No flood impact found.
sources: https://www.h-rez.com (Tapatio Springs Hill Country Resort page)

places.name: Flying L Ranch Resort & Golf Course
places.price_note: NOT RE-VERIFIED. The $134-172/night standard-unit range is the finder's figure from Expedia and Tripadvisor (April 2026). I could not load Expedia (429) or Tripadvisor (403). The official booking engine (flyinglranch.client.innroad.com) needs a bot check, and the official Rates page covers golf only. Prices for the group houses (Colonel's Quarters, Lapham's Lodge, Executive Villa 44, Bunkhouse) are unknown. Call (830) 796-7745. Resort fees and minimum stays are not published. Groups of 20+ can get tailored packages with meals and activities.
places.group_note: Many unit types. B-Side Western Place Suite sleeps 4 (1 King plus a queen sofa sleeper), with 4 upstairs and 4 downstairs units and no elevator. Executive Villa 44 has 4 bedrooms and sleeps 10. Colonel's Quarters has 10 bedrooms with en-suite baths and sleeps 22, including one ADA bedroom. Lapham's Lodge has 10 en-suite bedrooms and sleeps 22. The Bunkhouse sleeps 12. A family can take one group house, or a cluster of Western Place suites.
places.scenery_what: An open historic guest ranch around an 18-hole golf course, with rolling hills and big oaks. Only the Getaway Suite is described as having 'a Balcony overlooking the Golf Course'. It is a pleasant ranch setting, not a dramatic overlook.
places.steps_to_enter: The ADA B-Side units presumably have zero steps (unconfirmed). Fort Apache Cabins: 'This cabin does have steps leading to the front door.' Western Place and Ranch Suites are 4 up and 4 down with 'no elevator'.
places.access_detail: Official accommodations page, B-Side Western Place Suite: 'There are two ADA compliant units available by request, including a roll-in shower.' Colonel's Quarters: '1 Bedroom with 2 Queen Beds (ADA)' with 'Handicap Accessible Glass Shower & Bathroom'. Units to avoid for grandma: Fort Apache Cabins (steps to the door); the Historic Villas (you pass through a bedroom to reach the only bathroom); and upstairs Western Place or Ranch Suites (no elevator). Parking distance and AC are not stated on the page. Request the ADA unit when booking.
places.flood_note: The site says nothing about the Bandera-area flooding. I could not confirm how close the grounds are to a creek or the Medina River. No 2025 or 2026 flood notices on the official site.
places.red_flags: The price is unverified, and the online booking engine sits behind a bot check, so call. Only 2 ADA suites exist, 'by request'. There is no elevator anywhere. The resort is golf-centric, and the Chuckwagon dinner show and bar may be busy on weekends.
places.review_signal: No review source was reachable (Expedia 429, Tripadvisor 403). The official site says the resort is family-owned since 1947 with 'thoughtful renovations'.
highlights: Roll-in-shower ADA suite, plus an ADA bedroom inside a 22-sleeper group house (Colonel's Quarters), which suits the whole family under one roof
About an hour from downtown SA, 'Cowboy Capital' Bandera next door
On-site Wild West Bar & Grill, Chuckwagon Dinner & Show, mini putt, golf

places.name: Mo-Ranch (Pheasant Run hotel rooms; Manor House)
places.price_note: Official site: Pheasant Run is $155/room/night for 1-4 guests ('Pricing is subject to change in 2026'). Manor House Suite $500/night (up to 6). Whole Manor House $1,949/night (sleeps 37). Other options on the official site: Wynne/Flato Lodge $165/night (50 rooms, 2 queens and a full bath each; upstairs rooms have balconies); Casitas $335/night ('Two modern, ADA accessible apartments near the Guadalupe River', up to 4 each); Nicklos Place $2,120/night ('hilltop retreat with a breathtaking view', up to 24); Gatehouse $790 (2 bed, 2 bath). Check-in 4 PM, check-out 11 AM. Golf cart rentals are extra. The dining hall serves set meal times. A Thanksgiving buffet on Nov 26, 2026 costs $48.95/adult, $45.95/senior 65+.
places.group_note: Pheasant Run has 32 rooms for 1-4 people each (17 remodeled, 15 still under renovation), so a family can take a block of neighboring rooms. Manor House has 8 bedrooms, 'most with private baths', and can be booked whole for up to 37. Nicklos Place (up to 24) and the Wynne/Flato Lodge (50 rooms) are other group options. Conferences run most weekends, so book early.
places.scenery_what: A ranch on the North Fork of the Guadalupe with limestone bluffs and cypress-lined river. The big panoramas are at the Catwalk (45 ft high) and Inspiration Point, not necessarily at the Pheasant Run door. The site does not say what you see from Pheasant Run. The Manor House is a stone-and-cedar Spanish-style mansion on the hillside.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown for Pheasant Run and the Manor House. The Wynne/Flato Lodge is two stories, so ask for a ground-floor room.
places.access_detail: Pheasant Run page: 'some rooms in Pheasant Run have different layouts due to ADA accommodations', 'Free parking', 'Golf cart rentals'. Each room has a full private bath. AC is not stated on the Pheasant Run page; the site does note 'A/C and heating' for other buildings. The Manor House has 8 bedrooms 'most with private baths', with steps and ADA details unknown. The Casitas are the only units the site explicitly calls 'ADA accessible', but they sit near the river. The official Land page warns that trails are 'rocky, rough and steep at times', so rent a golf cart for grandma. Call (800) 460-4401 and ask for an ADA-layout ground-level Pheasant Run room.
places.flood_note: FLOOD ZONE AREA. Mo-Ranch sits on the North Fork of the Guadalupe. The homepage links a Mo Messenger issue 'all about the July 4th floods at Mo-Ranch' (2025). The City of Kerrville's 2026 flood page (updated 9/24/2026) confirms a second Guadalupe flood in July 2026. I could not confirm Hunt specifically. Mo-Ranch now runs a 'River Sentry Flood Warning System', and a UGRA siren was expected by May 2026. The site shows active 2026 conferences and booking, with no closure notice. Choose hillside buildings over the riverside Casitas.
places.red_flags: The flood history is real, so get a non-riverfront building. 15 of the 32 Pheasant Run rooms are unrenovated, so ask for a remodeled one. It is a Presbyterian conference center with dining hall hours (7:30-8:30a, 11:30a-1p, 5:30-7p) and weekend conferences. It is the farthest drive on the list (about 1h45 from SA). AC for Pheasant Run is not explicitly confirmed.
places.review_signal: No independent review source was reached. The official site shows active fall 2026 programming (Women's Conference, Thanksgiving Nov 26 2026) and online GuestRez booking.
highlights: $155/night hotel rooms with private baths and golf cart rentals to get around
River and bluff scenery at Inspiration Point and the Catwalk
A whole-house Manor House ($1,949, sleeps 37) or hilltop Nicklos Place ($2,120, 'breathtaking view', sleeps 24) could host the whole family
Thanksgiving buffet Nov 26, 2026, a no-cooking holiday option

places.name: Kerrville-Schreiner Park: Ranch House + Carriage House
places.price_note: Official city fee sheet: Ranch House $200 + tax + $200 cleaning deposit (sleeps 8, linens provided, bath and hand towels NOT included). Carriage House $60 + tax + $75 cleaning deposit (sleeps 6, rented only together with the Ranch House), so about $260/night for both. The Hillside Park Cabin is $125 + tax + $100 deposit (sleeps 6). Hillside mini-cabins are $65 but have no linens or bathroom listed. Cabin fees include a $3 facility fee. The city adds a 3% credit card fee. Cancellation fee is $25. Check-in 3 PM, check-out 12 PM. No minimum stay is published. Book online through the city's WebTrac portal or call (830) 257-7300 (office 8-5 daily, closed Thanksgiving Nov 26-27).
places.group_note: The Ranch House has 3 bedrooms and sleeps 8. The Carriage House next door adds 6 more beds, for 14 total, and is rented only with the Ranch House. A Hillside Park Cabin (sleeps 6) can be added nearby. It works well for one extended-family buyout with a full kitchen, washer/dryer and a fireplace.
places.scenery_what: 'Located on the Hillside of the park in an enclosed private setting.' Wooded hills and wildlife: the city lists whitetail, blackbuck antelope and axis deer, and reviewers mention 'Tons of deer'. There is no long-range vista, and the river side of the park is currently closed.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. Porch and step details are not published.
places.access_detail: Official Ranch House page: 'Two full-size restrooms with a shower', 'central air / heat', full kitchen, washer/dryer, living room with fireplace. It is a standalone house, but parking location, porch steps and grab bars are not published. Call (830) 257-7300 to confirm drive-up parking and step count before booking. Campendium reviewers note 'Giant potholes' on park roads.
places.flood_note: The Ranch House is on the Hillside section, across SH 173 from the Riverside section, away from the Guadalupe. The city park page says 'THE RIVER ACCESS AND BEACHFRONT OF KERRVILLE-SCHREINER PARK ARE CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE'. The 2026 Flood Response page (updated 9/24/2026) confirms river access is still closed after the July 2026 flood. The finder reported 8 riverside cabins destroyed in July 2025 (KENS5, which blocked access, so not re-verified). The Ranch House is listed as reservable online.
places.red_flags: A burn ban has been in effect since Sept 4, 2026, so no campfires (propane grills OK). The river, the main draw, is closed. Towels are not provided. No pets in any facility. Access details (parking, steps) are unpublished. RV-loop restrooms drew complaints in 2024 reviews (not relevant if you use the house's own baths).
places.review_signal: Campendium reviews (through Dec 2024): lots of deer, 'Giant potholes', RV-loop bathroom complaints. No reviews of the Ranch House itself were found.
highlights: Best value for a whole-family house: $260/night for Ranch House plus Carriage House, sleeping 14
Two full baths, central AC, full kitchen, washer/dryer, private enclosed hillside setting
Deer and blackbuck around the house; 5 min to Kerrville restaurants and a hospital
Seniors 65+ pay reduced day-use rates

places.name: Joshua Creek Ranch (Long Haus rooms; Guadalupe Tree Haus)
places.town: Boerne (132 Cravey Rd, about 45 min NW of San Antonio)
places.price_note: The published ranges are MEMBER vs NON-MEMBER rates, not weekday vs weekend. Long Haus non-member prices, per ROOM: Single King $209 (member $179), Englishman Suite $329, Flyfisherman Suite $379. Guadalupe Tree Haus non-member: full house $2,519/night, sleeps 18 (member $2,139); downstairs only $1,439 (member $1,219). Porch Haus $529, Covey and Stone Haus $689 (non-member). 2-night minimum April-September. On top of that: hunting season adds a 15% service fee + tax; summer adds a resort/service fee and a 20% dining gratuity. Meals need advance reservations and cost extra.
places.group_note: The whole Long Haus has 6 bedrooms, each with its own en-suite bath, and sleeps up to 16. Book several rooms or the whole building. The Tree Haus sleeps up to 18 in 4 master suites and 2 sleeping porches, or rent downstairs-only. Branch Haus has 12 more rooms.
places.scenery_what: Spring-fed Joshua Creek meets the Guadalupe River here. The site says all lodging has 'large outdoor patios with stone fire pits and spectacular views'. The Tree Haus is on the river in a 'private and tranquil setting in remote area with amazing views' (8 for that unit). The Long Haus sits near the main lodge and pool, so it is more resort-like (about 6).
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The Tree Haus downstairs-only option suggests a usable ground floor, but that is unconfirmed.
places.access_detail: Official lodging page, Long Haus: 'six separate bedrooms (each with its own on-suite bathroom)', 'Three-minute walk from the main lodge for dining', 'A few steps to the resort-style pool'. A 3-minute walk is roughly 500+ ft to meals, which is far for grandma unless you drive or cart. No ADA, wheelchair, golf-cart or parking info appears anywhere on the site or in the FAQs. AC is not stated. Call 830-537-5090.
places.flood_note: FLOOD RISK. The Tree Haus sits directly on the Guadalupe upstream of Comfort, the stretch hit in July 2025 and again in July 2026 (the City of Kerrville's 2026 flood page confirms a July 2026 Guadalupe flood). The official site posts no flood notice, and damage to Joshua Creek is unconfirmed. The Long Haus is by the main lodge, and its elevation is unknown.
places.red_flags: This is primarily a wingshooting and hunting lodge: 'full wingshooting season opening October 1st', with bird hunting 'September through April', so expect gunfire and hunting groups in fall and winter. The site does not say whether non-hunting leisure guests can book in hunting season. It is expensive after the 15% service fee and tax. There is no accessibility information, and meals are a walk away and require reservations.
places.review_signal: No guest review source was reached. The official news page says Joshua Creek won Orvis-Endorsed 2026 Wingshooting Lodge of the Year (Apr 2026).
highlights: Splurge tier: river-and-creek setting, resort pool, hot tub, fine dining, 45 min from SA
Long Haus: 6 en-suite bedrooms, so the whole family can share one building
Tree Haus downstairs-only ($1,439) for a ground-floor riverside splurge, if flood-safe and open

places.name: Sittin' On Top of Texas!! (Airbnb)
places.town: Bandera (hilltop ranch a few miles outside town; guests say about 15 min to Main St)
places.price_note: Airbnb showed a flat $177.50/night ($355 for 2 nights, before taxes) for Oct 20-22, Oct 23-25, Nov 3-5, Nov 6-8 and Nov 13-15, 2026, with the same rate on weekdays and weekends. Airbnb's displayed rate may already include cleaning and service fees. It was booked or unavailable for Oct 9-11, Oct 13-15, Nov 26-28 and Dec 1-3. Pet fee is $40 for the first pet and $20 for each additional one. There is no whole-ranch option; this is the only rental unit.
places.group_note: Only 1 unit (1 queen bed, maximum 2 guests), so it works as grandma's cabin plus one caregiver while the rest of the family stays in Bandera. Other Airbnbs showed up in the same map area (Timbuctoo 1 & 2 at about $218/night, Last Outpost Sophie's at about $169-181, Josietta's 3BR at about $331), but I did NOT vet them.
places.scenery_what: A covered porch on a hilltop with 'panoramic, breathtakingly elevated views' over hills and valleys, deer at the feeder, sunsets and sunrises over the valley, and a dark sky for stars. It is a gated private ranch; the host's family lives elsewhere on the property, and guests describe 'complete privacy'.
places.access_detail: Airbnb amenities list 'Free driveway parking on premises – 10 spaces', 'Single level home – No stairs in home', 'Window AC unit', heating, and a 'Full bath / but shower, no bathtub'. From reviews: 'you drive up to see the cutest cabin' (2021), and the drive up 'can be a little rocky but I was able to take a 2-door fiat' (2022). A July 2026 guest came with her mother, and a June 2026 guest said the porch breeze is wonderful on hot days. Unknown: the number of porch steps and whether there is a rail. Ask host Karen.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown porch step(s). Airbnb lists it as a single-level home with no stairs inside.
places.flood_note: The cabin is on a hilltop, not in a floodplain. The July 15, 2026 Medina River flood closed 30+ Bandera County roads (Bandera Bulletin), so ask whether the route has low-water crossings. Guests stayed July 30 and Sept 7, 2026, and nothing points to damage.
highlights: Airbnb 5.0 from 247 reviews, Guest Favorite, top 1%
Best 'step out to a view' pick in this batch
Drive-up, single level, shower with no tub
Hosts leave homemade sourdough; very attentive
places.red_flags: Sleeps only 2. Gated private road is rocky. AC is a window unit. No CO alarm listed. Remote, a few miles from town. Fire rules are strict (fire pit only, burn bans possible). Booked out on some fall dates.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 5.0 from 247 reviews (Sept 2020 to Sept 2026), all 5-star. Review themes are views, hospitality and privacy. No access complaints found in 247 reviews.
sources: Airbnb reviews for listing 43715949 (247 reviews read via listing review feed)

skeptic.name: Sittin' On Top of Texas!! (Airbnb)
skeptic.evidence: REFUTED as a family option: the listing sleeps only 2. Airbnb data shows personCapacity 2 and maxGuestCapacity 2, with 1 queen bed, and the host calls it a 'remote tiny cabin'. A price query for 4 adults returns nothing, so it is a couples cabin, and I found no other rentable units on the ranch. It could only house grandma plus one companion. The price is confirmed at $177.50/night flat (Airbnb all-in, $355 for 2 nights) for Oct 20-22, Nov 6-8, Nov 13-15 and Dec 4-6 2026, and Mar 5-7 2027. Oct 16-18 2026 and Apr 9-11 2027 are booked. Access facts: amenities list 'Single level home - No stairs in home', 'Free driveway parking on premises - 10 spaces', 'Window AC unit', and 'Full bath / but shower, no bathtub'. The Airbnb accessibility section is EMPTY because the host declared no features, so porch steps and railings are still unknown. Location: the cabin is 'about mid-way up Mount Medina' (Sep 2026 review), about 20 min to Bandera or Medina, reached by a gated private road. That road is described as 'a little rocky' (2022), and a May 2026 motorcyclist called it 'advanced level terrain'. The scenery claim holds: the porch has panoramic hill and valley views, deer, sunsets and stars, with 247 reviews averaging 5.0. FLOOD FLAG: a Jul 22 2026 reviewer nearly cancelled because of 'the flooding'. The hilltop cabin itself is not at river level, but the effect on access roads is unverified.

places.name: Hilltop View Sunsets Peaceful Nature PrivateHottub (Airbnb)
places.town: Helotes (hill-country subdivision overlooking the north side of Government Canyon SNA)
places.price_note: Airbnb display for Oct-Nov 2026, before taxes (may include fees): $332.50/night for 2 guests, $390.50 for 6, and $448.50 for 8, so about $29/night per extra guest. These are discounted from $370.50, $428.50 and $486.50. A last-minute discount (-$23) showed up for Oct 9-11. The weekday rate matched the weekend rate. It was unavailable Oct 23-25 and Dec 1-3.
places.group_note: Whole house for up to 8: 3 bedrooms (reviews say a king in each), an upstairs loft, and 2.5 baths. It fits the whole family in one place.
places.scenery_what: A backyard deck, hot tub and patio 'overlooking the canyon' (the back side of Government Canyon SNA), with sunsets over the hills and a view from the master bedroom balcony. The front door opens onto a quiet subdivision street; the yard has privacy fences, and neighbors are nearby but 'not on top of each other'.
places.access_detail: Listing 'Must climb stairs': 'Entry one step down into main living area one step up into dining kitchen and two steps down into bedrooms. Both baths have two steps down into bath/showers.' From reviews: the 'driveway is very steep and not lit well at night and several steps inside and outside' (Mar 2026). There are 'deep recessed shower/tubs that can be a challenge for elderly or disabled' (May 2026), and 'showers are sunken... someone older having issues getting in/out' (May 2026, 4 stars). Central AC is listed.
places.steps_to_enter: Steep driveway, then 1 step down at the entry. Another 1 step up to the kitchen, 2 down to the bedrooms, and 2 down into each shower.
places.flood_note: Hilltop home, not in a floodplain. No 2025 or 2026 flood impact found.
highlights: 30-35 min from downtown SA, the closest scenic option
Private hot tub and fire pit with a canyon view
Sleeps 8 under one roof
4.9 from 99 reviews, Superhost
places.red_flags: Split levels everywhere and sunken showers are a real fall risk for grandma. Steep, poorly lit driveway. Subdivision setting, not wild land. A 2021 guest said the master bath window faces the street. Dated 70s-style house; the hot tub had heating problems in 2021.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.9 from 99 reviews (90 five-star, 8 four-star, 1 three-star; July 2020 to Aug 2026). Three separate 2026 reviews warn about steps and sunken showers for older guests.
sources: https://www.airbnb.com/s/homes (Helotes map search, Oct-Nov 2026 dates, 2/6/8 guests)
Airbnb reviews for listing 44263360 (99 reviews read)

places.name: Landmark Inn State Historic Site
places.price_note: Rates on the THC site (Sept 2026): Room 1 (step-free, private bath) $120. Rooms 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are $100 each. Room 4 (upstairs, private bath) $120. Suites: Rooms 7+8 (step-free, shared bath) $160; 2+3 $160; 5+6 $160; 2+3+4 $300. WHOLE INN, all 8 rooms: $840/night, max 16 people. Book by phone (830-931-2133) during business hours, at least 2 days ahead; no same-day bookings. Cancel 72 hours ahead for a refund. $250 smoking fee. The site does not state a minimum stay or taxes.
places.group_note: 8 rooms, maximum 2 people per room. The family can rent the whole inn for $840/night (16 people). Only 3 rooms are step-free (1, 7, 8), and only Room 1 has both step-free entry and a private bath.
places.scenery_what: A shaded 5-acre historic park under big trees along the Medina River, with short trails on 'the Island' and a veranda and patio. Rooms 7/8 look out on the river bottom and the old mill dam. It is in the town of Castroville: peaceful and historic, but no hill vistas.
places.access_detail: THC site: 'At-grade access only into rooms 1, 7, and 8. Private bathrooms only in rooms 1 and 4.' Room 1 is a first-floor room with a queen bed, private bath and 'At-grade access'. All rooms have 'climate control' and 'free parking'. Unknown: the distance from parking to the Room 1 door, and whether its bath has a shower or a tub. I couldn't read reviews because Tripadvisor and Yelp blocked the fetch.
places.steps_to_enter: Room 1: at-grade, 0 steps (THC). Rooms 7 and 8: at-grade, but the shared bath is across the hall. Rooms 2-6 are upstairs.
places.flood_note: The grounds run down to the Medina River ford, mill dam and 'Island' trails, which are floodplain; the guest rooms are in historic buildings above the river bottom. The THC site showed no closure or flood alert as of Sept 24, 2026. No 2025 or 2026 flood impact found.
highlights: Cheapest verified step-free room with a private bath ($120)
Whole-inn buyout $840/night for up to 16
State-run historic site, 30-35 min from downtown SA
Riverside parlor and veranda for the group
places.red_flags: Tiny historic rooms (130-260 sq ft). No TV, phone, fridge or coffeemaker. Front desk is staffed only during business hours. Phone booking only. Only one room truly fits grandma. No hill views.
places.review_signal: Couldn't reach a review source (Tripadvisor and Yelp returned 403). Price and access are confirmed on the official THC page.

places.name: HomeAway Ranch & Wildlife Preserve
places.town: Boerne (334 Sisterdale Rd, about 3-4 mi north of downtown Boerne)
places.price_note: The ranch's cabins are also listed on Airbnb (host Vicky and Micky). Airbnb display for 2 guests, Oct 20-22 and Nov 6-8, 2026: Bird House, Treehouse and Honeymoon suites $156-234. Bavarian $170.50-205.50. Hansel & Gretel $174.80. Butterflies and LoneStar $197-231. Wildflowers $245.50. FarmHouse $254-306. Lindavista $338-346. Lodge $396. Master Cabin $398.50-416.50. Pinnywoods $375.50-433.50. One listing says 9% hotel tax is due before check-in, and there is no cleaning fee if house rules are followed (otherwise $100). Pets cost $50. The official site (homeawayranch.net, dated 2019) shows 'from' $132-176 and says to ask for group or package pricing for up to 50 guests (830-900-0124).
places.group_note: About 9 cabins plus suites; the site says groups up to 50 are welcome. Sleeps per unit: Master Cabin 9 (4BR/2BA), FarmHouse 8, Lindavista 6, Wildflowers 6, Butterflies 6, Lodge 4 (2BR/2BA, single level), suites 2-4. Several cabins can be booked side by side on the same ranch.
places.scenery_what: Oak and cedar woods with free-roaming goats, donkeys, horses and chickens around the cabins; porches and decks look into the trees. A guest noted 'how close together the cabins are', and another mentioned road noise and roosters. It's a woodsy animal-ranch feel rather than sweeping views.
places.access_detail: Airbnb lists the Lodge, Hansel & Gretel and Wildflowers as 'Single level home', all with central AC. Master Cabin: 'It is just 6 steps.' Treehouse: 'Only 4 steps.' Pinnywoods: 'Only 8 steps.' Lindavista is a 2-story cabin with stairs; a 2024 review says it 'needs a handrail'. On the Bavarian Cottage, a 2024 guest had to 'climb a 45° angle on loose rocks to get to the uneven steps without handrails'. A 2023 guest noted 'limited parking (between trees or near the chicken coop)'. A 2021 guest brought a 75-year-old grandmother to Wildflowers and loved it. A 2019 guest mentioned a walk that was 'a good distance, especially for our older guests'.
places.steps_to_enter: Varies by cabin. The Lodge, Hansel & Gretel and Wildflowers are listed single-level (entry steps not stated); Treehouse has 4 steps, Master Cabin 6, Pinnywoods 8. Bavarian has uneven steps up a loose-rock slope.
places.flood_note: Wooded upland off Sisterdale Rd north of Boerne; no creek frontage described. Boerne had a flash flood emergency on July 15-16, 2026 (Texas Tribune), but I found no damage reports for the ranch. Guests reviewed stays dated July 31 and Sept 7, 2026, and Airbnb shows fall 2026 availability.
highlights: Many cabins on one property, good for a family block
Central AC; the Lodge is single-level with 2 baths
Animal encounters and horseback riding for kids
About 50 min from SA
places.red_flags: Repeated complaints about sulfur/rotten-egg smelling water (2016, 2021, April 2025). Last-minute cabin switches or overbooking (2019, 2023, 2025). Roosters crow before dawn. 2025 reviews say some cabins 'needed some love'. Animal tours cost extra (2026 complaint). Little long-range view. No cell service per Hipcamp reviewers.
places.review_signal: Hipcamp 92% (about 142 reviews on the page). Airbnb listings 4.42-4.94 (e.g., Wildflowers 4.73/56, Hansel 4.5/52, Butterflies 4.75/44, Lindavista 4.72/39). Reviews are mixed on upkeep and water.

places.name: Mayan Dude Ranch
places.price_note: Rates are PER PERSON per night, not per unit, and all-inclusive: room, 3 meals, 2 horseback rides a day, and activities. Official Sleep page: Adult $225, Teen (13-17) $100, Child (0-12) $80, plus a 10% service fee and sales tax; add $20/day for single occupancy. 2-night minimum. The deposit is 1 day's stay; you need 60 days' notice for a deposit refund, and cancellations carry a 10% penalty. duderanch.com lists $195 (low season) to $250 (high season) per adult including fees, tax and gratuity. Example: 6 adults + 2 kids is about $1,510/night before the 10% fee and tax. Booking is by phone only (830-796-3312).
places.group_note: The ranch holds up to 85 guests. Staff assign cabins by party size, so a family block is possible. Ask for cabins near the lodge, dining area and parking.
places.scenery_what: A 348-acre ranch in the Medina River lowlands with cypress, a pool, corrals and roaming wildlife (deer, peacocks, turkeys). Trails climb 'to high in the hills for a panoramic view'. The view from the cabin doors themselves is not described.
places.access_detail: The official site gives no accessibility, AC or bathroom details, and the FAQ doesn't cover them. The ranch map labels a 'Stairs' area at cabins 31-36, so some cabins involve stairs. Meals are served at set dining areas (cowboy breakfast area, outdoor dining), which means walking between the cabin and meals. I couldn't read reviews because Tripadvisor and Yelp blocked the fetch. Call and ask for a ground-level cabin with a private bath and AC near parking and the dining hall.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown; the ranch map marks stairs at cabins 31-36.
places.flood_note: FLOOD FLAG: the ranch sits 'near the lowlands of the Medina River'. The Bandera Bulletin (July 15, 2026) reported the Medina at Bandera forecast to crest near 24.7 ft, major stage and near the 1987 record, with 30+ county roads closed. The ranch website shows no damage notice (the homepage was updated April 2026 and mentions Summer 2026 activities), but I couldn't verify any impact. Confirm by phone.
highlights: All-inclusive: meals, rides and activities, easy for a mixed-age group
Family-run for 75+ years
Room for the whole family (85-guest capacity)
places.red_flags: Access, AC and bath are all unverified. Per-person pricing gets expensive. Flood exposure in the river lowlands in July 2026. Phone-only booking; the website is partly stale (2022 summer dates). No special diets, no liquor.
places.review_signal: duderanch.com shows 4.8 average from 359 reviews (aggregate). I couldn't read individual reviews.

places.name: Lost Maples Cabins and Lodging (stretch pick)
places.town: Vanderpool (33557 FM 187, at the FM 187 / FM 337 crossroads, about 4 mi south of Lost Maples SNA)
places.price_note: Official site: cabins 'From $125/night', plus a $25 cleaning fee per 3-night stay, a $50 nonrefundable cancellation fee, and a pet fee of $35 per pet for up to 2 nights; call for weekly discounts. The site sends cabin bookings to Airbnb (host Ronny and Lydia). Airbnb display for Oct-Nov 2026 was $138.50-157.50/night (The Overlook, Luna Vista, Valley View, Lost Maples Lookout), the same for 2 or 4 guests. Peak-foliage weekends were partly sold out.
places.group_note: 7 one-bedroom cabins, each sleeping 4 (queen bed plus a full futon), all on the same RV-park property, so a family can take several side by side if the dates are open.
places.scenery_what: 'Nice cabins at the top of the RV Park. Good views down the valley.' They look over Sabinal Canyon hills with sunrise over the ridges, Milky Way skies and deer by the cabins. It is an RV and camping park, so there are other cabins, RV sites and tent sites nearby.
places.access_detail: Official site: each cabin has a 'bathroom with a shower/tub combo' plus heating and air conditioning. Airbnb, The Overlook: 'There are three steps to get to the porch.' Luna Vista is listed 'Single level home' and 'Perched high on a hill'. Every listing shows 'Free parking on premises'. From reviews: 'The cabins are close together' (Aug 2026). The AC is 'right above the head of the bed' (June 2026). A June 2026 family couldn't find the cabin and 'drove around for an extra 30 minutes'. Stepping over the tub wall is a hurdle for grandma.
places.steps_to_enter: The Overlook: 3 steps to the porch. The other cabins' entry steps are unknown; Luna Vista is single-level inside.
places.flood_note: The cabins sit uphill ('top of the RV Park') above the park's Sabinal River access. Vanderpool and the Sabinal were under flash flood warnings in July 2026 (Texas Tribune 7/16/2026). A July 20, 2026 guest said Lost Maples SNA was 'completely closed' after the flooding and advised staying out of the river, but the cabins kept hosting guests through Sept 21, 2026. The TPWD alert page now lists only a January hunt closure and a screwworm notice, so the park appears to have reopened. Book day passes for Oct-Nov.
highlights: Cheapest canyon-view cabins in the batch (about $139-158)
7 identical cabins for a family block
Fall maple color at Lost Maples SNA (reserve day passes)
Country store next door
places.red_flags: About 1h55m from SA, the farthest in this batch. RV-park neighbors. Tub/shower combos, not walk-in. Loud AC above the bed. Burn bans cancel fires, and no charcoal or propane either. Weak cell service and hard to find at night. Peak weekends sell out.
places.review_signal: Airbnb: The Overlook 4.95 (43 reviews), Luna Vista 4.96 (25 reviews), Valley View and Lost Maples Lookout newly listed. Reviews praise views, stars and cleanliness.

places.name: The Cedars Ranch (Reverie Hospitality) - XL Geodome Suites / Grand Cabins
places.town: Wimberley (506 Burnett Ranch Rd, about 7 mi from Wimberley center)
places.price_note: Kayak prices include taxes and fees and don't say which unit type. The cheapest quote for Thu 10/1/2026 was $137-$308 a night. Over the last 2 weeks weeknights averaged $179 and weekends $347. Rooms actually booked in the last 2 weeks went for $304-$405. Kayak says Saturday is the most expensive night (avg $405), Monday the cheapest (avg $137), and September the priciest month (avg $308). VRBO copies of the big geodome show about $316-$432+. There is a 2-night minimum on most weekends and holidays. Check-in 4pm, checkout 10am. A full-property buyout (sleeps 98) exists, but no price is published. Book direct on Cloudbeds or call 512-877-5371.
places.group_note: The official table lists 23 units, not 28: 10 XL Geodome Suites (sleep 4, king on the main floor plus a queen loft), 5 Grand Cabins (sleep 6, 2 king bedrooms plus a twin loft), 5 Deluxe Cabins (sleep 4), 2 Geodome Suites (sleep 2) and 1 Eco Yurt. A family can book several side by side, or buy out the whole property (98 guests).
places.scenery_what: A 20-acre oak-and-cedar Hill Country ranch. Units sit in the trees, and the dome's big curved window looks out at the oaks and the night sky. There is a resort pool with daybeds and walking paths. It is a woods-and-stars setting, not a sweeping ridge or water view.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The XL Dome puts its king bed on the main floor (queen upstairs in a loft) and has a walk-in shower. Grand and Deluxe Cabins have lofts.
places.access_detail: Official site: 'We have two handicap accessible lodging units' (not named). The Cloudbeds booking page lists wheelchair access, facilities for disabled guests and accessible parking. The XL Geodome has 1 full bath with a walk-in shower and central heating/cooling, with the king on the main floor. The site does not give the distance from parking to each unit, and I found no reviews describing the walk. Call 512-877-5371 to find out which 2 units are accessible and how far each is from parking.
places.flood_note: No report of 2025 flood damage found. The ranch is inland, about 7 mi from Wimberley center. I could not confirm how close it is to the Blanco River floodplain.
places.review_signal: Kayak: 8.8/10 from 10 verified ratings (9 Wonderful, 1 Poor). I could not open Tripadvisor or Google reviews (blocked), and my web-search budget ran out before this check.
highlights: 2 ADA units plus accessible parking (official site / Cloudbeds)
Every unit has its own bathroom and central AC
The whole family can be together: 23 units, buyout for 98
Panoramic dome window for stargazing from bed
Resort pool with daybeds, pickleball, bocce
places.red_flags: The 2 accessible units aren't named online, so they must be requested by phone. The walk from parking to each unit is unknown. Most units have lofts; grandma needs the main-floor king. Weekend prices roughly double weeknight prices. The property also hosts weddings and events, so ask whether one is booked on your dates.

places.name: Spoon Mountain Glamping - Kingfisher tent (wheelchair-accessible)
places.kind: glamping tent (South African safari tent, private pool)
places.town: Wimberley (210 Masonic Lodge Rd, under 5 min from downtown and Blue Hole)
places.price_note: $300-500 a night comes from the property's own comparison article. The booking widget shows live prices only once dates are entered, and I could not get a date quote. Cleaning, taxes and fees are added at checkout. Pool heating is $60/day. 2-night minimum (1-night stays only in gaps between bookings); 3-night minimum on holiday weekends. Full refund minus 3% only if cancelled more than 60 days out; no refund within 60 days. Renting all 3 tents allows small events at the shared Boma pavilion.
places.group_note: There are only 3 tents (Shaka, Chisum, Kingfisher), each for 2 adults with 1 king bed (3 people only if all share the king). ADULTS ONLY: the FAQ says no children or pets, and the Kingfisher page says minimum age 21. Booking all 3 tents holds at most 6 adults. This does NOT work for a family with kids. It works only if the group is small and all adults, or if Kingfisher is booked just for grandma plus one caregiver while the rest stay elsewhere.
places.scenery_what: Three safari tents raised on a wooded hillside at the end of a road. From your own wraparound deck you see oaks and a private fenced pool, plus the outdoor soaking tub. The property promotes Hill Country views and sunset over the Wimberley Valley, and dark skies. Each pool sits behind 10-ft privacy fencing, so the view is partly screened. No neighbors pass by.
places.steps_to_enter: Zero steps for Kingfisher: a long ramp to the deck, then lip-free entry. The other two tents require stairs.
places.access_detail: Official Kingfisher page: 'step-free access all the way in', with 'Accessible parking, lighted walkways, ramps, a wheel-in shower with grab rails'. FAQ: 'easily accessible parking, ramp to the deck, wide paths and doorways, rails in the shower and toilet, roll-under sink, lip-free entry, paved path to the community area.' Homepage: 'parking right outside, a long ramp to the deck'. Each tent has a split AC/heat unit in the living area and the bathroom. Shaka and Chisum are listed as 'requires stairs'.
places.flood_note: The tents are on a hillside, and the property says they are built for 60 mph sustained winds, with a storm shelter on site. No 2025 flood impact found. The Blanco River runs through Wimberley, but the site is described as a hillside, not riverfront.
places.review_signal: The property's own site quotes guest reviews; I could not reach independent Google, Airbnb or Tripadvisor reviews. Access facts come from the official site, which is detailed and consistent across pages.
highlights: Best-documented wheelchair access in this batch: ramp, roll-in shower, grab rails, roll-under sink
Accessible parking right at the tent
Private heated pool and soaking tub for each tent
Split AC/heat in both the living area and the bathroom
Under 5 min to downtown Wimberley and Blue Hole
places.red_flags: ADULTS ONLY (no children; the Kingfisher page says 21+). Only 2 per tent and 3 tents total, so it cannot hold a family group with kids. Strict cancellation: no refund inside 60 days. No firm nightly price without entering dates.

skeptic.name: Spoon Mountain Glamping - Kingfisher tent (wheelchair-accessible)
skeptic.evidence: The accessibility claims are confirmed by the owner's own site, but the price and group fit are wrong. The official Kingfisher page and homepage confirm: 'step-free access all the way in', accessible parking, 'parking right outside, a long ramp to the deck', a roll-in shower with grab rails and a seat inside the tent's own bathroom, wide doorways, and a split AC/heat unit. None of this is independently confirmed by guest reviews; the reviews embedded on the site are mostly about other tents. BIG PROBLEMS for this family: (1) House rules say 'Maximum occupancy: 2', 'Not suitable for children', 'Not suitable for infants', and a primary renter aged 21+. There is a 2-night minimum. The whole property is only 3 couples tents (6 guests max), and the other two tents (Shaka, Chisum) require stairs. (2) The price is far above $300-500. The site's live calendar API (per night, before fees and tax) shows Oct-Nov 2026 weekday median $428 (min $299), Fri/Sat median about $987, max $1,186 (Oct 16-17), and spring 2027 weekday median about $453 with Fri/Sat $866-1,072. A verified quote for Oct 30-Nov 1 2026 came to $992/night rent and $2,379.78 total for 2 nights, including a $95 cleaning fee, $27 management fee, and Texas plus Wimberley hotel tax. Pool heating is $60/day. Scenery: an oak hillside, with the private pool behind a 10-ft fence. A Jul 2026 guest in the Shaka tent noted 'a little bit of noise from the nearby highway and the neighboring property'. Availability: 15 of 31 October nights, 18 of 30 November nights and 83 of 92 Mar-May 2027 nights are open. No flood or closure notice; the site is on a hillside, not the river.

places.name: Your Own High-End Resort ("Fancy Like at Canyon Lake") - VRBO 2783992
places.kind: VRBO whole house (main house + adjacent casita)
places.price_note: VRBO checked 9/24/2026: 'from $689' average a night, and the default quote was '$2,066 for 3 nights', 'All fees included' (host says no hidden fees). Weekend and holiday rates are unknown; enter your dates. The listing states no minimum stay (the default quote is 3 nights). Complimentary early check-in. Events of up to 60 people are allowed (family gatherings, birthdays).
places.group_note: One gated property for the whole family: 6 bedrooms, 5 baths, sleeps 20, 3,660 sq ft. The main house has 3 king bedrooms plus bedroom #4, which is a partitioned area with curtained sleeping nooks (2 queens, 1 full, 2 twins); a 7th bonus bed is available on request. The adjacent casita has a king bedroom, a bunk room, its own bathroom and its own AC. The dining table seats 10 and there are 20 seats in total.
places.scenery_what: 5 private gated acres under mature live oaks, with lawn, deer, swings and benches. The backyard has a heated saltwater pool with a waterfall and a big hot tub, screened by bamboo and oaks. The listing describes it as secluded with 'No neighbors'. There is NO lake view from the house: the listing puts the lake views on a neighborhood walk, and the lake is a 3-min drive (swim beach and boat ramp 4 min).
places.steps_to_enter: None. The listing says 'no stairs required to enter home', and a ramp is available on request.
places.access_detail: VRBO accessibility section: 'Up close parking with no stairs required to enter home. One-story home. Can also provide ramp upon request.' Description: 'Main home is one story and parking is directly at entrance.' Provided: handrails into the pool and hot tub, slip-resistant shower mats, handheld shower heads, and on request a raised toilet seat and a shower chair with back and padded arms. Amenities: 'Central A/C. Guest house also has own A/C. Four separate A/C temp controls.' Gated, covered pull-through parking for 15+ vehicles plus a 2-car garage. The listing doesn't say whether any shower is walk-in or roll-in (the chair helps). A review mentions celebrating 'my mother's 90th birthday' there.
places.flood_note: The house is on the Startzville side above Canyon Lake. It is not riverfront or lakefront, and no floodplain issue was found. Canyon Lake is 98.2% full as of 9/24/2026 (it was 66.8% a year earlier, after the July 2025 rains), so the lake nearby looks full and pretty.
places.review_signal: VRBO: 10/10 'Exceptional', 91 verified reviews, top 1% in the area. Reviews mention multigenerational trips (a mother's 90th birthday; 8 adults plus 2 kids).
highlights: One-story, no stairs to enter, parking directly at the entrance, ramp on request
Shower chair, handheld showers, raised toilet seat and pool handrails provided
Central AC in 4 zones, plus the casita's own AC
The whole family under one roof: sleeps 20, 5 baths
Private heated pool and hot tub, fire pit, game room, gated 5 acres
places.red_flags: It is not really a lake-view property; it's a private oak-shaded estate 3 min from the lake. Most expensive option in this batch. Bedroom #4 is curtained nooks, not a closed room. Confirm with the host which bathroom has the easiest shower for grandma.

places.name: Summit Vacation & RV Resort - Tree Top Villa (3-bed wheelchair-accessible)
places.kind: cabin / villa resort (RV resort with rental villas and cabins)
places.town: New Braunfels (13105 River Rd, 4 mi from Canyon Lake)
places.price_note: Campspot: the accessible Tree Top Villa is 'Starting at $154/night' (3 of these units), the same as the standard 4-bed villas. Accessible River Loft Cabins start at $110 (2 units). Weekend and holiday highs aren't shown without dates. Campspot promos: 25% off 5+ consecutive nights (code 5NIGHTS), plus a flash promo code. The site doesn't state a minimum stay (it says 'daily or weekly stays'). Call 830-964-2531 to book the accessible villa by name.
places.group_note: The accessible Tree Top Villa has 3 bedrooms and sleeps 10; there are 3 of them. There are also 10 standard Tree Top Villas (4 bed / 4 bath, split-level, sleep 12) plus cottages, cabins and tipis on 75 acres. A family could book 2 or 3 villas side by side, but I couldn't confirm which villas are adjacent.
places.scenery_what: A front porch looking over the Texas Hill Country and the Guadalupe River valley. The resort has 253 ft of river frontage with river decking, 3 pools and a hot tub. It is a busy RV resort (66 RV sites), so the foreground is resort grounds, not open wilderness.
places.steps_to_enter: The accessible villa is described as single-story and wheelchair accessible; entry step count isn't stated. The standard villas are split-level with internal stairs.
places.access_detail: Campspot: 'Enjoy a single-story Tree Top Villa that is wheelchair accessible, has a full kitchen, and private bathrooms, as well as a front porch overlooking the beautiful Texas Hill Country.' Amenity tags: Accessible, Air Conditioning, Heat. The official site says the standard villas are 'split-level' 4 bed / 4 bath. The accessible River Loft Cabin has 'a roll-in shower'; the villa's shower type isn't stated. A Feb 2026 Campspot review: check-in was 'easy & smooth, we didn't even have to get out of our car'. Parking at the villa isn't specified. I could not verify the finder's claim that reviews complain about steps at the standard villas (Tripadvisor blocked).
places.flood_note: The resort is on the Guadalupe River below Canyon Dam. On Sat July 5, 2025, the Comal County Sheriff evacuated River Road between Sattler and Gruene during a flash-flood emergency and lifted the order that evening (KSAT). I found no damage report, and Campspot shows 2026 reviews and live pricing. The Tree Top Villas are on the hillside, so pick them over the riverside River Loft Cabins. Canyon Lake is 98.2% full (9/24/2026), so heavy rain could mean higher dam releases.
places.review_signal: Campspot: 4.5 stars, 29 verified reviews (Staff 4.8, Restrooms 4.6). Recent reviews (Feb-May 2026) are positive about clean cabins and easy check-in.
highlights: 3 single-story wheelchair-accessible villas that sleep 10 each
Cheapest family-size option in this batch (from $154)
Private bathrooms, full kitchen, central heat/AC
River access, 3 pools, hot tub, mini golf
25% off 5+ nights
places.red_flags: You must request the ACCESSIBLE villa by name; the standard villas are split-level with stairs. Parking distance and shower type in the accessible villa are unconfirmed. It is an RV park setting. The Guadalupe River Road was evacuated in July 2025.

places.name: Canyon Lakeview Resort
places.kind: lodge suites + lakeview cabins (plus reunion cabin and new glamping cottages)
places.town: Canyon Lake (872 Ledgerock Dr, north shore near Cranes Mill)
places.price_note: Kayak/momondo prices include taxes and fees. The Thu 10/1/2026 quote was $92-$207; in the last 2 weeks weeknights averaged $107 and weekends $135. January is cheapest and June most expensive. These are lodge-suite rates; the 2-bath Lakeview Cabins and the 20-person Ultimate Reunion Cabin were not priced online (book on Cloudbeds or call 210-787-1770). Pets are $25/night and date changes $50. Check-in is contactless (door code texted). Parking: 1 vehicle per lodge suite, 2 per cabin.
places.group_note: 16 lodge suites: Lodge Up sleeps 4; Lodge Down sleeps 6 (queen, built-in twin bunks, sofa bed, 1 bath, downstairs level); Lodge Up Deluxe sleeps 6. There are also 6 Lakeview Cabins (two levels, sleep 10-12, 2 baths, private hot tub), 1 Ultimate Reunion Cabin (3,100 sq ft, sleeps 20, 2 baths) and 8 new Glamping Cottages (no details online). Several units can be booked together.
places.scenery_what: A hillside above Canyon Lake: every unit has a lake view and a private deck, and deer come up to the balcony (free bag of deer feed). The property calls itself 'The Only True Lakefront Resort on Canyon Lake', with a private beach, and there are peacocks. Canyon Lake is 98.2% full as of 9/24/2026, so the water should look great. Guests say the upstairs balconies have the best view; the downstairs Lodge Down deck may be lower and more blocked.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The site is hillside and the lodge is one multi-level building. Lodge Down is the 'Downstairs Level'. The cabins are two-level with the queen bedrooms upstairs (a semi-private king area downstairs).
places.access_detail: Official unit pages confirm AC, a private bathroom and a lake-view deck in every unit, but say nothing about stairs, ramps or ADA. Kayak's review summary advises guests with mobility concerns to request a ground-floor room, says some rooms have a 'Murphy bed' guests called 'dangerous', and notes the lodge suites are in 'one big building'. The finder saw Tripadvisor reviews calling the stairs dangerous and reporting a broken stair rail; I could not open Tripadvisor (blocked) to re-check this.
places.flood_note: The resort is on Canyon Lake (a reservoir), up the hillside, not on a river. No 2025 flood damage found. The lake rose from 66.8% (9/2025) to 98.2% full (9/24/2026).
places.review_signal: Kayak: 7.0/10 'Good' from 315 reviews (134 Wonderful, but 26 Poor and 20 Mediocre). Praise for location, views and deer feeding. Kayak's summary lists complaints about cleanliness and maintenance ('broken blinds, outdated furniture') and mentions bed bugs.
highlights: Real lake view and deck from every unit
Feed deer right off the balcony
Cheapest option in this batch (lodge suites about $90-$135 with fees)
Cabins with private hot tubs for bigger groups; reunion cabin sleeps 20
Private beach and pool
places.red_flags: Hillside with stairs; reviews (via the finder and Kayak) warn people with limited mobility, and a broken stair rail was reported. No ADA info anywhere. Mixed reviews on cleanliness and maintenance, including a bed-bug mention. No staffed front desk (contactless check-in). Only 1 car per lodge suite. Call and ask exactly how many steps it is from the car to a Lodge Down suite before booking for grandma.

places.name: Camp Fimfo Texas Hill Country - Hilltop Coyote Cabin
places.kind: cabin (family campground resort, formerly Yogi Bear's Jellystone Hill Country)
places.town: New Braunfels (520 Whitewater Way, Sattler area)
places.price_note: Campspot starting prices: Hilltop Coyote Cabin from $255/night. The Hilltop Coyote Bubbly Cabin (on the bluff, private hot tub, 'awesome views') is from $305. Preferred Coyote is $285, standard Coyote $255, Willow $214, Bluebonnet $196 and Cypress $177. Weekend and holiday highs aren't shown without dates. Other fees: golf cart rental (price not listed), pets $50-75, early or extended amenity access $10-25. Cabin check-in is 4pm. October and December weekends have Halloween and holiday events, which means crowds.
places.group_note: Each Coyote cabin has 3 bedrooms and sleeps 12 (a queen bedroom, a room with 2 twin bunks, a room with twin/double bunks plus trundle, and a sofa bed), but only ONE bathroom. There are many copies: 8+11 Hilltop Coyote, 10 Hilltop Bubbly and 14 Coyote locations are listed. A family can book several cabins, though I couldn't confirm they'd be side by side.
places.scenery_what: Cabins on a hill above a bend of the Guadalupe River. The Hilltop Bubbly cabins sit on the resort's 'own Texas Hill Country bluff, offering awesome views', each with a porch and hot tub. The standard Hilltop Coyote cabins look out over hills and resort grounds. It is a lively family resort with a water playground, alpine coaster, swim-up bar and river access, not a quiet nature spot.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The cabins have a front porch; the entry step count isn't published.
places.access_detail: Campspot: each Coyote cabin has 'a full kitchen and private bathroom' (1 bath for up to 12), with AC and heat. The FAQ says personal golf carts are 'only allowed if needed for ADA purposes' with tags, and golf cart rentals are available. No ADA or accessible cabins are listed anywhere. Avoid the Riverview A-frames and Treetop cabins for grandma: they have no bathroom, and guests use the bathhouse. I couldn't verify parking next to the cabin or the hill grades. Campspot notes 'ongoing construction in various parts of the campground' (hours 8am-9pm).
places.flood_note: The resort is on the Guadalupe River below Canyon Dam, near River Road, which was evacuated on July 5, 2025 during a flash-flood emergency (lifted the same evening). I found no damage report, and Campspot shows reviews through Aug 2026 and live 2026 rates. The hilltop cabins sit well above the river. Canyon Lake is 98.2% full, so heavy rain could mean dam releases.
places.review_signal: Campspot: 4.5 stars, 88 verified reviews (Location 4.8, Value 4.3). An Aug 2026 review reports 'poor water pressure and unable to take showers' on the last day. Named '#1 RV Campground in the USA' by USA TODAY 10Best readers.
highlights: Big 3-bedroom cabins sleep 12 with a full kitchen and AC
Bluff-top Bubbly cabins have a private hot tub and a view
Lots for kids: water playground, alpine coaster, river
Golf cart rentals; ADA personal carts allowed with tags
Many identical cabins, so several families can book
places.red_flags: Only 1 bathroom for up to 12 people. No accessible cabins listed. Ongoing construction (8am-9pm). The grounds are hilly and reviews say it's not walkable, so drive or take a cart. It is busy and loud on event weekends. Aug 2026 water-pressure complaint.

places.name: Starlight Horizon
places.price_note: Official site says standard cabins cost 'as low as $190 a night'. The Hot Tub Cabin is the same nightly rate. Weekend and holiday rates, taxes and cleaning fees are not published, and the Cloudbeds booking page did not show prices to our fetcher. Every booking is fully refundable until 7 days before check-in. A 3-night stay is mentioned only for a newsletter credit offer, not as a minimum. You can book 2-, 3-, 4- or 5-cabin groupings, or buy out all 14 cabins (up to 100 people overnight) with 'no event fees'. The buyout price is not published. Call 512-859-5810.
places.group_note: 13 identical 3BR/2BA cabins, each about 1,400 sq ft and sleeping 8 (king, 2 queens, sofa), plus one 1BR Hot Tub Cabin that sleeps 3. The Cloudbeds page sells 2-5 cabin groupings for 11-40+ guests. The ramp cabins L, M and N sit together near the pool (J-M are near the pool and games, N is closest to it), so grandma's ramp cabin can be right next to the family's cabins. This is the best budget fit for a big group.
places.scenery_what: Modern cabins close together on 5 acres north of Canyon Lake, with porches, open unfenced backyards, shared fire pits, a pool and a raised terrace. The site claims 'open Hill Country views' and dark skies for stargazing. No lake view is claimed, and the marina is about 12 minutes away. Cabins A and E are at the front, near FM 306. It feels more like summer camp than a view spot.
places.access_detail: Official cabins page: 'Cabins L, M and N have ramps to the front door. The rest are reached by steps.' L, M and N are each listed as 'Stair Free entry'. Amenities list 'Walk In Showers' and 2 full bathrooms in each cabin. Checkout instructions set the thermostat to '74 Auto / 67 Auto', which points to central AC and heat. Parking: boats park 'in individual cabin spaces', which suggests each cabin has its own spot, but the distance from car to door is not stated. The lot is not gated. No grab bars or ADA features are mentioned. Book L, M or N specifically.
places.steps_to_enter: Cabins L, M, N: ramp, stair-free entry. All other cabins: steps (count not stated).
highlights: Cheapest group option: from $190/night for a 3BR/2BA cabin that sleeps 8
Ramp entry at cabins L, M and N, with walk-in showers and 2 full baths in each cabin
Whole-property buyout or 2-5 cabin groupings, with no event fees
Pool, 6 fire pits with firewood provided, yard games, dark-sky stargazing
Fully refundable until 7 days out
places.red_flags: Scenery is modest: 5 acres, with cabins close together. The raised terrace over the pool 'does not have a railing'. The property is 'intentionally dark' at night and hands out flashlights, which is a tripping risk for grandma, so bring a lantern and keep her near cabin N. Cabin N (closest to the pool) has no boat parking, and its car parking is not described. No third-party review counts were checked.
places.flood_note: Upland site on FM 306 north of Canyon Lake. It is not on the Guadalupe riverbank. We found no 2025 flood damage or closure mentioned on the official site, but did not check this against news or FEMA maps.
places.review_signal: Official-site testimonials praise the quiet and dark skies ('perfect for star gazing'). Google, Airbnb and Tripadvisor ratings were not checked because the search budget ran out.

places.name: Starry Hilltop I - VRBO 9700008ha
places.town: Wimberley area (Hays County, between Wimberley and Blanco, near Devil's Backbone)
places.price_note: VRBO shows 'Starting from $205' as of Sep 24, 2026, and says rates include all fees. Weekend and holiday rates were not shown. Minimum stay is not stated. Renters must be 25 or older. Check-in after 4 PM, check-out before 10 AM. It is a single whole-house rental, so there is no buyout question. Managed by Hill Country Premier Lodging (512-847-7460), but the listing was not found on their own site.
places.group_note: One house with 3 bedrooms and 2 baths. The master has a queen bed, and the other two bedrooms each have 2 twin bunk beds, so it sleeps 10 only if people use the top bunks. Realistically 2 adults in the queen plus kids or younger adults in the bunks. There is a dining table for 10, plus an outdoor kitchen and fire pit. The name 'Starry Hilltop I' suggests a sister rental exists, but that is not confirmed.
places.scenery_what: A 15+ acre hilltop. You step onto a large deck with 'long southern views of Hill Country majesty and the Devil's Backbone', with wildlife and dark skies for stargazing. Reviewers mention a 'great view off the back porch' and sunsets. No neighbors are described.
places.access_detail: VRBO confirms AC, 'Onsite parking available', 3BR/2BA, and a queen master bed. Heating is not listed; there is a 100-year-old iron stove in the stone-cabin room. The listing has no accessibility section. Deck and entry step counts, the driveway surface and bathroom shower or tub types are not stated. The finder's note that the listing mentions steps to the entry and deck could not be confirmed in the text we fetched. Rural hilltop access is likely a private ranch road. Ask the host how many steps there are and what kind of shower.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The house has a large deck, and the step count is not stated. Ask the host.
highlights: The best view of the six: a hilltop deck with long southern views toward Devil's Backbone
Whole house on 15+ acres, private
From $205/night all-in on VRBO
Dark skies, outdoor kitchen, fire pit
9.0/10 from 36 VRBO reviews
places.red_flags: No WiFi, on purpose. Two of the three bedrooms are bunk rooms. There is no accessibility info, and the step count and driveway are unknown. Part of the house is a century-old stone cabin, so floors may be uneven. Renters must be 25+. The exact address is not public.
places.flood_note: Hilltop site between Wimberley and Blanco, above the Blanco River valley. It is not in a floodplain as described. No 2025 flood impact was found.
places.review_signal: VRBO 9.0/10 ('Wonderful') from 36 reviews. Quotes include 'Hidden Gem...peaceful with a great view off the back porch' and 'Isolated surrounded by wildlife'. None of the reviews we saw mention access.

places.name: Lagom Retreat
places.town: Dripping Springs (2501 Old Red Ranch Rd)
places.price_note: Official 'starting at' rates per cabin: Nomad $250, Wildwood $375, Hideaway $395, Homestead $425, Stargazer $495, Cabin Anna $675. The site says rates vary by cabin, date and length of stay, so weekend rates run higher. Fees and minimum nights are not published, and the booking app (app.lagom-retreat.com) blocked our fetcher. Dog fee is $200. Exclusive use of the property is mentioned on the Events page, but no price is given. Contact 512-587-7428 or hello@lagom-retreat.com.
places.group_note: 6 cabin types. The Homestead is the only family unit (1,150 sq ft, sleeps 6-7): a king bedroom with twin bunks, a queen LOFT and a full sofa bed, one full bath and a full kitchen. The others sleep 2-4: Nomad, Wildwood and Hideaway sleep 2; Stargazer (3 units) and Anna sleep 4. That is at least 8 units, so the family could take the Homestead plus a king-bed Stargazer or Hideaway for grandma. An events center holds 75.
places.scenery_what: A 36-acre Swedish-style retreat with rolling Hill Country around it. The 3 Stargazer cabins in the northwest part of the property have 270-degree curved floor-to-ceiling windows, so you see landscape by day and stars from bed. Wildwood has panoramic front and back windows, and Hideaway has a mirror-clad exterior. The Homestead's own view is not described.
places.access_detail: Official site: every cabin has climate control or AC, a private full bathroom with shower and a private hot tub. The Homestead lists 'AC and Heating', a king bedroom (the loft is the queen) and front and back porches. Cabin Anna's page warns its ladder loft 'may be difficult or unsafe for... older guests, or anyone with mobility challenges'. No page states parking location, walking distance, entry steps or ADA features. Stargazer has a 'large deck'. Call to ask which cabin is closest to parking with the fewest steps.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated for any cabin. Cabin Anna and the Homestead have lofts, so grandma should take a main-level king bed.
highlights: Every cabin has a private bath, AC or heat and its own hot tub
Stargazer cabins have 270-degree windows for panoramic views from bed
The Homestead sleeps 6-7 with a full kitchen
Can pair a family cabin with a 2-person king cabin for grandma
places.red_flags: Expensive for the space: $425+ for a 1-bath family cabin. Lofts and ladders in Anna and the Homestead. Parking, steps and ADA details are not published anywhere. No third-party reviews were checked.
places.flood_note: Dripping Springs uplands. None of the cabin pages describe a riverfront or creekside location, and we found no 2025 flood impact. Floodplain status was not checked against FEMA maps.
places.review_signal: Not checked. The search budget ran out, and there is no rating on the official site.

places.name: Lucky Arrow Retreat - Breezeway Cabins w/ View
places.price_note: Rates are not shown on the official site, Hipcamp or the Cloudbeds booking engine as fetched. The booking page says 'Room rates do not include Hotel Tax, Resort Fees, or Credit Card Processing Fees', and extra fees apply for a 3rd and 4th adult. 10-day cancellation policy. Pets are $150 each per stay. Exclusive property use is 'inquire'. Check live rates at hotels.cloudbeds.com/reservation/aSxvhf or call 512-400-4197.
places.group_note: 40 units: 6 Breezeway Cabins (private hot tub; the 'Views' version looks over Hill Country), 16 Courtyard Cabins (shared courtyard hot tubs), 5 Porch Houses, 3 Safari Tents, 1 Vintage Trailer and 10 Yurts. Cabins sleep 4 (queen plus queen sleeper sofa). A family can book several cabins or ask about exclusive use. Two pools (one heated family pool), a general store open 8-8 and chef meals.
places.scenery_what: The 'Breezeway Cabin + Views + Hot Tub + Fire Pit' units look out over Hill Country from a private hot tub. The resort markets 'sweeping Hill Country views', a rooftop Sky Terrace and landscaped grounds with trees and peacocks. The accessible Courtyard Cabin #16 faces a shared courtyard, not the view.
places.access_detail: Cabins, Porch Houses and Safari Tents have private full baths and AC. Yurts use a shared bathhouse, so avoid them. Hipcamp: 'Handicapped-accessible rooms are available'. The Cloudbeds booking engine names Courtyard Cabin #16 (Seguin) as the accessible unit, with shared hot tubs and fire pit. FAQ: 'ample parking', but also warns 'there are gravel pathways that need to be considered'. The amenities page says the resort is 'fully walkable from all resort accommodations'. Car-to-cabin distance and golf carts are not stated. Tradeoff: the accessible unit is not a view cabin.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. The accessible unit is Courtyard Cabin #16; step counts for Breezeway view cabins are unknown.
highlights: Named accessible unit: Courtyard Cabin #16 (Seguin)
Breezeway view cabins have private hot tubs looking over Hill Country
40 units, so it is easy to book the whole family side by side
Heated family pool, general store, on-site meals, walking gate to Bell Springs Winery
places.red_flags: Price unknown and resort fees are extra. There are gravel pathways. It is a wedding and event venue with up to 200 guests, so weekends may be busy or noisy. A ResortPass reviewer complained that the yurt-area bathrooms are through the family pool area, with 'only 2 toilets and 2 showers' (applies to yurts and day rooms, not cabins).
places.flood_note: Bell Springs Rd uplands west of Dripping Springs. It is not described as riverside, and we found no 2025 flood impact.
places.review_signal: Hipcamp 100% from 9 reviews. ResortPass has a negative note on yurt and day-room bathhouse access. Tripadvisor and Booking.com blocked our fetcher.

places.name: Camp Lucy
places.price_note: Official site does not show rates; booking is through reseze.net or 512-894-4400. Momondo shows the cheapest deals from $355 and an average of about $539/night. Texas Travel Talk says 'starting at $409 per night'. Rates for the family cottages (Creekside, Lucy's) were not found and are likely much higher. Resort fee is not disclosed. Check-in after 3 PM, check-out by 11 AM. Some rooms are dog-friendly.
places.group_note: 41 rooms, suites and cottages on 282 acres. For the family, the two cottages are key. Lucy's Cottage sleeps 10 (3BR/3BA: king+full, king, 2 XL twins, queen sofa, full kitchen, outdoor kitchen, sunroom). Creekside Cottage sleeps 8 (3BR/2BA). Both sit at the base of the property along Onion Creek. Estate Rooms, some ADA, are up top near amenities if grandma prefers a hotel room close to the restaurant and spa.
places.scenery_what: Rolling hills, old oaks, a vineyard and restored chapel and temple buildings. Vista Rooms have a 'semi-private outdoor patio offering a beautiful view of Camp Lucy's rolling hillside' or a 'ravine-overlook' balcony. The cottages sit down by Onion Creek. It is a polished resort landscape rather than an open panorama.
places.access_detail: The Estate Rooms page confirms ADA-compliant rooms exist ('stone bathtub... not available in ADA rooms'; glassed-in rain shower instead). Texas Travel Talk: 'plenty of free parking all around the grounds.' The cottage pages say they are 'not walkable to resort amenities due to steep hill — but just a short 1 minute drive', so the family would drive up to meals and the pool. Vista Rooms have a 'step-down living area'. Step counts at cottages and which rooms are ground-level are not published. Momondo lists air-conditioning. Call to assign an ADA room or confirm the cottage entry.
places.steps_to_enter: Not published. ADA Estate rooms exist, Vista Rooms have a step-down living area, and cottage entry steps are unknown.
highlights: Confirmed ADA rooms with rain shower
Lucy's Cottage: 3BR/3BA, sleeps 10, full kitchen, so grandma gets her own bath
Full-service resort: restaurant, spa (Conde Nast 2026 best new hotel spas), pool, vineyard
Plenty of free parking around the grounds
places.red_flags: The splurge tier. The cottages are down a steep hill from the amenities, so you drive between them. Cottage rates are unpublished. It is a wedding venue, so weekends may be busy. The cottages are creekside on Onion Creek, which has a flash-flood history.
places.flood_note: Creekside Cottage and Lucy's Cottage sit 'along Onion Creek at the base of Camp Lucy', a flash-flood-prone creek. The Wikipedia article on the July 2025 Central Texas floods does not name Dripping Springs or Onion Creek, and the official site mentions no flood damage. Rooms up the hill are not in the creek bottom. Avoid creekside cottages if heavy rain is in the forecast.
places.review_signal: Momondo 9.7/10 from 14 verified reviews ('beautiful grounds'). No review comments on stairs, walking or accessibility were found.

places.name: Mystic Hills Vacation Suites - HillTOP Suite
places.price_note: No rates are published. The eviivo booking link (via.eviivo.com/MysticHillSuites78676) returned 403 to our fetcher, so we could not confirm live availability. Call 512-924-9244. Minimum nights and fees are unknown.
places.group_note: A 2-unit adults-only duplex: the HillTOP Suite and the Garden Suite, each with a king bed and sleeping 2. It only works as grandma's room (plus one companion) next to a family house booked elsewhere nearby. Both suites together hold 4 adults. No kids.
places.scenery_what: Official page: views of 'the Texas Hill Country from the Porch'. It is a hilltop suite with its own porch, hot tub, fire pit and chiminea. The extent of the view and any neighbors could not be verified.
places.access_detail: Official page for the HillTOP Suite: 'Bathroom is handicap accessible with stools available for shower and commode', with a separate entrance and porch. Parking, entry steps and walk from the car are not stated. AC is not listed; only an electric fireplace appears in the amenities.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. The suite has a separate entrance and porch.
highlights: Only candidate with a confirmed handicap-accessible bathroom (shower and commode stools)
Private porch with Hill Country view, private hot tub and fire pit
3 miles from Wimberley Square
Pet friendly
places.red_flags: Adults-only and sleeps 2, so it cannot host the family. Price unknown. We could not confirm the booking page is live or that there is AC. No reviews were checked.
places.flood_note: Hilltop location about 3 miles from Wimberley Square, not on the Blanco River or Cypress Creek as described. No 2025 flood impact was found for this property.
places.review_signal: Not checked. The search budget ran out, and no ratings were found on the Wimberley Getaways page.

places.name: Mystic Quarry - Safari Lodges / Premium Tiny House
places.price_note: Live Newbook booking-engine quotes pulled 9/24/26, per night before tax. Safari Lodge: $121.50 weeknight (Oct 20-22), $171.50 weekend (Oct 16-18), weekly rate $128.50. Premium Tiny House with Loft: $181.50 weeknight, $201.50 (Nov 6-8 wknd) to $237.50 (Oct 16-18 wknd). Premium Tiny House (no loft): $171.50-$201.50. Standard/Deluxe/Premium cabins $171.50-$191.50 wknd. Lodge base rate = 2 people (+1 cot for a fee); Hipcamp says the tiny house base rate covers 4 people + 1 vehicle. Extra-person fees not shown. 2-night weekend minimum, 3 nights on major holidays, $45 one-night surcharge. Extra vehicles $5/day ($10 peak). Cancel 4+ days out for a refund minus $25. No whole-park buyout listed.
