places.group_note: Premium Tiny House with Loft sleeps 2-6 (queen/king on main floor, sofa bed, twin beds in a loft reached by a 'wide angled ladder'). Safari Lodges sleep 2 (3 with a cot), and there are only 3 (G6, G7, G8). The park has about 15 tiny houses, 9 cabins, 3 lodges and 5 tipis. For Oct 16-18 the engine showed 4 loft tiny houses, 3 premium tiny houses and 3 lodges open, so a family can take several units. Call 830-964-3330 to ask for side-by-side units.
places.scenery_what: Live-oak campground grounds on the old quarry site. Tiny houses advertise a 'panoramic view of the campgrounds', so you see the park, other units, the pool and hot tub. No lake or ridge view. The Guadalupe below Canyon Dam is about a minute's walk away (per Nextdoor listing).
places.steps_to_enter: Lodges 'sit atop a raised deck'. Tiny houses have 8x15 or 10x12 decks. The number of steps isn't published and no ADA unit is listed.
places.access_detail: Official lodge page: private bedroom, 'AC/heat, bath, and covered porch' on a 'raised deck'. Tiny house page: 399 sq ft main floor, full kitchen, 'sizeable shower'. Hipcamp: loft 'accessible by wide angled ladder' (fine for kids, grandma sleeps on the main floor). Spot2Nite: 'Each site is allowed one vehicle', and the policy page says park in designated areas only and never on the grass. That suggests parking at your own site but doesn't confirm the distance. Personal golf carts are banned but rentals are available. No review found that mentions steps or elderly guests.
places.flood_note: Near the Guadalupe below Canyon Lake Dam (about 2 miles from the dam). I found no report of 2025 flood damage or closure. The July 2025 disaster crest was upstream in Kerr County. Ask which units sit highest.
places.review_signal: Tripadvisor 4.7/5 (search snippet), Expedia 9.4/10, Hipcamp 96% (13 reviews). One Tripadvisor tiny-house review says it 'comfortably fit all of us'.
highlights: Cheapest private-bath option here: lodges from $121.50 weeknights
Full bath, AC and kitchenette in every lodge and tiny house
Pool and hot tub on site, near Gruene, Canyon Lake and Whitewater Amphitheater
Several tiny houses open on fall weekends
places.red_flags: Raised decks mean steps (count unknown). Scenery is campground grounds, not a vista. Lodges sleep only 2. Tipis and safari tents have no in-unit bath, so skip them. 1 vehicle per site. Renters must be 21+. Loft by ladder only.

places.name: The Yurtopian (Wimberley and Dripping Springs sites)
places.town: Wimberley (135 Winn Ranch Rd) / Dripping Springs (7000 McGregor Ln)
places.price_note: The official site doesn't publish rates (it books through its own engine and is running a 10% off fall weekdays promo). The VRBO listings for the 'Lizzie' and 'Dottie' yurts (Dripping Springs) show 'Starting from $319/night' as of 9/24/26, and VRBO says 'Our prices include all fees'. So $319 is an all-in floor, not a base rate. Weekend and high rates weren't confirmed. Single nights are allowed Sun-Thu except holidays. Cancel 30+ days out for a full refund, otherwise everything is forfeited. The lodge can be reserved exclusively ($400 for Yurtopian guests, $800 with up to 25 outside guests, per their shop listings). You can't book the whole property online.
places.group_note: Wimberley (6 yurts) is ADULTS ONLY. Dripping Springs (10 yurts) has only 3 family yurts (Annie, Amie, Dottie Ger), each for 4 people max (king + 2 cots), and children must be 5 or older. Yurts are spread 150-300+ ft apart through the woods, so a family ends up split across separate yurts, not side by side. Drive times shown are for the Dripping Springs family site (approximate). The Wimberley site is about 80 min from SA and 60 min from Austin.
places.scenery_what: A private deck in the trees, with woods on all sides and no neighbors in sight. The big Hill Country view ('miles and miles of Texas skies') is from the rooftop deck, reached by a stair, not from the door. Dark skies for stargazing.
places.steps_to_enter: Each yurt 'sits on a private deck', step count not stated. The rooftop viewing deck is up a stair.
places.access_detail: Wimberley page: 'Outside each yurt, you'll find a large deck with a hot tub/plunge pool... and a private bathroom with a walk-in limestone shower', so the bathroom is on the deck outside the yurt. That's a problem for grandma at night. The VRBO Dottie listing shows 'Toilet · Outdoor shower' and only 'Onsite parking available', with no path or step details. The FAQ says there's a minisplit AC/heater. No review evidence on walking distance from car to yurt.
places.flood_note: Yurts are on a wooded hillside (Wimberley) and on 46 acres with a creek trail (Dripping Springs). I found no 2025 flood impact or closure. Units don't appear to be riverfront.
places.review_signal: The site claims '600+ five-star stays'. Tripadvisor (Wimberley) shows 35 reviews, ranked #3 of 20 specialty lodgings (search snippet). VRBO Lizzie is 10/10 on 2 reviews. A directory review mentions noise from neighboring yurts.
highlights: Most secluded, 'no neighbors in sight' feel of the six
Private hot tub, fire pit, grill and rooftop stargazing deck at every yurt
Minisplit AC/heat and a king bed
places.red_flags: Weak fit for this group: Wimberley bans kids, and Dripping Springs allows only 3 family yurts (kids 5+, max 4 each) spread through the woods. Bathroom sits outside the yurt on the deck. Step and parking distances are unknown. Mostly couples-sized. Strict 30-day cancellation.

places.name: Camp Fimfo Texas Hill Country - Hilltop Coyote / Coyote cabins
places.price_note: Live quotes from Camp Fimfo's booking engine (Campspot park 55) on 9/24/26, average per night before taxes (unclear whether resort fees are included). Hilltop Coyote and Coyote cabins (sleep 12): $261.38 weeknight (Oct 20-22), $416.15 weekend (Nov 6-8), $516.60 weekend (Oct 16-18). Preferred Coyote: $292-$576. Hilltop Coyote Bubbly (private hot tub), Coyote Suite and Coyote Clubhouse: $312.62 weeknight to $616.02 weekend. Bluebonnet/Cypress (sleep 8): about $181-$358. Golf cart rental is extra, with a 2-night minimum and driver 21+. Pets $50/$75. No buyout offered.
places.group_note: Coyote and Hilltop Coyote cabins have 3 bedrooms (1 queen room, the rest bunks/trundle) plus a sofa bed, sleep 12, and share ONE bathroom. The Coyote Suite (sleeps 4: king + queen rooms, private hot tub) is best for grandma. For Oct 16-18 the engine showed 10 Hilltop Coyote, 12 Coyote and 9 Preferred Coyote open, so booking several cabins together is easy. Ask the park (830-743-9803) to place them side by side.
places.scenery_what: Hilltop cabins 'perched atop our very own Texas Hill Country bluff, offering awesome views' from a front porch. Around you is a busy resort: RV sites, pools, swim-up bar, alpine coaster and zipline. The Guadalupe River is down the hill.
places.steps_to_enter: Front porch on every cabin, step count not published.
places.access_detail: The booking engine flags EVERY cabin type isAccessible=false. FAQ: 'Personal golf carts are only allowed if needed for ADA purposes, in which case the proper tags are required'. Rental golf and limo carts are available (a 'Deluxe' cart has cushioned seats with armrests). Cars drive in at 5 mph, and 'If your site is occupied, we are simply unable to accommodate overflow parking', which implies you park at your site, but at-cabin parking isn't stated. Cars can't drive to the river except for Riverview cabins. Treetop and Riverview cabins use a shared bathhouse, so avoid them.
places.flood_note: The resort sits on the Guadalupe below Canyon Lake. Riverview cabins are at river level, while Hilltop and Coyote cabins are well above it on the bluff. I found no 2025 flood closure or damage report.
places.review_signal: USA TODAY 10Best Readers' Choice: #1 Best RV Campground (per resort). The Dyrt has 1 review ('Great campground with resort amenities'). Tripadvisor and Google reviews couldn't be retrieved.
highlights: Big-group math works: 3BR cabins sleep 12 from about $261 weeknights
Many identical cabins, so the whole family can cluster
Hilltop bluff views, pools, river access, mini golf for the kids
ADA-tagged personal golf cart allowed; rentals available
places.red_flags: Nothing flagged accessible. One bathroom per 12-person Coyote cabin. Bunk-heavy beds. Family-resort noise and crowds. Active construction (a unit description gives 'Construction hours are 8am-9pm'). Porch steps unknown.

places.name: Dream Gruene - 6BR riverfront, no stairs (Airbnb)
places.price_note: Whole 6BR property (2 condos). Airbnb totals include cleaning and service fees, before taxes (searched 9/24/26, 10 adults): Oct 20-21 $610 for 1 night. Oct 20-22 $1,058 for 2 nights (about $529/night). Nov 10-12 $1,467 for 2. Nov 20-22 weekend $1,395 for 2 (about $698/night). Dec 4-6 $1,467 for 2 (about $733/night). Finder's 5-night search was $2,097 (about $420/night), so longer stays spread the cleaning fee. Plus $5.40/night damage protection. Oct 16-18, Oct 23-25 and Nov 6-8/13-15 weekends were NOT available. Must be 25+ to book. No pets or parties.
places.group_note: Two side-by-side ground-floor condos (Units 101 and 102) rented together: 6 bedrooms, 12 beds, 4 baths, 2 kitchens, 2 living rooms, 2 washer/dryers. Sleeps 16-18 (Airbnb caps booking at 16). Each unit gets 2 parking spaces (4 total plus a couple of guest spaces), so carpool.
places.scenery_what: 2.5 acres of mature trees, lawn and riverbank at Gruene Rapids. Back patios and balconies look toward the river through trees, and deer wander by. It's in town, 9 minutes' walk from Gruene Hall, so it's pretty but not remote vistas.
places.steps_to_enter: 0. Airbnb's step-free feature says there are no steps, stairs, or curbs from arrival to the entrance.
places.access_detail: Host: 'first-floor riverfront condos... ideal for groups wanting space, privacy, no stairs', 'gated parking yards from door'. Photo captions: 'Front Entrance, just feet away from your parking spot', 'Accessibility Parking 3 Spots from Entrance'. Airbnb accessibility features list step-free access, a disabled parking spot, a lit path and no steep hills. Both master suites have king beds and an 'En Suite Walk in Shower with Rain Shower Head'. Central AC. A rentable 4-seat golf cart can 'scoot from river and back' (the river is 'a couple hundred yards, 2 min walk'). The back balconies have a staircase down toward the river, but it isn't needed for entry.
places.flood_note: Riverfront complex at Gruene Rapids on the Guadalupe below Canyon Dam, so it's in a river floodplain area. Water level depends on dam releases. I found no 2025 flood damage report (the July 2025 disaster crest was upstream). Check the FEMA zone and the host's flood policy before booking.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 5.0 (26 reviews), Superhost Mark (12 yrs hosting). Review themes: hospitality, location, walkability, cleanliness, river.
highlights: Best grandma access of the six: zero-step entry, parking feet from the door, walk-in showers
Whole family under two connected roofs, 6BR/4BA, two kitchens
Walk or golf-cart to Gruene Hall, the Gristmill and the river
Free SUPs, fire pit, grills and a smoker on site
places.red_flags: Scenery is an in-town river setting, not Hill Country panoramas. Only 4 parking spaces. Many fall weekends already booked. Must be 25+. Floodplain location, so check the forecast.

skeptic.name: Dream Gruene - 6BR riverfront, no stairs (Airbnb)
skeptic.evidence: The access claims hold. The listing text says 'Excellent access! Can park car right up to the front door. No stairs, no gates no elevator.' Airbnb's Step-free access, Disabled parking spot and Lit path features are all present. Photos show units 101/102 on the ground floor of a covered breezeway, next to a paved lot with marked accessible spaces. An Oct 2025 review says 'Condos were both downstairs... Good location for loading in and out.' Both master baths have a glass walk-in shower, but it has a low curb, so it is not roll-in. The guest baths are tub/shower combos. Central AC is listed. Scenery is overstated, so I lowered it to 5. This is a 3-story condo building: the front door opens onto a breezeway and parking lot. The back patios are raised decks with stairs down to the lawn. Host captions say the river is a 'Couple hundred yards. 2 min Walk', and a June 2025 review says the river 'entrance is rocky'. Two reviews note the walk into Gruene is uphill. The price was understated. Airbnb's all-fees-included quotes (before taxes, 6 guests) were $683.80/night Nov 9-11, $697 Nov 20-22, $526 Dec 6-8, $748 Dec 11-13, $517 for Jan 11-14 (3 nights), $808 Jan 15-17, $939 Mar 5-7, and $948 Apr 16-18 after a discount. The calendar is open through May 2027 (Nov 13-15 is booked), with a 1-3 night minimum. Reviews from July, Sept, Oct and Dec 2025 and 2026 show no disruption from the July 2025 floods. It is two separate condos side by side, not connected (Feb 2025 review). They sleep 16-18.
sources: Airbnb StaysPdpBookItQuery and PdpAvailabilityCalendar API responses for listing 563210251410431554 (queried 2026-09-24)
Airbnb StaysPdpReviewsQuery for listing 563210251410431554 (26 reviews, Jul 2023-Sep 2026)

places.name: Lake Views, Game Room, Movie Room, Elevator, Lux (Airbnb)
places.price_note: Whole house. Airbnb totals include cleaning and service fees, before taxes (searched 9/24/26, 10 adults): Oct 20-22 $1,549 for 2 nights (about $775/night, 'originally $2,473'). Nov 10-12 $2,011 for 2. Nov 20-22 weekend $2,242 for 2 (about $1,121/night, 'originally $3,859'). Finder's 5-night search was $2,458 (about $492/night), and longer stays drop the per-night cost a lot. Big strikethrough discounts suggest a new-listing promo that may end. Oct 16-18, Nov 6-8 and Dec 4-6 weekends were not available. No pets. Smoking fine is $1,000.
places.group_note: One 5,000 sq ft house on 3 levels: 4 king suites each with a private bath (master plus 2 more on the middle floor, 1 on the lower level), a bunk room (4 bunks), 4.5 baths. The listing says sleeps 18 (Airbnb booking cap shows 16). The driveway 'holds however many vehicles show up'.
places.scenery_what: High on a hillside above Canyon Lake: floor-to-ceiling windows, and a top-floor deck with Adirondack chairs 'pointed straight at Canyon Lake and the sunset'. The master and bedroom 3 have private balconies with hill views. It's a residential neighborhood, so other houses are around.
places.steps_to_enter: Host (accessibility section): 'There are steps to enter the home, and this home is 3 stories with steps to all levels. We do have an elevator.' The front door enters on the middle level. Step count not stated.
places.access_detail: 'A private elevator reaches all three floors', and a photo caption says 'The elevator is the reason grandparents can come. Three floors, no stairs'. Interior stairs are 'wide... with real railings'. Grandma can have a king suite with an en-suite bath (the master has a tub plus a walk-in-size shower). Driveway parking on the premises. Central AC. Unconfirmed: how many exterior steps there are, and whether you can enter at the elevator's bottom (former garage/game-room) level to skip them. Ask the host.
places.flood_note: Hillside home well above Canyon Lake, so no flood exposure. I found no 2025 impact.
places.review_signal: New listing: 2 reviews (5.0). Host Scott is a Superhost with 889 reviews and a 4.87 average. One guest praised 'the views from the patio'.
highlights: Best view of the six that still has good grandma access: lake and sunset from the deck and bedrooms
Private elevator to all 3 floors plus 4 king en-suites
Game room, arcade, movie room and bunk room keep the kids busy
Big driveway for multiple cars
places.red_flags: Unknown number of steps to reach the front door. Only 2 reviews. Pricey on short weekend stays. The promo 'originally' prices may return. Neighborhood roads are narrow and curvy. No pets.

places.name: Sage Hill Inn & Spa (Ranch House + ground-floor cottages/casitas)
places.town: Kyle (4444 RM 150, between Kyle and Wimberley, on Onion Creek)
places.price_note: Live ThinkReservations quotes pulled 9/24/26, per night before tax, for 2 adults. Weeknight (Oct 20-22): Pecan Cottage $349, Martin King $399, Hartson/Porter/Wallace King $419, Juniper and Live Oak Cottages $449, Verbena Casita $509, Ranch House $1,399. Weekend (Nov 20-22): Red Oak $399, Kyle King (ADA) and other kings $479, cottages $549, Lavender Casita $599. Ranch House for Oct 17-19 was $1,699 Sat and $1,399 Sun. Every stay includes continental breakfast plus a $75/day restaurant credit per room. $50/night per extra guest over 2 (not charged in the Ranch House). 2-night minimum on Fri-Sat. Site promo: 15% off midweek. One night's deposit. Cancel 14+ days out for a refund minus $25, 8-14 days for a gift certificate, 7 or fewer days means no refund. Whole-inn buyout is possible for a family reunion (price not listed).
places.group_note: Ranch House: 3BR (2 kings + queen, twin daybed on request), 2.5 baths, sleeps 7, full kitchen, private hot tub and fire pit. Add ground-floor cottages (Live Oak sleeps 4, Juniper 3) and casitas (2 each) to fit more family. Big catch: 'We welcome children 16 and older', and younger kids are allowed only if you reserve the ENTIRE Inn for a wedding or family reunion.
places.scenery_what: 88 acres of oak ranch land inside 2,500 protected acres along Onion Creek, with trails, gardens and a pool. The Kyle King Room has a private deck with 'stunning views to the north'. It's quiet ranch scenery with sunsets and stars, not a lake or canyon panorama.
places.steps_to_enter: The Kyle King Room is 'ground floor barrier-free'. The Ranch House is ground floor with its own driveway and covered parking (entry steps not stated). Some rooms need steps and there are no elevators. The spa has 2 steps.
places.access_detail: Accessibility statement: the Kyle King Room ADA bath has 'a tub for two, separate roll-in shower equipped with grab bars, roll-under vanity and wider doorways'. 'Elevated access to some rooms and suites requires the navigation of steps. There are no elevators.' Other ground-floor rooms have walk-in showers or step-in tubs. Dining and common areas are step-free with double doors. The Ranch House is 'a short walk from the main Inn, with its own driveway and covered parking area'. AC isn't stated anywhere on the site, so confirm it.
places.flood_note: The property runs along Onion Creek, which is flood-prone downstream. I found no 2025 flood impact or closure. Ask which units sit above the creek.
places.review_signal: Tripadvisor and Expedia blocked the lookup, so no third-party review score was confirmed here.
highlights: Only true ADA roll-in-shower room of the six (Kyle King Room)
Ranch House: private driveway, hot tub, full kitchen, sleeps 7
Breakfast plus $75/day dining credit per room, spa and pool on site
Closest to Austin (about 35 min)
places.red_flags: NO KIDS UNDER 16 unless you buy out the whole inn. Priciest option (Ranch House $1,399-$1,699/night). $50/night per extra adult in rooms. AC not stated on the site. Strict cancellation.

places.name: Gruene Mansion Inn
places.price_note: Official room pages: Gast Haus (river view, ground level) from $215; Das Fluss Haus #11 and River Lookout $270-375; River Hideout $260-345; Grand River Lodge (river view, sleeps 6) from $305; Bluebonnet Lodge $315-425; Sunday Haus courtyard rooms $250-335; Texas Suite $345-475. Rates cover 2 people (4 in the 6-sleeper lodges), then +$25 per extra person per night. 13% tax. 2-night minimum on weekends, 3 nights on most holidays. Cancel by 3pm 7 days out for a refund minus a $75 fee. Parking is free. No whole-inn buyout price is posted.
places.group_note: 33 rooms, each with its own entrance, bath and porch. Rooms sleep 2, 4 or 6. Kids are allowed ONLY in the courtyard rooms, Bluebonnet Lodge and Grand River Lodge. All other River View and Mansion rooms are adults only. Family plan: grandma in Grand River Lodge (ground floor, river porch, sleeps 6), adults in ground-level river rooms (Gast Haus, Das Fluss Haus, River Hideout), and kids in Bluebonnet (upstairs) or the courtyard Sunday Haus rooms. Book by phone to get rooms next to each other.
places.scenery_what: The River View rooms have front porches with rocking chairs looking out over the Guadalupe River through big trees. You're inside a historic inn complex next to Gruene Hall and the shops, so other buildings and people are around. The courtyard rooms look onto the inn's courtyard, not the river.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The Grand River Lodge page says it is ground floor with 'two separate bathrooms each with a shower,' and 'Both bathrooms are located downstairs.' Only the loft is up a spiral staircase. Gast Haus, Das Fluss Haus #11 and River Hideout are listed as ground level. Bluebonnet Lodge, Texas Suite and the Country Penthaus rooms are upstairs. Sunday Haus rooms have a spiral staircase to the bedroom. The site gives no porch step counts.
places.access_detail: Grandma's best room is Grand River Lodge: ground floor, a queen bed, and two downstairs bathrooms with walk-in-type showers. Nearly every other room, including all the ground-level river rooms, has an 'antique clawfoot tub with shower,' and stepping over a clawfoot tub wall is hard for an elderly person. There's 'Onsite Complimentary Parking' with a dashboard pass, but no page says how far it is from each room. The policies page mentions ADA only for service animals, and no room is listed as ADA. Every room has 'A/C & Heating.' I couldn't open any review site (Yelp and Tripadvisor returned 403), so there's no reviewer evidence about stairs, hills or walking. Call (830) 629-2641 and ask how far Grand River Lodge is from parking and how many porch steps it has.
places.flood_note: The inn sits on the Guadalupe in Gruene, downstream of Canyon Dam. I found nothing about 2025 flood damage here, but I couldn't run news searches, so treat that as unverified. The site shows it is open daily 8am-7pm with a live ResNexus booking link.
places.review_signal: No review data retrieved (Yelp and Tripadvisor blocked, Booking.com returned empty). Evidence is official pages only.
highlights: Rocking-chair porches over the Guadalupe River
Grand River Lodge: ground floor, sleeps 6, two downstairs showers, kids allowed
Walk to Gruene Hall and the historic district
33 rooms, so a whole family can book a cluster
places.red_flags: River View rooms (except Bluebonnet and Grand River Lodge) are adults only. Clawfoot tubs in most rooms. Grandma-to-parking distance is not published. Weekend 2-night and holiday 3-night minimums. $75 cancellation fee, no refund inside 7 days.

places.name: Bastrop State Park Cabins #12 "Lost Pines Lodge" + #14 (the two ADA cabins)
places.price_note: Official TPWD rates: Cabin #12 is $200/night and Cabin #14 is $130/night, plus a $5/adult/day park entrance fee (kids 12 and under free). A Texas State Parks Pass waives entry. Fri or Sat stays need a 2-night minimum, and holiday weekends must include the holiday. Linens are provided but not pillows. The other historic cabins cost $110-150 but only have a unit AC in the main room and aren't accessible.
places.group_note: #12 sleeps 8: L-shaped, 4 bedrooms, 2 baths, full kitchen, fireplace, big screened back porch. #14 sleeps 4: 2 bedrooms, 1 bath with a bathtub/shower, central AC. Book both for 12 people. Up to 11 more historic CCC cabins (#1-#11) sleep 2-6 each for extra family, but they have window-style AC and aren't accessible. They're separate cabins in the park, so check with the park how close #12 and #14 are to each other.
places.scenery_what: Loblolly pine forest (the Lost Pines), still growing back after the 2011 fire. It's quiet woods and the cabin's big screened porch. There's no lake or hill-country view from the door.
places.steps_to_enter: TPWD doesn't give a step count. Photo captions say 'The parking area of Cabin 12 is wheelchair friendly', and the cabin is labeled 'Accessible'. Cabin #14 is also labeled accessible, but its entry isn't described.
places.access_detail: TPWD Cabin 12 page captions: 'The parking area of Cabin 12 is wheelchair friendly,' 'The bathroom in Cabin 12 is wheelchair friendly,' 'The accessible shower in Cabin 12.' Central A/C and heat. Cabin #14 is labeled accessible with central A/C, but its bathroom is a 'Bathtub with shower' (not roll-in). The cabin list shows only #12 and #14 as accessible. I found no reviews that talk about access. Parking at the door is based on TPWD's photo of a dedicated wheelchair-friendly parking area for the cabin, so it isn't measured.
places.flood_note: The cabins sit in upland pine forest, not a river floodplain. TPWD mentions past floods and fires in the park, but I found no July 2025 flood impact. The park is open. Active alerts include a screwworm advisory plus a second alert whose details weren't visible.
places.review_signal: No third-party reviews retrieved. The evidence is TPWD's official cabin pages and photo captions.
highlights: Wheelchair-friendly parking and an accessible shower at Cabin #12 (official)
Central AC, full kitchen, fireplace, big screened porch
Cheapest private-bath option: $330/night total for 12 people across both cabins
Historic CCC park with a golf course and Lake Mina nearby
places.red_flags: No big views, just woods. $5/adult/day entry fee. Weekend 2-night minimum. No pillows provided. Active park alerts (screwworm, plus one unspecified). Bastrop County burn ban noted on the LCRA pages, so campfires may be banned.

places.name: The Island on Lake Travis (condo resort; ground-floor Villa 1104 plus other owner units)
places.price_note: VRBO 1BR units checked 9/24/2026: 'from $155' (for dates around Nov 23, 2026) and 'Starting at $158/night,' both advertised as including all fees. Villa 1104 doesn't show a nightly rate on the manager's site. Its terms are 50% due at booking if you book 30+ days out and the rest within 30 days of check-in, with no minimum stay stated. I found no weekend or holiday top-end rate, so price_high is unknown. There's no whole-property buyout; units are individually owned.
places.group_note: A gated condo complex on a 14-acre island. Units are individually owned and mostly 1BR, sleeping 2-4. Villa 1104 sleeps 4. North Shore Vacation Rentals manages 30+ properties, and more units are on VRBO, so a family would book several condos in the same complex. They won't necessarily be next door to each other.
places.scenery_what: A private balcony or patio looking straight out over Lake Travis and the hills, with sunsets. Villa 1104's listing calls it 'one of the best views from the Island.' Other condo buildings are part of the view. The lake was 90.3% full (675.2 ft) on 9/24/2026, about 6 ft below full pool. It is not completely 'full.'
places.private_bath: In unit (1 bedroom, 1 bath), but a guest review says 'The bathtub jets did not work but we still enjoyed a good soak'. The bathroom is a jetted step-in tub, not a walk-in shower.
places.steps_to_enter: Villa 1104 is on the ground floor, and the listing mentions no stairs. The other units rely on elevators (5 on the property).
places.access_detail: The Villa 1104 listing says it's a ground floor unit and 'Covered Parking is on ground level with reserved parking,' with an electronic door lock, but it gives no walking distance from the car. A VRBO review of another unit said: 'The property was represented as wheelchair accessible, but the elevators were not working during our stay.' A third-floor unit's reviewer liked the 'Parking spot close to elevator which was close to condo.' Some reviews mention broken AC units and hot tubs. Bathroom shower type is unknown. Book ground-floor units only, or confirm the elevators work before arrival.
places.flood_note: This is a lake reservoir, not a river floodplain. The condos sit above the water. Lake Travis rose sharply in the July 2025 Hill Country floods, but I found no report of damage to The Island (unverified). The indoor pool is 'closed until long-term maintenance is complete.'
places.review_signal: VRBO unit 211208ha: 8.6/10 across 214 reviews, location rated 9.6. Guests praise the views, and complaints are about elevators, AC and hot tubs.
highlights: Balconies right over Lake Travis with sunset views
Ground-floor Villa 1104 with covered reserved parking
About $155-158/night all-in per 1BR condo
Gated island with pools, marina, restaurant/bar, and a shuttle
places.red_flags: Elevators reported out of service during some stays. Indoor pool closed. Reviews mention broken AC and hot tubs. It's about 2 hours from San Antonio, near the edge of the range. Quality varies by owner. Villa 1104's rate isn't posted.

skeptic.name: The Island on Lake Travis (condo resort; ground-floor Villa 1104 plus other owner units)
skeptic.corrected_private_bath: In unit (1 bedroom, 1 bath), but a guest review says 'The bathtub jets did not work but we still enjoyed a good soak'. The bathroom is a jetted step-in tub, not a walk-in shower.
skeptic.evidence: The Villa 1104 listing confirms: 'One bedroom one bath villa overlooks beautiful Lake Travis', up to 4 guests, 'Covered Parking is on ground level with reserved parking... There are 5 elevators on property', a coded door lock, AC and central heating, and amenity tags 'Home Step Free Access' and 'Single Level Home'. A reviewer says 'The room is on the first floor so access to the gym, hot tubs and pools.' Lake level is verified: 675.19 ft, 90.3% full on 2026-09-24 (TWDB). REFUTING / CAVEATS: (1) The jetted bathtub is a step-over tub, a real hazard for a grandma who can't walk far. (2) It sleeps only 4, so a family needs several separately owned units. Those units vary in floor, elevator dependence and bath type; the manager's site says only 'Reserved covered parking garage with elevator access'. (3) The walking distance from the reserved garage spot to 1104 is not stated. (4) Nightly rates appear only in the booking widget, so the $155 low is unverified. The listing is live with booking terms (50% at booking if 30+ days out), so it appears bookable. Specific fall 2026 or spring 2027 dates are unverified. No flood closure found.

places.name: Lake Bastrop South Shore Park: LCRA cabins + ÖÖD mirror glamping houses
places.price_note: LCRA: standard cabins from $75 (sleep 4), deluxe cabins from $129 (sleep 3), ÖÖD houses 'Starting at $350.' The ÖÖD houses are booked through Cameron Ranch Glamping, whose listings say 'Dynamic pricing starts at $299+ per night.' That route has a 2-night weekend minimum, a 50% non-refundable deposit with the rest due 14 days out, and a $49 per-pet fee on The Bloom. There's no buyout.
places.group_note: 12 standard cabins (sleep 4) and 6 deluxe cabins (sleep 3) are booked through LCRA. The 2 ÖÖD mirror houses (The Bloom, site #25, and The Hideaway, site #22) sleep 2 each through Cameron Ranch Glamping. Plan: grandma plus one person in an ÖÖD house, the family in nearby cabins. They're all in the same campground, but it isn't confirmed they're next to each other.
places.scenery_what: Pine and oak woods inside a public campground. The Hideaway listing says the mirror house 'sits inside the campground,' with 'other park guests' around, and about a '3 minute walk away from the lake.' There's no lake view from the ÖÖD houses. The finder's 'on the water' note is not supported. You don't get a lake view until you walk to the shore.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown for both the ÖÖD houses and the cabins. No listing mentions steps or ramps.
places.access_detail: The ÖÖD houses have 'HVAC,' a 'Private restroom with shower' (The Hideaway lists a 'walk-in shower'), and 'Parking available on-site,' but no distance is given. The LCRA standard and deluxe cabins are 'Climate controlled' with no bathroom listed, so people there use the park's flush restrooms and showers. LCRA notes 'Some restrooms ... will be under construction beginning April 27.' No ADA units are listed anywhere. Only an ÖÖD house works for grandma's bathroom needs.
places.flood_note: Lake Bastrop is a reservoir, not a river, and none of the 2025 flood rivers run here. I found no 2025 flood impact. The park is open sunrise to sunset. A Bastrop County burn ban is in effect, so no campfires.
places.review_signal: No reviews retrieved (Yelp blocked). The evidence is the LCRA and Cameron Ranch Glamping listings.
highlights: Cheapest cabins in the set (from $75)
ÖÖD mirror houses with a walk-in shower, AC and a kitchen for grandma
Lake 3 minutes on foot, with kayaking nearby
places.red_flags: No lake view from the units. Standard and deluxe cabins have no bathroom. Some park restrooms are under construction. Burn ban. ÖÖD houses sleep only 2 and need a 50% non-refundable deposit. It's a public campground with neighbors around.

places.name: Lake Bastrop North Shore Park: LCRA Airstream campers
places.price_note: LCRA says Airstreams are 'Starting at $199.' A Do512 Family article from about 2019 said $225/night with a 2-night minimum, so that figure is old. I couldn't see the top weekend rate. The same park also has glamping tents from $150 (sleep 2-4) and cabins from $350 (sleep 6). The Magnolia premium lakefront cabin, booked via Cameron Ranch Glamping, is about $299+ weekdays and $349+ weekends, with a 2-night weekend minimum.
places.group_note: 5 Airstreams sleep 4 each (one queen and two twins). The park also has glamping tents and lakefront cabins that sleep 6. A family could take several Airstreams together, with grandma in The Magnolia lakefront cabin.
places.scenery_what: A lakeside park on Lake Bastrop with pines and trails. Do512 says the Airstreams are 'in such close proximity to the water,' but no source confirms a lake view from the trailers. The Magnolia cabin's listing does confirm 'Lake views from the granite patio.'
places.steps_to_enter: Airstreams have a step-up entry into a narrow door, which is normal for the trailer type, but LCRA doesn't give a step count. The Magnolia cabin's entry steps are also unknown.
places.access_detail: LCRA lists each Airstream as 'Climate controlled' with a 'Private restroom with shower' and a patio with gas grill and fire pit. Do512 says 'dual AC units.' A 25-ft trailer bathroom is very small and the entry is a step up, so it's poor for a mobility-limited grandma. Parking at the trailer isn't stated. A better grandma unit here is The Magnolia premium lakefront cabin: 'One private spot adjacent to the cabin,' 'Mini-split HVAC (A/C + heat),' a bathroom with shower, and sleeps 6. Its step count isn't listed.
places.flood_note: Lake Bastrop is a reservoir, not on any of the 2025 flood rivers. I found no 2025 flood impact. The park is open sunrise to sunset. A Bastrop County burn ban is in effect, so the fire pits can't be used.
places.review_signal: No reviews retrieved (Yelp blocked). The evidence is the LCRA page, a roughly 2019 Do512 Family article, and the Cameron Ranch listing for The Magnolia.
highlights: Real glamping feel: Airstreams with private bath, kitchen, grill and patio
Lakefront Magnolia cabin with parking next to the door and lake views from the patio
Kayak and paddleboard rentals, about 10 miles of trails
places.red_flags: Airstream step-up and tiny bathroom are bad for grandma. Lake view from the Airstreams isn't confirmed. Burn ban. The $225 price and 2-night minimum come from an old article. No ADA info.

places.name: Lakeway Resort & Spa (ADA lake-view rooms)
places.price_note: Kayak: deals from $196, average weeknight $299, average weekend $321 (the full range runs to $593, including suites). Momondo shows $196-308. Add the official $50/night resort fee plus tax and $10/night self-parking. Pets are $150 per stay. No buyout.
places.group_note: A full hotel, so the family can take many rooms on the same floors. Double Queen Lake View rooms sleep 4. Lakeview Junior Suites have 'adjoining room options,' the LBJ Suite (968 sq ft) can connect to a King room, and the Mansfield Suite (1,144 sq ft) has a sleeper sofa and an extra bathroom.
places.scenery_what: Lake-view rooms have private balconies over what the resort calls 'Lake Travis' deepest waters,' with hills on the far shore. Kayak reviewers: 'The views from the lake side balconies are expansive.' It's a view from a hotel balcony, not a step-out-into-nature setting.
places.steps_to_enter: Zero steps. The official accessibility page lists 'an accessible entrance without stairs' and says an accessible elevator serves all levels.
places.access_detail: Official accessibility page: 'There are 9 accessible parking spots,' 'All accessible parking spaces are closest to the hotel entrance,' a covered accessible pickup/drop-off area, 'an accessible entrance without stairs,' and an elevator to all levels. The parking garage has elevator access. There are 9 accessible rooms with 'roll-in shower' options and grab bars, including 'Double Queen Lake View with Roll-In Shower & Balcony' and 'King Lake View with Roll-In Shower & Balcony.' Grandma can be dropped at the door. The 100-300 ft figure is my estimate of the hallway walk from the entrance to her room, which the resort doesn't publish. Ask for an ADA lake-view room near the elevator.
places.flood_note: The resort sits above Lake Travis, a reservoir. The lake was 90.3% full on 9/24/2026. I found no 2025 flood impact on the hotel (unverified).
places.review_signal: Kayak and Momondo: 7.9/10 from 665 reviews. Guests praise the lake views and swim-up bar, and complain about 'outdated furniture,' springy beds and uneven service.
highlights: ADA lake-view rooms with roll-in showers and balconies
Stair-free entrance, covered drop-off, elevators, accessible parking closest to the door
Adjoining rooms and suites for the family
Pool, spa and restaurants on site, so nobody has to drive around
places.red_flags: $50/night resort fee plus $10 parking on top of the rate. Reviews call the rooms dated. It's a hotel, not glamping. About 1h40m from San Antonio.

skeptic.name: Lakeway Resort & Spa (ADA lake-view rooms)
skeptic.evidence: The access claims hold on the official site, but the price could not be verified and extra fees apply. The accessibility page (https://www.lakewayresortandspa.com/accessibility) confirms: 9 accessible self-parking spots, all closest to the hotel entrance; a covered accessible pickup/drop-off area; an accessible path to check-in, to guest rooms and to public spaces; an accessible elevator; and 9 accessible rooms out of 168, all lake view with balcony, with grab bars and 36-inch lever doors. The Stay page lists roll-in showers in both 'Double Queen Lake View with Balcony & Roll-In Shower' and 'King Lake View with Balcony & Roll-In Shower'. The accessibility page names the roll-in shower only for the Double Queen, so ask which room type is actually roll-in. The page does NOT mention a parking garage, so the claim's 'garage with elevator access' is unconfirmed. The walk from the entrance to the room is not published anywhere, so the 100-300 ft figure is unknown. PRICE: the $196-321 nightly rate could not be checked. The site shows no rates, the booking engine is behind Cloudflare, and a WebSearch budget cap blocked third-party lookups. Whatever the room rate is, the Stay page and FAQ add a $50/night + tax resort fee (it includes a $25 daily food and beverage credit and a golf cart to the marina) and $10/night self-parking. There is no valet. Check-in age is 21+, check-in is 4 PM, and dogs cost a $150 fee. Real cost is at least about $60/night plus tax above the room rate. Scenery is a hotel-balcony lake view, not step-out nature. No closure or flood notice appears on the site. The resort is operating, but availability for specific fall 2026 / spring 2027 dates was not checked; call (512) 261-6600.

places.name: Cameron Ranch Glamping (formerly GLAT Austin): lakefront cabins at Lake Bastrop North Shore
places.price_note: Official Magnolia cabin page: 'Weekday rates typically start around $299+', and 'dynamic pricing starts at $349+ per night and increases on weekends'. The LCRA park page says cabins start at $350. The weekend top rate isn't published (a 2021 article cited $450 on busy summer weekends). Minimum stay is 2 nights on weekends and 1 night on weekdays. Pets cost $49 each per stay (listing page; the home page says $39). Booking takes a 50% non-refundable deposit, and cancelling less than 30 days out gets no refund. Taxes not shown.
places.group_note: Hipcamp lists 4 lakefront cabins side by side in the same cluster: #1 Armadillo (4-6), #2 Magnolia (6, best for 2-4), #3 Firefly (6), #4 Cardinal (2). There are also safari tents #5, #6 and #8 (2-4 each; shared park restrooms). A family could book 2-3 cabins next to each other. Only Magnolia shows on the official site's search; the others are booked through Hipcamp.
places.scenery_what: A granite patio with fire pit, gas grill and seating, right on the Lake Bastrop shoreline in a pine and oak park. An old GLAT review: 'The lake was beautiful, right outside our cabin!' It's inside a public LCRA park, so other glampers and park visitors are nearby.
places.steps_to_enter: unknown (not stated; ask whether the cabin door has steps)
places.access_detail: Official listing: 'One private spot is included beside the cabin; additional parking is available within a short 2–3 minute walk.' The Hipcamp cabin listings say the same. Cabins have a 'Private bathroom with shower' and 'Mini-split HVAC (A/C + heat)'. Access type is drive-in. Warning: the old GLAT tent reviews describe 'About 1/4 mile walk down a gravel trail' and parking about 100 yards away. That applied to the tents and shared bathhouse, so book a cabin only.
places.flood_note: Lake Bastrop is an off-river reservoir, not on any of the rivers that flooded in July 2025. No 2025 flood impact was found. Normal lake-level swings only.
places.review_signal: The new Cameron Ranch Hipcamp listing is 100% from only 2 reviews (one complains about a hornet nest in the bathroom and a noise complaint). The old GLAT Austin Hipcamp listing (now 'Not currently accepting bookings') had 87% recommend from 31 reviews; its access complaints were about the tents.
places.red_flags: The operator changed from GLAT Austin to Cameron Ranch Glamping (family business based in Coldspring, TX), so the recent review history is thin. It's inside a public park. Bastrop County burn bans can shut the fire pits, with no refund. The deposit is strict and non-refundable. Do NOT book the safari tents for grandma (shared park restrooms 'a short walk away').
highlights: Lakefront cabins with 1 parking spot right beside the door
Private bath + mini-split AC/heat in every cabin
Cowboy plunge pool/hot tub, fire pit, gas grill on the granite patio
Several cabins side by side for a family
Budget-to-mid tier: about $299-349+ per night

places.name: Hyatt Regency Lost Pines Resort & Spa (water-view rooms)
places.price_note: Hotwire's lead price was $423 for Mon Oct 5-6, 2026, and that figure INCLUDES taxes and fees, so the base rate is lower (not shown). The resort fee is $56.88 per room per night. Water-view rooms and the Litton House cottage cost more (amount not found). Hyatt.com blocks automated checks, so get exact dates quoted there or on Costco Travel. Parking: Hotwire says self-park is $25/day and valet $45/night. The Costco listing says one car's self-parking is included and extra cars are $25/night.
places.group_note: A big resort, so you can book as many rooms as you need. Water View rooms are about 450 sq ft with 1 king or 2 queens and a balcony or patio. The Litton House cottage (2,600 sq ft, 2 bedrooms, full kitchen, pond and golf-course views) could be a family base. Sleeps 4 per room assumes 2 queens (not confirmed).
places.scenery_what: Water View rooms have 'serene water views from the private balcony or patio' (Costco listing) over a 405-acre resort on the lower Colorado River, with pines, ranch land and a golf course. Pretty, landscaped grounds, but it's a busy resort, not seclusion.
places.steps_to_enter: Zero-step: elevators plus an accessible path (Hotwire). The 2014 special-needs review says 'No stairs or changes in elevation'.
places.access_detail: Special Needs Travel Mom (2014): 'No stairs or changes in elevation, low pile carpeting, lots of wide, flat, paved walkways', and the Hyatt 'is happy to provide a golf cart ride'. It lists 13 ADA rooms with roll-in showers, grab bars and shower chairs on request. Hotwire (2026): wheelchair-accessible parking and path of travel, elevator, accessible rooms with a shower. But 'may have limitations', and the resort has 3 buildings on 4 floors with exterior corridors. Use valet to drop grandma at the door. Whether a water-view room can also be an ADA room is not confirmed; ask when booking.
places.flood_note: The resort sits along the lower Colorado River below the Highland Lakes dams. None of the sources checked reported July 2025 flood damage or closure. Costco says it is fully operating (rooms renovated 2021, lobby 2023).
places.review_signal: Hotwire's review summary says the pool and lazy river were a hit with guests of all ages. The access review is old (2014) but very positive for mobility needs.
places.red_flags: Resort fee ($56.88/night) plus parking fees add up. It's a large, busy family resort, not glamping. The only price confirmed is an all-in single-night quote. Water-view prices were not found.
highlights: Most walker-friendly option: flat paved paths, elevators, roll-in-shower ADA rooms
Golf cart rides around the property (per a 2014 review)
Water-view rooms with a balcony or patio on the Colorado River grounds
Lazy river, pools, spa, restaurants on site: nobody has to cook
About 30 min from Austin, about 1h25 from SA

places.name: Lake Travis Escape (Walker Luxury Vacation Rentals; VRBO "Lakeside Luxury with Infinity Pool")
places.price_note: Walker's own quote tool, checked 9/24/2026, with base rent for the whole house: Oct 13-15 (Tue-Thu) $847 for 2 nights, about $423/night. Nov 3-5 is the same, $846. Weekend Oct 16-18 is $1,102, about $551/night. The F1 weekend (Oct 23-25) is $2,187, about $1,093/night. Per-stay fees: cleaning $425, damage waiver $149, admin fee about 10% of rent, processing about 3.5%, and about 12% tax (Lago Vista + Texas). A 2-night weekday total came to $1,637 all-in. VRBO shows 'from $863/night, all fees included' for Jan 4-6, 2027, so booking direct with Walker is cheaper. Nov 6-8, Nov 13-15, Thanksgiving, Dec 4-6 and Oct 6-11 were already unavailable, and 1-night stays were rejected. The renter must be 25+.
places.group_note: One house for the whole family: 4 bedrooms (2 kings, 1 queen, and a bunk room with 2 queen-over-queen bunks plus twin trundles) and 4.5 baths. The driveway fits 6 cars.
places.scenery_what: Lakefront on Lake Travis with 'breathtaking lake vistas'. The infinity pool, screened porch, outdoor dining and deck all look out over the lake, and all 4 bedrooms have lake views. It's in a quiet residential neighborhood, so there are neighbors.
places.steps_to_enter: None from the driveway to the main floor. The pool level has steps.
places.access_detail: Listing text on VRBO and Walker: 'This home is partially wheelchair accessible, with no stairs from the driveway to the main floor featuring a bedroom with a walk-in shower, along with the main living areas, kitchen, and deck. However, access to the pool level involves steps.' The driveway holds 6 vehicles. VRBO lists air conditioning. Give grandma the main-floor bedroom.
places.flood_note: On a lake, not a river floodplain. The house sits on the Lake Travis shoreline in Lago Vista. No house-specific 2025 flood impact was found. Lake Travis is a flood-control reservoir, so after heavy rain the water level can rise sharply.
places.review_signal: VRBO 9.4/10 'Exceptional' from 58 reviews; Walker site 5.0 from 8 reviews. Guests praise the views, screened sunroom, outdoor fireplace, pool and cleanliness. One VRBO review mentions minor maintenance issues (warped floors, light bulbs, a broken towel hook).
places.red_flags: Pool level has steps. Strict house rules: no parties or events, outdoor spaces closed after 10 PM, renter 25+, no pets. Prices spike on event weekends (F1). Many fall 2026 weekends are already booked. Book direct with Walker to avoid the VRBO markup.
highlights: Whole group under one roof (sleeps 14, 4.5 baths)
Zero-step entry from the driveway to a main-floor bedroom with a walk-in shower
Infinity pool + hot tub + screened porch overlooking Lake Travis
About $423/night weekdays for the whole house (split across the family)
Walker direct booking is cheaper than VRBO

skeptic.name: Lake Travis Escape (Walker Luxury Vacation Rentals; VRBO "Lakeside Luxury with Infinity Pool")
skeptic.evidence: Access holds, but the price range is wrong. The Walker listing text, taken from the page's embedded data, says verbatim: 'This home is partially wheelchair accessible, with no stairs from the driveway to the main floor featuring a bedroom with a walk-in shower, along with the main living areas, kitchen, and deck. However, access to the pool level involves steps.' Walker also lists air conditioning. Address is 6102 Lakeshore Dr, Lago Vista. It sleeps 14: 4 bedrooms (King, King, Queen, and a bunk room with 2 queen-over-queen bunks and twin trundles), 4 full baths and 1 half bath. Guests cannot use the garage. Outdoor spaces are closed 10 PM to 7 AM, the primary renter must be 25+, and no parties are allowed. All 8 reviews (2023-2025) are 5 stars and none mention stairs, but none independently confirm the step-free route either. A Matterport 3D tour (my.matterport.com/show/?m=APz2iR3HkdD) can confirm the driveway-to-main-floor route before booking. 'All 4 bedrooms have lake views' and '6-car driveway' are NOT stated on the Walker page. PRICE, from Walker's live direct-booking quote endpoint: Oct 16-18 2026 rent $1,102 ($551/nt), total $1,957 with a $425 cleaning fee, $149 damage waiver, $152.60 admin fee, $53.41 processing fee and taxes. Oct 16-19 averages $509/nt, Oct 20-23 $534/nt, Oct 23-26 $945/nt, Mar 5-8 2027 $687/nt and Mar 19-22 2027 $702/nt. The site's own 'from' rate is $527. The claimed $423 low could not be reproduced, and all-in cost for a 2-3 night stay runs about $830-1,380/night. Unavailable dates: Oct 9-12, Nov 6-9, Nov 13-16 2026 and Apr 9-12 2027. Available: Oct 16-23 2026 and March 2027.

places.name: Lake Austin Spa Resort
places.price_note: Official fact sheet: 'Nightly rates start at $595 per person' (all-inclusive: 3 meals a day, activities, spa facilities, gratuities, valet and self-parking). So a cottage for 2 is about $1,190+/night before tax; 1 person is presumably at least $595 (single-occupancy pricing not stated). Booking takes a $1,000 deposit per person, forfeited if you cancel within 21 days. Current offers: $600/night spa and experience credit Sep 1-Dec 31, 2026; a 20%-off fall offer; stay 3 nights and the 4th is free; Sun-Wed 3-for-2.
places.group_note: 40 cottages and bungalows; the resort takes small group bookings and room blocks. Guests must be 16+ (16-18 with an adult), so this only works if the family has no young kids. Per-unit capacity was not stated.
places.scenery_what: Cottages on the Lake Austin shore with hill country views. 'Most rooms offer spectacular views of Lake Austin' and have private porches, some with gardens or hot tubs. BUT from Oct 12 to Nov 30, 2026 the lake will be lowered 'to its river channel level for planned maintenance' (resort offers page), so fall views will be much reduced.
places.steps_to_enter: Varies by cottage. The resort says it has 'stairs, ramps, and low-grade inclines in select areas'.
places.access_detail: Resort FAQ: 'The property is a non-contiguous, multi-level design with stairs, ramps, and low-grade inclines in select areas' and asks guests with mobility needs to contact the resort in advance. The location page says it's 'a short walk up' from check-in to the spa. Accommodations page: 'All cottages and bungalows are located within a short walk of the LakeHouse Spa.' Valet and self-parking are free; how far parking is from the cottages is not stated. Call and ask for a level, close-in cottage. AC is almost certain at this resort but wasn't stated on the pages read.
places.flood_note: Lakefront on Lake Austin, a constant-level reservoir below Mansfield Dam. No 2025 flood closure was found (the site shows 2025-2026 press and awards, and a blog post dated Sep 23, 2026). The planned drawdown on Oct 12-Nov 30, 2026 lowers the lake to its river channel.
places.review_signal: The resort's press page cites Condé Nast Traveler 2025 Readers' Choice: #1 US destination spa. It is an award-winning, long-running resort.
places.red_flags: Guests must be 16+. Pricing is per person (very expensive for a family). $1,000 deposit per person. Multi-level grounds with stairs. The fall 2026 lake drawdown hurts the view. It's a wellness spa, not glamping.
highlights: Splurge tier: all-inclusive meals, spa facilities, lake activities, gratuities
Lakefront cottages with private porches and gardens
Free valet parking
About 30 min from downtown Austin
Avoid Oct 12-Nov 30, 2026 (lake drawdown)

places.name: Living Waters on Lake Travis: the Firefly Room safari tent (only)
places.price_note: Rates are not shown without dates. The Glamping Hub safari-tent listing says 'Prices for upcoming dates start at 115.00 per night', but the sister Red Room listing shows the same figure, so it may be a property-wide minimum. Book on Cloudbeds (hotels.cloudbeds.com/reservation/vItKGd). Cancelling within 48 hours of booking gets a full refund; no refunds within 60 days of arrival. Late checkout costs $25 per half hour. Contact them for full-property rates.
places.group_note: 7 units on the property, and the whole property can be rented. The Firefly sleeps 2 adults (+1 child). Other units: La Casa de Joy straw-bale house (bedroom upstairs, spiral stairs), Blue Loft (bed is up a ladder), Bunkhouse (4 twin bunks, bathroom with standing shower), Cottage Upstairs (upstairs), Romantic Red Room (detached bath casita), Love Shack tent (portable toilet).
places.scenery_what: Official site: an 'Epic lake view scenic deck perched under a huge oak tree, positioned for sunset-watching' over Lake Travis at the mouth of the Pedernales, with hammock chairs, a fire pit and a dock.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown; the tent sits on a deck. Airbnb flags 'Must climb stairs' for the sister Love Shack tent on the same property.
places.access_detail: The finder's note that the Firefly has a private bath is WRONG. The official Firefly page lists 'Outdoor shower and private portable restroom', and Cloudbeds describes 'our mostly-private outdoor shower area behind the tent'. The tent has 'Air-conditioned and heated'. The property slopes down to the water ('floating in the water down the hill'), and Airbnb says the lake is about a 10-minute walk. Parking distance to the Firefly was not stated anywhere I could verify. A night-time portable toilet makes this a poor fit for grandma.
places.flood_note: The property (24315 Pedernales Dr) says it sits 'at the mouth of the Pedernales River' on Lake Travis, and the Pedernales flooded hard in July 2025. Travis County posted a (now expired) order limiting recreational use of the Pedernales River & Lake Travis between mile markers 27-37 after flash flooding; the page cites a July 14, 2026 disaster proclamation. Check dock and water conditions before booking. The tent itself is up the slope from the water.
places.review_signal: Glamping Hub: property 4.9/5 (27 reviews); safari tent listing 8 reviews, e.g. 'Very hot in the tent as expected during the day' and 'It was tough with the heat around 1p to about 6p'. Airbnb (Love Shack tent) 4.77 from 62. Tripadvisor could not be checked (blocked).
places.red_flags: Portable toilet and outdoor shower, no indoor bathroom. Hot during the day. Sleeps 2 only. Flood-prone Pedernales mouth. The official site looks stale ('© 2023'; says the lake is 'currently low'). Not pet friendly.
highlights: Sunset lake-view deck under a big oak
AC + heat in the tent, king bed
Kayaks, paddleboards, dock, yoga pavilion; winery about a 4-min walk
Whole property can be rented for a group
Budget price (maybe from about $115/night)

places.name: Colorado RiverBend Retreat: River Shack cabin + Terry's Riverside Camper (+ tent sites)
places.price_note: The River Shack and Terry's Camper prices are not shown on Hipcamp without dates. Tent sites start at $35/night on Hipcamp. Extra people, cars and pets are paid on site; the River Shack pet fee is $125. Minimum 1 night. Sites are capped at 6 people, with fines if you go over.
places.group_note: The River Shack sleeps 2. Terry's Riverside Camper sleeps 2-4 (one family pitched a tent next to it for '4 adults & 2 littles'). Tent sites 2 (riverside), 3 (private, wooded) and 4/5/6 (primitive) hold up to 6 each and share a community bathhouse. Terry's Camper did NOT appear among the sites currently listed on the Hipcamp page (last review April 2026), so confirm it's still bookable.
places.scenery_what: Wooded riverside campground on the Colorado River east of Smithville, with birds and deer. The River Shack 'Is Situated Above the Colorado RiverBend Retreat, Overlooking The campground' with a porch and a private enclosed spa. That's a view of the woods and campground, not a river panorama. The riverside tent sites face the water.
places.steps_to_enter: unknown
places.access_detail: River Shack: Hipcamp amenity flags include toilet and shower, and it's described as 'a fully furnished BNB'. Access type is drive-in (2WD), but distance from the car, steps and AC are not stated. The finder's claim that Terry's Camper has a private bath is contradicted by reviews: 'Bathroom was clean, well lit and close by' (Dec 2025) and 'the outhouse... 2 showers and toilet and just across from the camper' (Dec 2025). The camper does have an 'ac/heater unit'. Tent sites have gravel parking pads and 'Walking Distance To The BathHouse'.
places.flood_note: Right on the Colorado River floodplain below the Austin dams. Host warning: 'When Travis Co. Opens The Gates On Us Little Guys Down River!... the SandBar Is NonExistant As The Rising waters Cover it.' The host recommends Hipcamp weather insurance. No specific 2025 damage was found; reviews continue through May 2026.
places.review_signal: Hipcamp 99% recommend (293 recommends, 260 bookings). Reviews through May 2026 praise the host Bridget and a very clean hot-water bathhouse.
places.red_flags: Rustic campground: toilet paper and towels no longer provided, hunting gunfire may be audible, check-in must be before 8 PM, strict noise and kid rules. The river rises when dams release. East of Austin, not Hill Country. Terry's Camper has no in-unit bath and may no longer be listed. River Shack price, steps and AC are unconfirmed.
highlights: Cheapest option: tent sites from $35/night for the rest of the family
River Shack private cabin with enclosed spa overlooking the grounds
Riverside sites with kayaking and fishing
Host and bathhouse get consistently strong reviews

places.name: Bastrop State Park - historic CCC Cabins #12 and #14 (wheelchair accessible)
places.price_note: From the official TPWD page: Cabin 12 'Lost Pines Lodge' is $200/night and Cabin 14 is $130/night. The other cabins (1-11) are $110-150. You also pay the daily entrance fee ($5 per adult, kids 12 and under free). Fri/Sat stays need 2 nights, and a holiday-weekend stay must include the holiday. TPWD says 'Information and prices can change.' There is no whole-park buyout, but the park also has group barracks.
places.group_note: Cabin 12 has 4 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and 6 beds, and sleeps 8. It has a full oven. Cabin 14 has 2 bedrooms and 1 bath, and sleeps 4. That makes 12 beds between the two accessible cabins. There are 13 cabins in all (1-12 and 14), and every one has an indoor bathroom. Cabins 1-11 have window AC units in the main room and sleep 2-6. The family can reserve several cabins through Texas State Parks reservations.
places.scenery_what: Tall loblolly pines of the Lost Pines forest around 1930s stone-and-timber CCC cabins. It is forest, with no lake, river or hill-country panorama from the door. There is a scenic overlook with ADA parking on Park Road 1A.
places.steps_to_enter: TPWD calls Cabins 12 and 14 wheelchair accessible. Cabin 12 is L-shaped, with a 'Screened-in porch entry into large living area.' TPWD does not say whether there is a ramp or how many steps there are.
places.access_detail: TPWD accessibility page: 'Cabin 14 and Cabin 12 are wheelchair accessible.' Cabin 12 has central AC and heat 'unlike other cabins' and 2 bathrooms, one in each wing. Cabin 14 has 1 bathroom 'with bathtub and shower', which is a tub, not a walk-in shower. Linens are provided but pillows are not. The park lends an all-terrain wheelchair if you call (512) 321-2101. The Copperas Creek restrooms have a seated shower, handrails and parking in front. TPWD gives no detail on parking distance or the ramp, so call the park to confirm. The review sites (Tripadvisor) blocked access, so no review evidence was gathered.
places.flood_note: The cabins sit in upland pine forest. Nothing found puts them in a floodplain. As of 9/24/2026 the park alerts list only a burn ban (Aug 24, 2026) and a notice that the lake is not yet stocked. There is no cabin closure and no July 2025 flood impact. The forest is still recovering from the 2011 wildfire.
highlights: The only verified ADA cabin that sleeps 8 with 2 private bathrooms and central AC
Cheapest accessible whole-family option ($200 for 8 people)
12 more cabins nearby, all with indoor bathrooms
Call ahead to borrow the park's all-terrain wheelchair
About 40 min from Austin
places.red_flags: The scenery is forest, not the sweeping vista the family asked for. Cabin 14 has a tub/shower combo only. TPWD does not document parking or the ramp at the door. A burn ban is active, so no campfires. Most other cabins have 1 bathroom and window AC only. The review sites could not be reached to check access words.
places.review_signal: No review pages could be loaded (Tripadvisor 403). The official TPWD pages confirm price and ADA status.

places.name: Lake Buchanan RV & Cabin Resort (formerly Big Chief RV Resort), waterfront cabins
places.price_note: From the official rates page (winter / summer daily): Waterfront Cabin 1a, sleeps 8, $175/$205. Waterfront Cabin 1, 2BR, sleeps 6, $142/$174. Waterfront 1BR Cabins 2-6, sleeps 4, $121/$152. Waterfront Shelter Cabin 1b, sleeps 3, $75/$100. The Waterview and Hillside cabins run $100-152. All units add $10/night on weekends and have a 2-night minimum. Weekly rates run $450-1,230. The page does not say which dates count as winter or summer, or what the taxes are. There is no whole-resort buyout.
places.group_note: There are 12 cabins. Waterfront Cabins 1, 1a, 1b and 2-6 sit together on the shore, so the family can book a row: for example 1a (8), 1 (6) and 2-6 (4 each). Cabins 7-10 are pet friendly. Cabins 8 and 10 are hillside, so skip them for grandma. The resort also has a pool, hot tub, clubhouse with kitchen, pavilion, swimming dock, beach and boat ramp.
places.scenery_what: Open water of Lake Buchanan, the largest Highland Lake, with sunsets over the lake from the waterfront cabins. The site describes an 'incredible view of the lake', and a camper review says 'the sunsets were AMAZING.' This is an RV resort, so RVs and other cabins are nearby.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. These are log cabins and no photo or text confirms porch steps. Call and ask for a waterfront cabin with no steps.
places.access_detail: The official site lists a private bathroom, AC/heat and a full kitchen in every cabin (the shelter cabin also has 'A/C, heat' and a 'private bathroom'). The official site, Hipcamp and Campendium give no accessibility, step or parking-distance information. Two cabins are labeled 'hillside'. Reviews do not mention steps, hills or elderly guests.
places.flood_note: The waterfront cabins sit on the Lake Buchanan shoreline. Buchanan is a flood-storage reservoir whose level swings; it is not constant-level, and it rose sharply in the July 2025 Hill Country floods. No damage or closure reports were found. The official site says it is 'Open year-round' and takes online bookings. Ask how high the cabins sit above the water.
highlights: Real waterfront cabins with lake sunsets from the door
Budget to mid prices ($75-215) with official published rates
A row of side-by-side waterfront cabins suits a family group
Pool, hot tub, swimming dock and beach on site
Private bath, AC and full kitchen in every cabin
places.red_flags: Steps and parking at each cabin are unconfirmed. It is an RV resort, so you are not alone with the view. Very few reviews: Campendium 4.4/5 from 6 reviews (2019-2022, under the old Big Chief name), and Hipcamp has none. The operator changed: it is now USA Camping Company. The lake level fluctuates.
places.review_signal: Campendium rates it 4.4/5 from 6 reviews (2019-2022). Reviewers write 'We could see lake and sunsets were great' (2021) and 'the lake was pretty low, but the sunsets were AMAZING' (2022). Hipcamp shows 'booked 6 times' with no reviews. No reviews mention access.

places.name: Inks Lake State Park cabins (Lake Cabins and Hillside Cabins)
places.price_note: From the official TPWD page: $55/night plus the daily entrance fee. A weekly rate of $330 is offered December through February. Weekends and holidays need 2 nights. A third-party guide (updated 9/20/2026) adds a $25 refundable cleaning deposit. Bring your own bedding. No cooking inside.
places.group_note: There are 22 limited-use cabins, each with two sets of twin bunks and sleeping 4. They sit in two clusters: Lake Cabins on an inlet and Hillside Cabins on a granite rise. The family can reserve several. Two cabins are wheelchair-friendly (#1 and #17). Weekends sell out, so book early.
places.scenery_what: Per a third-party guide, the Lake Cabins have a covered front porch facing a quiet inlet, and the Hillside Cabins sit on a granite rise facing west for sunsets. The park itself has pink granite outcrops meeting the lake. It is not confirmed which cluster ADA Cabin 1 is in, or what it looks out on.
places.steps_to_enter: TPWD says Cabin 1 has cement paths from the paved parking area into the cabin, so it has a wheelchair route. Cabins #1 and #17 are wheelchair-friendly.
places.access_detail: TPWD: 'Cabin 1 is wheelchair accessible. It has cement paths from the paved parking area to picnic table, elevated fire ring, upright grill, the interior of the cabin and nearby accessible bathrooms.' The park bathrooms have 'roll-in showers with fold-down seats.' But the cabins have NO bathroom inside. TPWD says only 'Restrooms with showers are nearby', and a third-party guide says they are 'within a 150-foot walk.' The cabins have bunks only, so grandma would sleep on a twin bunk mattress. The cabins have an A/C unit and ceiling fan.
places.flood_note: Inks Lake is a constant-level lake between the Buchanan and Wirtz dams. As of 9/24/2026 the park alerts show a burn ban (July 28, 2026) and hunt closures of some trails and campsites on Dec 3-6 and 14-17 and Jan 4-7, 11-14 and 18-21. No flood closure is listed.
highlights: Cheapest option at $55/night
Wheelchair Cabin 1 has a paved path to the cabin and to accessible roll-in showers
Pink granite and lake scenery, with big skies
22 cabins, so there is room for the whole extended family
places.red_flags: No in-cabin bathroom or water, which is a real problem for grandma at night. Bunk beds only, and you bring your own bedding. No cooking inside. A burn ban is active. Deer-hunt closures run in December and January. Weekends sell out. Best for the younger family, with grandma staying in a hotel or cabin that has a private bath.
places.review_signal: No review pages were checked because search was unavailable. TPWD says 'Day passes and camping sell out every weekend and holiday.'

places.name: Hampton Inn Marble Falls-On the Lake

skeptic.name: Lakeview Haven: 3BD Lakefront Stay | Lake Access & Kayaks
skeptic.evidence: The access and scenery claims hold up, but the price range needed fixing and the group size is a real limit. Checked against the live listing JSON (still active; current title '3BD Lakefront Stay | Lake Access & Kayaks'; the host calls it 'Lakeview Haven' in the description) and all 27 reviews (5.0, Aug 2025 to Sep 2026). ACCESS: The amenity 'Single level home / No stairs in home' is confirmed. The description says '2,450 sq ft single-story home' and 'parking in the driveway for two vehicles'; any extra cars go on the side of a 'very narrow lane'. BUT the host has declared NO Airbnb accessibility features (the accessibility section is empty), so steps at the front door or from the patio onto the TREX deck and lawn are still unconfirmed. Ask the host. BATH: 2 full baths. The primary en suite has a 'Separate luxurious free-standing bath tub and shower', so grandma does not have to step into a tub. The second bath just says 'Shower', type unknown. AC, heating and ceiling fans are listed. SCENERY: A covered patio and deck look over a 'long, flat yard' down to Lake LBJ, and guests describe the lake view and deer from the house. Caveats from a July 2026 review: the water is choppy because the house is 'close to the wake zone and lots of boats', midge flies at night, and TONS of goose droppings at the water's edge. The 'few stairs right down into the water' that review mentions are on the next-door lot's swim entry, not on grandma's path. GROUP SIZE FLAG: max 6 guests, 3 beds (1 king, 2 queens), so it cannot hold a big extended family alone. PRICE (Airbnb all-in nightly, fees included, before taxes, from dated search results): Dec 8-10 and Jan 12-14 midweek $539.50; Apr 20-22 midweek $557; Nov 10-12 $560; Dec 4-6 $591; Nov 6-8 weekend $655; Oct 16-18 weekend $759.50; Mar 12-14, Apr 16-18 and May 14-16 2027 weekends $822.50. So fall 2026 is about $540-760, but spring 2027 weekends reach about $823. BOOKABLE: The calendar shows open dates across Oct 2026 to Aug 2027, 2-night minimum. FLOODS: The listing's reviews start Aug 2025 and none mention flood damage. I could not run a further news check on July 2025 Lake LBJ damage because the web search budget was used up, so that part is unverified beyond the reviews.
