The official FAQ says 'most of our stays are designed primarily for couples', but invites groups to contact them to 'select the right combination of accommodations.' A family would need several units, which are separate but close together.
places.scenery_what: Each tent or dome sits on its own raised private deck on a ridge, looking out over rolling Hill Country. The Suite Tent has 'uninterrupted... ridge views' from a hot tub. The Forest Dome is tucked in trees with less view. There's a pond, walking trails and dark skies, and the other units are nearby.
highlights: Private bathroom inside every unit (official FAQ) and split-system AC and heat
Suite Tent: separate living area, private hot tub, sleeps up to 6
Named '#1 Glamping Destination in the U.S.' by The Dyrt (2024), per the property
A July 2025 Hipcamp review says the ridge-top elevation kept guests safe during the historic flooding
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. Every unit sits on a raised deck, and the Suite is described as 'set on an elevated deck'. Ask which unit has the fewest steps.
places.access_detail: Official FAQ: 'all four geodesic domes include private bathrooms located inside the accommodation' and 'All tents and domes include electricity, Wi-Fi, and air conditioning.' On parking, the FAQ only says 'Guests should park in the designated parking areas.' The Suite listing says 'Free parking is available nearby.' I could not confirm the earlier claim that parking is next to the units. The safari tents' baths have a 'clawfoot tub and attached shower', which is hard for an elderly person to step into; the domes have a regular 'private shower', which is a better pick for grandma. No review mentions steps or mobility. July 2023 and July 2024 dome reviews say the AC 'will not stand up to the mid-day sun' in summer.
places.flood_note: Ridge-top property, not in a floodplain. A Hipcamp guest who was there during the July 2025 'historical flooding' wrote, 'we were at an elevation that ensured our safety', but also reported power outages and flooded roads, and the host timed their exit. In heavy rain, expect road closures around Burnet County rather than water at the units.
places.red_flags: Built for couples, so most units hold only 2 adults. The distance and steps from car to deck are unconfirmed. Safari-tent bathing is a clawfoot tub. There are no kitchens (mini fridge, microwave and coffee maker only). Domes get hot on summer afternoons. A Dec 2024 review mentions morning construction noise, 'sounded like a cement factory within a mile'.
places.review_signal: The site shows 5.0 stars from 48 Google reviews. Hipcamp: 100% recommend (8 reviews). Airbnb units: 4.79-5.0 (Woodland Dome 4.94 from 53 reviews; Suite 4.95 from 20). Reviews praise the views, cleanliness and host Laura.

places.name: Talula Mesa Glamping Resort
places.price_note: Official FAQ rates: Grand Tesoro $250 weekdays / $350 weekends; Grand Arrow $275 / $375; Grand Aztec $295 / $395. The site gives an overall range of '$80-$450 per night' depending on season, guests and pets, and the Mini Aztec sits at the low end. The Grand tent rate covers 2-3 guests, and a 4th guest is +$50/night. The website books 2 nights minimum; 1-night Sun-Thu stays are possible by calling. Hipcamp shows 'from $270'. The site says booking direct is cheaper than Airbnb. Firewood is $10 a bundle. Pets: the FAQ says $25 per dog, but the Hipcamp listing says no animals. No whole-resort buyout price is published.
places.group_note: 4 tents on 15 acres, 100-300 ft apart: 3 Grand tents (king bed on the main floor plus a small queen loft for kids 5+, 3 guests base, 4th guest for an extra fee) and 1 Mini Aztec. About 13 guests fit on the whole property. A guest review mentions wanting to 'rent the whole property', but the site doesn't state buyout terms, so call.
places.scenery_what: A hilltop mesa above Lake Travis. Each Grand tent has a floor-to-ceiling glass back wall and a back porch with a private hot tub. The Grand Aztec has the most open lake-and-hills view, the Arrow has a lake view through trees, and the Tesoro looks across a ravine at the hill country. Big sunsets and stars.
highlights: Private hot tub on every Grand tent
King bed is on the main floor, so grandma doesn't have to climb to the loft
Only 4 tents, so it's quiet and could house most of a family
Lake access at Turkey Bend Recreation Area, a 2-minute drive; kayaks and paddleboards are free to borrow
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown for the tent porches. The kids' lofts are up above the king bed, and the property has stone steps (for example, down to the yoga hut). Parking distance is not stated.
places.access_detail: Official FAQ: 'A shared bathhouse is located between all of the tents, about a 30-second walk' with 'two enclosed, heated showers... two sinks, and an indoor toilet'. Hipcamp says '1 toilet' shared by all 4 tents. Guests are told to bring flip-flops and a headlamp for night restroom trips. AC is window units: 'If the outdoor temp reaches 100... it might be 85 in your tent', and a June 2024 review says it was 'still warm at the peak of the day'. There's a propane fireplace for winter. The king bed is on the main level. Parking distance is not published.
places.flood_note: Hilltop above Lake Travis, not in a floodplain. The July 2025 flood destroyed the RR 1431 Cow Creek bridge east of the property on the Austin-side route; the new bridge opened Aug 19, 2025 (DailyTrib). In July 2026, Lake Travis filled to about 681 ft (full) with no reported damage.
places.red_flags: No bathroom in the tents, and one toilet shared by up to 4 tents, which is a poor fit for grandma unless she sleeps elsewhere. The window AC struggles on hot afternoons. Lofts are for kids 5+. The site footer says (c) 2025, and live date availability couldn't be checked; the Hipcamp listing is LIVE, with a Dec 2025 review.
places.review_signal: The official reviews page and Hipcamp (100%, 6 ratings) are strongly positive about the views, privacy and the owner, Shannon. Recurring caveats are shared-bathhouse nerves ('it wasn't an issue') and summer heat.

places.name: On The Rocks Glamping Resort
places.town: Marble Falls area (6807 Shaw Dr, hilltop above the upper Lake Travis / Colorado River arm, near Turkey Bend; next to Talula Mesa)
places.price_note: Official rates are embedded in the Lodgify pages. Luxury Suites 2 and 3 cost $199 Mon to Wed, $225 Thu and Sun, and $325 Fri and Sat. Premium Suites 1 and 4 cost $219 Mon to Wed, $250 Thu and Sun, and $350 Fri and Sat. Taxes are extra. A cleaning fee line exists at checkout, but the amount is not shown. A $300 damage-deposit hold applies. You pay 50% when booking and the rest 7 days before arrival. Cancel 30+ days out for a full refund, 14+ days out for 50%, and after that nothing comes back. The pet fee is $100 for the first dog and $50 for a second. No minimum stay is stated. There is no buyout price, and the whole place is only 4 tents. I could not check the live calendar because the Lodgify API sits behind a Cloudflare challenge.
places.group_note: There are 4 safari tents, each for 2 guests maximum with a king bed, so 8 adults at most. The rental agreement says 'We do not allow children'. It also allows 'one guest vehicle' per booking and at most 2 non-overnight visitors. That works only for an adults-only part of the family. Relatives with kids would have to stay at Talula Mesa next door, which I did not verify.
places.scenery_what: You step out onto an elevated private wooden deck with a cable rail, looking across a wide hill-country valley to the Lake Travis / Colorado River arm. The official photos show a real panorama and sunsets from the deck hot tub. Neighbors are the other 3 tents and privacy fences a few yards away.
places.access_detail: From the official site: each suite has 'Heating and A/C' (a mini-split shows in the photos) and a 'full bathroom' with a rain-head shower. The resort area has 'Private parking with gated entrance'. A photo captioned 'View as you enter your private gated area' shows you enter through a fenced courtyard straight onto the deck. The site does not say how far the parking is from each tent, how many steps lead to the decks, or whether the shower has a curb. The site is a rocky hilltop, as the name suggests. I could not get any review text; search budget was exhausted and third-party review pages were blocked.
places.flood_note: The tents sit on a hilltop well above any floodplain. The July 2025 flash floods hit the Lake Travis area (Sandy Creek in NW Travis County) and Burnet County, but the site shows no flood notice and the tents are not exposed. The nearby lake access at Turkey Bend (LCRA) was not checked.
highlights: True hill-country panorama from every private deck
Private hot tub or soaking tub on each deck, plus a shared pond pool, community hot tub and fire pit
Real in-tent bathroom, AC/heat and kitchenette
Official posted rates of $199 to $350 a night
places.red_flags: NO CHILDREN allowed (rental agreement rule 5). Only 2 guests and 1 car per tent. It is marketed as a couples' getaway. Steps and the walk from parking are unconfirmed, on a rocky hilltop. The water is well water with high mineral content.
places.review_signal: No review text retrieved. The official photos confirm the view.

places.name: Horseshoe Bay Resort (The Tower lake-view rooms, Palm Villas, The Residences)
places.price_note: The official SynXis booking engine would not show rates without a live session. The figures here come from aggregators. Kayak lists the cheapest at $158/night (King), $158 to $451 over the last 2 weeks, December cheapest (about $252 average) and May priciest (about $361), with Saturday the most expensive night. Momondo averages about $258 and goes up to about $607 for some room types. Suites, Residences and private homes cost more, and I did not verify those prices. OFFICIAL add-ons: a $45/night resort fee (Wi-Fi, pools, fitness, kayaks and paddleboards, and 'transportation throughout the resort'). Self-parking is $17/day (from Jan 1, 2026); valet is free for the first hour and $40 overnight. There is a $75 pet fee, and only Palm Villas take pets. Cancel 72 hours before arrival or pay for one night. The 'Midweek Getaway, Upgraded' package runs Sun to Thu, needs 2 nights, and includes free valet, breakfast, a $100 daily resort credit and an upgrade.
places.group_note: Hotel rooms in The Tower include Classic Accessible King and Classic Accessible Double. The 99 Palm Villas are pitched as 'perfect for families or groups'. Residences are 1 to 3 bedroom condos (Classic condos sleep up to 8, max 6 adults), and Premier Water View condos have balconies or patios over Lake LBJ. There are also private homes, condos and townhomes for rent. A family could book several rooms or condos in the same building, with grandma in an accessible Tower room.
places.scenery_what: Tower rooms can be booked by Lake, Hill Country, Pool or Resort view. Premier Water View condos look straight over Lake LBJ from a private balcony or patio. The grounds are manicured, with a marina and a sandy beach. It is a busy resort with golf, other guests and events, not a wild view.
places.park_at_unit: Not at the unit. Self-parking is in 'multiple surface parking lots conveniently located within walking distance of our hotel' ($17/day). Valet is tiered, up to $40 overnight, and can drop her at the entrance. Complimentary resort transportation to amenities and restaurants is by request.
places.private_bath: In unit, but the official accessibility page lists only a 'Tub with grab bars' and 'Toilet with grab bars' for accessible rooms, a step-in tub. No roll-in or walk-in shower is listed.
places.access_detail: The official accessibility page lists 'Accessible parking spaces for cars in self-parking facility'. It also lists an accessible route from the entrance to registration, the restaurants and the spa. Accessible rooms have 32-inch clear doorways, a 'toilet with grab bars' and a 'tub with grab bars'. No roll-in shower is mentioned, so ask for one. The FAQ says Classic Accessible King and Double rooms can be booked online, and resort transportation is included in the resort fee. Valet can drop her at the door. The pages I read do not mention elevators, so confirm them for any Residences unit. Aggregator pages also mention 'a select number of accessible guest rooms'.
places.flood_note: The resort is on Lake LBJ, a constant-level lake on the Colorado that took floodwater from the Llano and Colorado in July 2025. It is clearly operating in 2026: parking rates effective Jan 1, 2026, and holiday events are posted. I found no flood notice. The lakeside Residences and marina are the units closest to the water.
highlights: Easiest option for grandma: bookable ADA rooms, accessible parking and routes, valet, resort transport
Lake-view rooms and water-view condos on Lake LBJ
Condos and villas for the rest of the family in one place
Pools, beach, spa, dining on site, so nobody has to drive
places.red_flags: The $45/night resort fee and $17 parking or $40 valet add up. Reviews complain the resort fee isn't shown upfront. Accessible baths have tubs with grab bars, not confirmed roll-in showers. Nightly prices are aggregator figures, not official. It feels like a golf resort, not glamping.
places.review_signal: Momondo rates it 8.1/10 from 294 ratings. Kayak snippets praise a 'beautiful resort', 'spectacular' lake views and well-kept grounds. Complaints cover surprise resort fees, uneven service and event noise.

skeptic.name: Horseshoe Bay Resort (The Tower lake-view rooms, Palm Villas, The Residences)
skeptic.corrected_park_at_unit: Not at the unit. Self-parking is in 'multiple surface parking lots conveniently located within walking distance of our hotel' ($17/day). Valet is tiered, up to $40 overnight, and can drop her at the entrance. Complimentary resort transportation to amenities and restaurants is by request.
skeptic.corrected_private_bath: In unit, but the official accessibility page lists only a 'Tub with grab bars' and 'Toilet with grab bars' for accessible rooms, a step-in tub. No roll-in or walk-in shower is listed.
skeptic.evidence: The official FAQ confirms ADA rooms: 'Classic Accessible King Room and Classic Accessible Double Room.' The accessibility page lists accessible self-park spaces, an 'Accessible route from accessible public entrance to accessible guest rooms', 32-inch doors, and a tub with grab bars (no roll-in shower). Elevators are not mentioned on any page I read. Extra costs: 'daily Resort Fee of $45 per room, per night' plus $17/day self-parking or valet. There is no swimming in the lake: 'There are no direct access points to swim on Lake LBJ from the resort property.' The Tower is described as having 'spectacular views of the resort and rolling hills beyond' (250 rooms). Lake view is a filter option, but whether any Classic Accessible room has a lake view is unknown. The Palm Villas (99) and Residences pages give no accessibility, floor or elevator details. The $158 to $450 range could not be verified from official pages. The marina page shows no flood, closure or construction notices, and the resort is taking bookings (offers are live). Net: step-in tub, paid parking not at the door, $45/night fee, and an unconfirmed lake view for the ADA rooms make it weaker for grandma than claimed.

places.name: Waterfront Luxury w/Views, Patio, Water Access (single-story 4BR)
places.price_note: Price unknown. Airbnb loads the price client-side, so it would not come through even with dates in the URL. The public availability calendar shows it is bookable: 18 of 31 October nights, 22 of 30 November and 19 of 31 December 2026 are open. The minimum stay is 3 nights, and 5 on some November dates. It is managed by the host 'Fairly' (Superhost, 1,362 reviews, 4.8). Horseshoe Bay STR permit #224. It is probably splurge tier, but that is unverified.

places.scenery_what: Listing photos show the house on a cove of Lake LBJ. There is a lawn down to a stone-edged waterline, a covered patio with a wall of glass, and a boat dock, with a sunset photo from the patio. Across the narrow cove you see other large lake homes, so the neighbors are clearly in view.
places.access_detail: The listing says 'This single-story luxury retreat' and 'Single-story layout'. Airbnb amenities include 'Free parking on premises', 'Air conditioning' and 'Bathtub', and there are 4.5 baths. Airbnb shows NO step-free or accessibility tags. The front door is a double entry, and the listing doesn't say whether there are entry steps or how far the parking is. The patio looks level with the lawn in the photos. With only 4 reviews (all 5.0), there are no access comments.
places.flood_note: The house is directly waterfront on Lake LBJ, a constant-level lake that carried the July 2025 Llano and Colorado floodwater. I don't know if the property was affected. The listing is live and has open dates.
highlights: Single-story house right on the water with a dock and lawn
4.5 baths for 12 people
Big covered patio and open-plan living with lake views
Horseshoe Bay dining and golf nearby
places.red_flags: Price unknown. The 3-night minimum is 5 on some November dates. Airbnb lists the carbon monoxide alarm as 'Unavailable'. Only 4 reviews. No step-free tags, so confirm entry steps with the host. Neighbors are close across the cove.
places.review_signal: 4 reviews, 5.0 in every category. No text retrieved.

places.name: Black Rock Park (LCRA) - Airstreams and cabins on Lake Buchanan
places.kind: Airstream trailers + camping cabins (LCRA public park)
places.price_note: Official 'starting at' rates: Airstreams $199 (sleep 4, private bath), standard cabins $75 (sleep 4, no bath), deluxe cabins $129 (sleep 3, no bath). Weekend and holiday rates were not shown. The Campspot booking page loads rates client-side. On top of that you pay the park entrance fee: $5 per adult, $2 for seniors 65+, military and disabled guests, and free for kids 12 and under. Kayak and paddleboard rentals cost $49 to $109. No minimum stay is stated.
places.group_note: There are 4 Airstreams (named Laurel, Buck, Gus and Lasso) side by side in the RV loop. The 12 standard and 6 deluxe cabins line a lakeside peninsula about 700 to 1,100 ft away by the park map scale, and you can drive between them. Lake View Hall can be booked for group meals. The best split is grandma in an Airstream and everyone else in cabins.
places.scenery_what: The park map (Jan 14, 2026) shows the Airstreams in the interior RV area, a few hundred feet from the shore and not on the water. Stepping out, you see the RV loop, mini golf and park lawns. The cabins, not the Airstreams, sit along the Lake Buchanan shoreline peninsula. Those would rate about 7, but they have no bathroom.
places.access_detail: Official: the Airstreams are 'Climate controlled' with a 'Private restroom with shower', an indoor kitchen, and a patio with a gas grill and fire pit. Cabins are 'Climate controlled' but have no bathroom listed. Cabin guests use the flush restrooms and showers building at the cabin-area entrance (site 56 on the map). The Airstreams sit on drive-in spurs off the RV loop, so she can probably park beside the trailer, but that isn't stated. No ADA units are listed. Airstream trailers usually have an entry step and a tight bathroom, which is unconfirmed here. I found no review text.
places.flood_note: The park is on the Lake Buchanan shore at the top of the Highland Lakes chain. The July 2025 floods raised the Highland Lakes, but the park is clearly operating: an Oct 2, 2026 'S'mores and Stars' event is posted and the park map is dated Jan 2026. There is no closure notice. The only active notice is a Llano County burn ban.
highlights: Cheapest option: cabins from $75, Airstreams from $199
Real campground feel with swimming beach, kayak and paddleboard rentals, mini golf
$2 senior entry for grandma
Lake View Hall for family gatherings
places.red_flags: The Airstreams are NOT lakefront. The lakefront cabins have no bathroom, so it's a walk to the shared bathhouse. Airstream entry steps and tight bathrooms are a risk for grandma. It is about 2 hours from SA, near the edge of the range. Burn ban currently in effect.
places.review_signal: None retrieved.

places.name: The Antlers Inn - Train Depot cabin and Sunrise/Sunset cottages
places.kind: inn/B&B (historic inn with cottages, depot and caboose cabins)
places.price_note: Price unknown. The official site shows no rates. Its SiteMinder booking engine (direct-book.com/properties/theantlersinndirect) is live but sits behind a bot challenge I did not bypass. Policy: full deposit at booking, rates based on double occupancy, taxes extra. Cancel by 14 days out for a refund less $25, 48 hours to 14 days out for 50%, and under 48 hours you pay the whole stay. Book 3+ nights by phone for 15% off (holidays excluded). Pets are allowed in cabins for $100. Check-in 3 PM, check-out 11 AM.

Sunrise cottage page: 'Direct parking in front', a porch with rocking chairs, and a 'traditional tub/shower combination' in each bath, which is harder for grandma. No ramp is mentioned for the cottages. The amenities page lists 'AC/Heat in all accommodations', private entries and free on-site parking. The Depot's shower type isn't stated. No review text was retrieved.

I could not confirm whether this property was affected. The site shows no flood notice and lists every unit as bookable, but its 'special events' list stops at 2024 and Suite 5 is marked 'under renovation'. Call 325-388-4411 to confirm the grounds, pier and units are in normal shape.
highlights: Park right in front of every unit
Train Depot has an accessible ramp, 2 private baths, sleeps 8
Several family units side by side on one property; kids welcome outside the inn suites
On-site restaurants and the Lake LBJ pier a short walk away
places.red_flags: No prices online. Flood impact from 2025 is unverified. The cottages have tub/shower combos and no stated ramp. The view is grounds, not the lake. No reviews checked.
places.review_signal: None retrieved (Yelp returned 403, and other review pages couldn't be reached without search).

places.name: Lakeside house with sunset views and kayaks on Lake Marble Falls (Airbnb)
places.price_note: One data point only: the finder's 9/24/2026 Airbnb search showed about $2,274 for 5 nights, marked down from $2,695, which is about $455/night. Airbnb search totals usually include fees before taxes. I could not re-pull the price because Airbnb loads it client-side. The public calendar shows it bookable: 14 of 31 October nights, 25 of 30 November and all of December 2026 are open, with a 1 to 2 night minimum.

places.scenery_what: The listing describes '180° views of the lake' from the living and dining room. Photos show wide calm water on Lake Marble Falls with a wooded far shore, a lakefront gazebo on a floating dock, a stone fire-pit patio, and deer and ducks. A public boat ramp is right next door.

highlights: Confirmed single-level, step-free entry and a wide accessible parking spot
180-degree lake view from the main living space
Kayaks, paddle boat, private dock, gazebo and fire pit
Strong reviews: 4.89 from 128

skeptic.name: Lakeside house with sunset views and kayaks on Lake Marble Falls (Airbnb)
skeptic.evidence: The listing is live and bookable, and the car-to-house access is confirmed. The claim fails on price, and reviews show a steep hill down to the water plus yard and upkeep problems. Checked against the live listing JSON (current title 'Pet-Friendly Lake House w/ Sunset Views & Kayaks'; the host calls it 'Lakeview Retreat'; 4.89 from 128 reviews) and about 50 recent reviews, Feb 2025 to Sep 2026. CONFIRMED: The accessibility stops are exactly two. 'Disabled parking spot' (private spot at least 11 ft wide) and 'Step-free access' for the LIVING ROOM (no steps or thresholds over 2 in between the guest entrance and that room). There is also 'Single level home / No stairs in home'. The photo caption 'Front door and front yard... two covered areas that can fit up to 4 cars' supports parking at the door. AC, central heating and ceiling fans are listed. The bathrooms are NOT covered by any step-free declaration. The primary en suite has 'a nice shower' and the hallway bath (shared by everyone in the house) has 'an amazing Shower'. No bathtub is listed, but whether the showers have a curb is unknown. REFUTING EVIDENCE: A June 2025 review says 'the steepness of the trek down the hill to the water wasn't clear from the photos'. That means the lakefront gazebo and dock, the headline scenery features, are NOT step-out for grandma. She gets the view from the living room windows and patio only. Other reviews: sticker burrs cover the yard (Aug 2026, May 2025); weeds, 'lots of ants' so you could not sit or stand long, and the patio 'wasn't much better' (3-star, July 2026); water stains on the ceiling and a dated interior (3-star, May 2026); the public boat ramp next door 'can be disruptive'. The 'sleeps 12' is overstated: the sofa beds are leather fold-downs that 'could maybe fit 2 small kids, not adults' (Aug 2026), and 2 bathrooms serve up to 12 people. The scenery itself is real: the 'entire back wall of windows' faces the lake, 'no houses on the other side', and there are lots of deer. So the scenery score of 7 stands. PRICE is wrong: it is not a flat $455. Airbnb all-in nightly (fees included, before taxes) from dated searches: Dec 4-6 $443; Nov 10-12 $462; Oct 12-14 $509.50; Apr 20-22 $541.50; Jan 12-14 $542; Nov 6-8 $546.50; Apr 16-18 $649.50; May 14-16 $699.50; Mar 12-14 2027 $707. Price did not change between 6 and 10 adults. BOOKABLE: The calendar is open across Oct 2026 to Aug 2027, 1-2 night minimum. FLOODS: A July 2025 review says they 'couldn't get into the water due to the recent flooding' (the house sits just below Wirtz Dam). Reviews continue every month afterward with no damage reports, but a dock or shoreline condition check with the host is advised. No further news search was possible because the web search budget was used up.

places.name: Black Rock Park Airstreams (LCRA)

highlights: True glamping with a private bathroom and AC

Walk to Blanco's town square and cafes

Main-floor bedroom for grandma, loft for kids

2-3 min to Fredericksburg Main Street

Weeknights are about half the weekend price
places.red_flags: Weekend rate ($654) is nearly double the weeknight rate. Farthest drive in the set: about 2h from SA and 2h20m from Austin. Rural rocky road with loose cattle and weak cell service. About 30 min to Fredericksburg for groceries and pharmacy. Ranch and hunting land around it, so it's a sit-and-look spot, not a walking one. Cabin 2 has steps and had an AC/heat failure in Apr 2025.

places.name: The Johnson House - Within Blanco State Park
places.price_note: Airbnb search prices (checked 9/24/2026, fees folded in, before taxes): $262.50/night Tue-Thu Nov 10-12 for 6 adults; $372.50/night Fri-Sat Dec 4-6 for 12 adults. Earlier finder data: about $312/night Dec 4-6 for 6 adults. It did not show for the Nov 6-8 or Oct 16-18 weekends, so those may be booked. House rules: $30 prearranged late checkout; $100 for up to an hour late without prior arrangement; $50 lost-key fee.
places.group_note: The whole 5BR/2BA house sleeps 14 (5 queens plus 4 singles). It's the only unit here, but it sits beside Blanco Riverside Getaway, so overflow family could book cottages there.
places.scenery_what: A big front porch with rockers and a swing looking at the Blanco River and the water spilling over the dam, inside the state park, with 'only 1 neighbor, the state park police'. A shaded paved path leads to Blanco's square in about 5 min. One 2024 review says park vehicles and equipment were parked in front of the house, 'obstructing the view of the river'.
places.steps_to_enter: Listed as a 'Single level home' but also flagged 'Must climb stairs', most likely the porch steps of a raised 1911 farmhouse. The number of steps is unknown, so ask the host.
places.access_detail: Listing: free parking on premises, with the rule 'Park on the INSIDE of the rock wall', so parking is on the house grounds. Central AC plus portable fans. 2 baths for up to 14 people. Reviews: hot water runs out ('Only one person could shower at a time', 2023), 'Hot water in one of the bathrooms is tricky' (Sept 2026), and 'the back AC unit was not cooling' until the host sent an AC repair person (Apr 2025). The address doesn't take you to the actual house, so guests have trouble finding it (Nov 2025). No review mentions stairs or elderly access.
places.flood_note: Riverfront inside Blanco State Park, directly on the Blanco River floodplain by the dam. The river is known for flash floods. The TPWD alert page (checked 9/24/2026) shows only a burn ban, and reviews run through June, Aug and Sept 2025 and on to Sept 2026, so there was no visible closure after the July 2025 floods. Watch the forecast and leave early if heavy rain is coming.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.80 (163 reviews, latest 2 weeks ago). Recurring praise for the porch and river ('The porch and view was really extra!'). A 2024 review from a grandmother with 5 grandkids was positive.
highlights: Porch over the river and dam, inside a state park
One house for 14, the easiest way to keep the whole family together
Walk to Blanco's square, BBQ and coffee
About 1h05m from SA, the closest in this set with Blanco Riverside
places.red_flags: 'Must climb stairs' flag with an unknown step count. Only 2 baths for up to 14 guests, and hot water has run short. AC hiccups (2025). A historic older house. Park vehicles are sometimes in front of the view. It sits in the river floodplain. Guests must check in with the park to reach the river or other park areas. Not a TPWD cabin.

places.name: Carter Creek Winery Resort & Spa
places.price_note: Rates were checked Sep 24, 2026 on Google Hotels, which shows the official-site rate. Weeknight (Thu Nov 19-20): King villa $155 base from the official site, $137 from the cheapest third-party site. Double Queen villa $177 (Hotels.com). Google calls $98-154 typical for that weeknight. Weekend of Nov 6-8: King and ADA King $350 official, Double Queen $373 (Expedia base). Weekend of Dec 11-13: King and ADA King $240 official. Added costs: a $25/night resort amenity fee plus taxes, and dogs are $75 per stay. The deposit is the first night. Cancellations must be made 72 hours ahead. Booking direct gets 20% off 2 nights, 25% off 3 nights, and AAA/AARP or military members get 10% off. The $100/day credit package ends Sep 30, 2026. There is no extra fee for a 3rd or 4th adult (max 4 per villa). No whole-property buyout is listed.
places.group_note: There are three villa types. The Double Queen sleeps 4 (max 4 adults, no extra-adult fee). The Deluxe King and the ADA Deluxe King each sleep 2. The total number of villas is not published. A family can book several villas online and ask to be placed near each other, but the terms say room-location requests depend on availability. The on-site restaurant takes online reservations for up to 6. Larger groups have to call.
places.scenery_what: Each villa has a private patio or porch on a winery campus along US 290. Guests can request vineyard or pool views. The pool, hot tub, tasting room, brewery restaurant and spa are all within walking distance. It is pleasant wine-village grounds, not a sweeping Hill Country vista or wilderness.
places.steps_to_enter: The ADA villa has a ramp entry. The site lists 46-inch exterior entry pathways and an accessible entry to the private patio. Step counts for the standard villas are not stated.
places.access_detail: The official ADA page for the ADA Deluxe King Villa (494 sq ft) lists: "On site accessible self-parking", "Ramp entry to rooms", a roll-in shower with two grab bars, an ADA toilet with bars, lowered A/C and heat controls, 36-inch clearance throughout, and accessible pool entrances. It has a separate soaking tub plus an accessible shower. How far the accessible parking is from the ADA villa door is not published, which is the only reason this is not scored 10. On Google Hotels and the OTAs, 'Deluxe Villa, 1 King Bed, Accessible' is bookable at the same rate as the standard King.
places.flood_note: Not on a river. It sits on US 290 about 2 miles south of the Pedernales River. The official site mentions no 2025 flood impact, and the resort is open and taking bookings for Nov and Dec 2026.
highlights: Only candidate with a fully documented ADA villa (ramp, roll-in shower, grab bars)
Pool, hot tub, spa, restaurant, brewery and tasting room all walkable
Double Queen villas sleep 4 with no extra-adult fee
Weeknights from about $155 plus a $25 resort fee
places.red_flags: It is a highway-side wine resort, not wilderness scenery. There is a $25/night resort fee plus taxes. Weekend rates run about double weeknight rates ($240-373). How many villas exist, and whether villas can be placed next to each other, is not published.
places.review_signal: Google 4.3/5 (277 reviews). Tripadvisor 4.6/5 (616 reviews). Reviews praise having the winery, brewery, spa and restaurant on site and the roomy villas. No access complaints turned up in the review snippets I could see.

places.name: Walden Retreats Hill Country
places.price_note: Rates were checked Sep 24, 2026 on Google Hotels. Weeknight (Thu Nov 19-20): Classic tent $310 base from the official site ($315 on Hotels.com), Superior tent $473, Premier tent $592 (the OTAs use these tent names, not the site's). Weekend of Dec 4-6: Classic $320 from the official site, Premier $706 (Expedia base). The weekend of Nov 6-8 was already sold out, and Google offered Oct 30-Nov 1 at about $317 instead. Rates assume 2 people. A 3rd or 4th adult is suites only, at $40 per person per night plus a $50 one-time air-bed fee. Dogs are $50/night. Half is paid at booking and the rest 15 days before arrival. Cancellations within 14 days get no refund, and there are no weather refunds. Full-property buyouts exist (policies mention them), but no price is listed.
places.group_note: 15 tents: 7 suites that sleep 2-4 (queen air mattress for guests 3-4) and 8 studios that sleep 2 (4 of them with wood-fired hot tubs). The property is adult-oriented. No children under 7 are allowed except at weddings or full buyouts, and kids 7-17 can stay only in suites (the FAQ says two 'Family Suites'). A family would book several tents or ask about a full buyout, which includes a 3,500 sq ft event lodge.
places.scenery_what: Canvas safari tents with 300-400 sq ft wrap-around decks among the trees on 96 acres of cliffs above the Pedernales River. The site describes it as "Perched among the cliffs of the Pedernales River". There is a 5,000 sq ft lawn and a big fire pit high above the river, private fire pits and grills, and dark-sky stargazing from the deck. There are no TVs anywhere on the property.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. Tents sit on wooden decks. The private-events page says 1 of the 15 tents is ADA accessible, but gives no details.
places.access_detail: Official FAQ: "all vehicles must remain in our parking lot". The lot is "a short 5 minute walk from all of our rooms. We will provide transportation in our golf cart during check in and check out" only. The property "consists only of gravel roads, paths and dirt hiking trails". The river is a 10-minute walk ending in a "very steep descent" with a rope. Each tent has a private ensuite bath with a clawfoot tub (a high step-in) and an outdoor shower. The mini-split AC and heat sit over the bed, but the tents are "uninsulated canvas". The private-events page says "(1 ADA accessible)". Ask whether grandma can get that tent and extra cart rides.
places.flood_note: The tents sit on bluffs above the Pedernales, with 1,500 ft of private river frontage below. The site mentions no 2025 flood damage, and the property is open with rates for Nov and Dec 2026. The tents are high above the river, but the river area itself is subject to flash floods.
highlights: The true glamping pick: safari tents on cliffs above the Pedernales
Private ensuite bath, kitchen, AC and heat, and a wrap-around deck in every tent
One ADA-accessible tent per the property's events page
Google 4.9/5 from 302 reviews
Full-property buyout option for a family event
places.red_flags: No driving to the tents. It is a 5-minute gravel walk, and the golf cart runs only at check-in and check-out. The clawfoot tub is hard to step into. Canvas tents get hot or cold in extreme weather. Kids under 7 are not allowed without a buyout, and kids 7-17 can stay only in suites. Weekends sell out and the cancellation policy is strict. Burn bans can cancel campfires.
places.review_signal: Google 4.9/5 (302 reviews). Reviewers praise the clawfoot tubs, the kitchenettes (no stove, just a Breville oven and a grill) and the friendly staff. One reviewer called it a 15-minute hike down the cleared trail to the river.

places.name: Outbound Ranch
places.town: Gillespie County (near Hye, about 20 min from Fredericksburg)
places.price_note: Prices come from Airbnb search results checked Sep 24, 2026, for 8 adults. Weeknight Nov 17-19: $478/night ($956 for 2 nights, discounted from $1,060). Weekends Nov 6-8 and Dec 11-13: $1,177/night ($2,354 for 2 nights). Airbnb labels these prices as including all fees, so cleaning and service fees are probably already inside the nightly figure, and taxes may be extra. The house rules add a $200 fine for arriving before 4 pm or leaving after 10 am, and $200 fines for smoking or candles. No minimum stay was visible.
places.group_note: Whole house, max 8 guests: a king master, a queen room, and a bunk room with 3 twins and 1 full. It is an Airbnb Luxe listing managed by Heavenly Hosts. A family bigger than 8 would need a second rental nearby. The listing mentions no guest house.
places.scenery_what: A modern 2023 house on 33 secluded private acres. The living room has 10-foot floor-to-ceiling windows onto the Hill Country. There are sunrise views from the porch, an outdoor sauna with a picture window, and a private hot tub. Airbnb's summary calls the views from the sauna and hot tub 'sweeping', and the property has dark skies for stargazing and a fire pit with Adirondack chairs.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. The listing has no 'Must climb stairs' flag and its accessibility section is empty. Single-level layout and step count at the entry are not confirmed, so ask.
places.access_detail: Free parking on the property, with a garage and a driveway (security cameras are 'on the garage facing the driveway and one facing the front entrance'). It has AC and heat. The master bathroom is ensuite with a 'spacious walk in shower'. The hall bath has a stand-in shower, and there are no tubs. Airbnb shows no stairs warning, unlike the Blue Dog and Serengeti listings. The hot tub, sauna and cold shower are outdoors, and the outdoor shower is closed from mid-October to March.
places.flood_note: The house is on acreage in Gillespie County, and the listing mentions no river frontage, so river-flood exposure looks low. I found no report of 2025 flood impact. The listing is active and bookable for Nov and Dec 2026.
highlights: Best 'step out to the view' house among these candidates: 33 private acres with floor-to-ceiling windows
Private hot tub, outdoor sauna, fire pit, dark skies
Master bath has a walk-in shower, with no tubs to climb into
Airbnb 4.96/5 (45 reviews), Guest Favorite, Luxe
places.red_flags: This is the splurge: about $1,177/night on weekends. It sleeps only 8. Single-level and step-free entry are not confirmed. Check-in and check-out rules are strict with $200 fines. The outdoor cameras record audio.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.96/5 from 45 reviews, a Guest Favorite. Sub-scores are 5.0 for cleanliness and accuracy, 4.9 for check-in and location, and 4.8 for value. The host is a superhost who responds within an hour. The review summary highlights a spotless, high-end house and the sauna and hot tub views. Individual reviews could not be pulled, so I did not see any access-specific comments.

places.name: Sweet Serengeti Safari Ranch (Safari cabin + 3 B&B rooms in the main house)
places.town: Blanco (about 2 mi from the town square, behind Real Ale Brewery)
places.price_note: Prices come from Airbnb search results checked Sep 24, 2026. Cabin (sleeps 8): $357.50/night on the weeknight of Nov 17-19 (6 adults) and $380.64/night on Dec 11-13. It was not available Nov 6-8 or on the January and February dates I tried. B&B rooms (2 guests each, breakfast included): African Rainforest $210/night, Wild Safari and Peacock Forest $202.50/night (Nov 17-19). African Rainforest was also $210 on Nov 6-8 and Dec 11-13. Airbnb shows fee-inclusive totals, and taxes may be extra. The cabin has a 2-night minimum. Dogs are allowed in the cabin only (max 2, strict rules).
places.group_note: The cabin sleeps 8: a downstairs ensuite Cal-King room, an open loft with 2 trundle beds up a narrow staircase, and a queen sofa bed. All 8 share ONE bathroom. The main house has 3 themed B&B rooms (Wild Safari, Peacock Forest, African Rainforest), each with a king bed and a private attached bath, sleeping 2 each. Booking the cabin plus all 3 rooms puts about 14 people on the same 40-acre ranch. The rooms are in the hosts' own home, with shared common areas.
places.scenery_what: A 40-acre exotic-animal ranch. The cabin overlooks a pond with a big gazebo, a dock, kayaks and a paddleboat. Zebras, donkeys, wildebeest, oryx and an ostrich wander up to the cabin and the house windows to be hand-fed. There is a fire pit and a saltwater hot tub. It is charming ranch-and-pond scenery rather than a big Hill Country panorama.
places.steps_to_enter: Cabin listing: "Both entrances to property have steps" (count not given), plus a narrow staircase to the loft. The B&B room listings have no stairs flag, and their entry steps are not stated.
places.access_detail: Cabin: "There is a carport next to the cabin for guests park in". Extra cars park up at the main house, a 'short distance' away. There is a downstairs ensuite master bedroom, so grandma would not need the loft stairs. But both cabin entrances have steps, and one bathroom serves everyone in the cabin. B&B rooms: a private attached bath (the Wild Safari room has a "Large on-suite bathroom"), homemade breakfast, and no stairs warning. For grandma, a B&B room may be the easier option. The ranch is 'a working ranch' with tractors, and the ostriches are 'curious'.
places.flood_note: The ranch is not riverfront. It sits on a pond near Real Ale Brewery, and Airbnb's summary puts it about a 5-minute walk from Blanco State Park, which is on the Blanco River. The listings mention no 2025 flood impact, and they are active and bookable for Nov and Dec 2026. Ask the host whether the ranch sits in the Blanco River floodplain.
highlights: Hand-feeding zebras and donkeys from the porch: a big hit with kids and grandma
Closest to San Antonio of the six, at about an hour
Cabin plus 3 B&B rooms lets about 14 people stay on one ranch
Pond, gazebo, saltwater hot tub, breakfast in the B&B rooms
Cabin rated 4.99/5 from 540 Airbnb reviews
places.red_flags: The cabin has only 1 bathroom for up to 8 people. There are steps at both cabin entrances and a narrow loft staircase. The B&B rooms are inside the hosts' home. The ostriches peck at cars. It is a working ranch with machinery. The cabin often books up, and it was unavailable Nov 6-8 and on the January and February dates I tried.
places.review_signal: Airbnb ratings: cabin 4.99/5 (540 reviews, 5.0 in every sub-score, Guest Favorite). Rooms: Wild Safari 4.99 (158), African Rainforest 5.0 (82), Peacock Forest 4.97 (75). The summary says guests return year after year and many call it a 'once-in-a-lifetime' experience. The hosts are superhosts. Individual reviews could not be pulled for access words.

places.name: Blue Dog River Ranch - RIVERFRONT Cabin on the Pedernales River
places.price_note: Prices come from Airbnb search results checked Sep 24, 2026, for 8 adults: $468.50/night on the weeknight of Nov 17-19, and $503.50/night on the weekends of Nov 6-8 and Dec 11-13. Airbnb shows fee-inclusive totals, and taxes may be extra. No minimum stay was visible. No pets are allowed, and the listing does not rent to work crews.
places.group_note: Whole log cabin with 4 bedrooms, 6 beds and 2 full baths, max 10 guests. The upstairs master has a queen, a futon and its own bath. Downstairs are a queen room, a full room and a bunk room (bunks max 150 lb), sharing 1 bath. There is parking for 4 cars. A small cottage on the same 6 acres is rented long-term, so it is not available to the family.
places.scenery_what: A renovated log cabin on 6 acres on the banks of the Pedernales, with a big oak in the front yard and a covered back patio. A short trail leads down to spring-fed swimming holes and small rapids. There are sunsets, deer at dusk and wildflowers. The upstairs bedroom 'overlooks the country'. The river is down a trail rather than in front of the door.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. The listing's 'Must climb stairs' flag refers to the upstairs bedroom: "There is one bedroom upstairs and one bathroom. 3 bedrooms downstairs and 1 bathroom down." Entry step count is unknown, so ask the host.
places.access_detail: Free parking on the property, 'parking for 4 cars', and a photo of the entrance to the driveway. There is AC and heat. Grandma could sleep downstairs (a queen room) and use the downstairs bath. That bath is a 'tub/shower' combo, so she would have to step over a tub edge. The river is reached by "a short trail down to the river", and the host warns of "snakes, cactus, or stickers". It is fine for the family, but grandma would stay up at the house and patio.
places.flood_note: The cabin is riverfront on the Pedernales, "on the banks" of the river, which the task brief lists among the rivers hit by the July 2025 Hill Country floods. The listing is active, still rated 4.97 and a Guest Favorite, with prices for Nov and Dec 2026. It says nothing about any flood damage or repairs. Ask the host about 2025 impacts and the flood/evacuation plan, and check forecasts before the trip.
highlights: Private river access with swimming holes, kayaking and fishing
Sleeps 10 in one house for about $470-505/night, the best per-head value
3 bedrooms and a bath on the ground floor
About 5 min to Johnson City and the start of the 290 Wine Trail
places.red_flags: Riverfront on a flood-prone river, and the listing is silent about 2025. The downstairs bath is a tub/shower combo. Entry steps are unknown. Rough country ground on the way to the river. The host's response rate is 88%.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.97/5 from 89 reviews, a Guest Favorite. Sub-scores are 5.0 for cleanliness, communication and location, and 4.9 for accuracy, check-in and value. The summary says guests highlight a spotless, well-stocked cabin and many return. The host is a superhost. Individual reviews could not be pulled for access words.

places.name: Postcard Cabins Hill Country (the former Getaway outpost, now part of Marriott)
places.town: Wimberley area (1405 Pump Station Rd, Wimberley; NOT Fredericksburg)
places.price_note: Rates were checked Sep 24, 2026 on Google Hotels, which shows the official Marriott rate. Weeknight (Thu Nov 19-20): 1-Queen or Accessible cabin $155 base from Marriott, 2-Queen Bunk about $179 (Expedia base). Weekend of Nov 6-8: 1-Queen or Accessible $259, 2-Queen Bunk $278. Weekend of Dec 11-13: $256 and $276. Dogs are a $50 cleaning fee per stay. Smoking inside is at least $150/night. There are no weather refunds unless a state of emergency is declared. A daily destination fee was noted at the brand level by the earlier finder, and I could not confirm the amount.
places.group_note: Tiny cabins with a queen bed or queen bunks. Marriott says each sleeps '1 to 4 guests depending on the layout', and the OTA lists the 2-Queen Bunk for 3 guests. Each cabin is booked separately. Marriott says guests "may request cabins to be near each other", but cabins "may be spread throughout" the outpost. The number of cabins is not published. There is a 'Book a Group of Cabins' option.
places.scenery_what: A small modern cabin on a wooded Hill Country lot with a large window to the trees. Outside is a private fire pit, a picnic table and Adirondack chairs. A reviewer says the cabins are 'nicely spaced out' with a walking trail. There are no pool or on-site amenities and no big vista. Jacob's Well and Blue Hole are 12-16 minutes away by car.
places.steps_to_enter: Not stated. Google, Expedia and Hotels.com sell an 'Accessible Cabin 1 Queen' room type, but Marriott's own cabins page showed 'No Accessible Rooms Available at this Hotel'. Confirm by phone at (888) 236-2427.
places.access_detail: From Marriott's Plan Your Stay page: "Each cabin includes a private parking space just steps from the door." Each cabin has AC and heat and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower, but "hot water may be limited to about 5 minutes at a time" in cold weather. On-site roads are gravel. Check-in is contactless by text, with no front desk. Google lists 'Accessible parking'. The cabins are compact, and Google's review topics show the bathroom mentioned unfavorably 45% of the time.
places.flood_note: Not riverfront per Marriott. It sits in the Blanco River country between Blanco and Wimberley. I found no report of 2025 flood impact, and the outpost is open with rates for Nov and Dec 2026.
highlights: Park right at the cabin, the easiest car-to-door access of the cabin options
Cheapest weeknights in the set (from about $155)
Book several cabins, and an accessible cabin type is sold on the OTAs
Closest of the six to Austin and San Marcos
places.red_flags: A recent Tripadvisor review (about 3 months old) says "Marriott took over and the entire places has gone bad" and complains of poor service and communication. Google review topics lean negative on the bathroom (45%) and the kitchen (50%). Cabins are tiny with small bathrooms, and hot water is limited in cold weather. One review warns the water is salty. Cabins for a group may be spread out. The accessible cabin is listed inconsistently. There are no staff on site and no dining.
places.review_signal: Google 4.3/5 (194 reviews). Guests like the peaceful setting, the trail, the spacing between cabins and the s'mores kits. Tripadvisor is 3.6/5 from only 5 reviews, including the recent complaint about the Marriott takeover. Bathroom and kitchen get the most negative mentions.

places.name: Casa Hacienda Agave (Airbnb)
places.town: Fredericksburg (2575 N Hwy 16, about 6 min from Main St)
places.price_note: Checked in Airbnb search with dates on 9/24/26 for 10 adults. The totals shown already include Airbnb fees but not taxes. Weeknights (Oct 20-22, Nov 10-12) were $1,015/night for 2 nights, marked down from $2,230. Weekends (Oct 16-18, Nov 6-8) were $1,109.50/night. The finder saw about $920/night averaged over 5 nights. Early check-in is $68/hour and late checkout $50/hour, if the calendar allows. The listing says 'You must be 21 years or older to rent this property', which reads as a rule for the person booking. No pets. The owner's site (haciendaagavefbg.com) sends bookings to Airbnb and also rents out an event venue.
places.group_note: One house with 5 bedrooms, 7 beds and 4 baths, for up to 14 guests. The host says to message them for 'more units available', and a June 2023 guest wrote that 'the apartments next to the house' held their group of 25, so there are extra rentable units on site. Past reviews are mostly big groups: a 50th anniversary, 9 adults with 5 toddlers, and bachelorettes.
places.scenery_what: A manicured front lawn with a stone fountain and horse sculptures. Behind it is a walled courtyard with a long pool, turf and loungers, with a wooded hill showing over the wall. The property fronts a highway, so there's no open Hill Country panorama. Reviews say 'right on the highway' and 'traffic noise; tolerable'. The listing calls the views 'stunning hill-country views', but the photos and reviews don't back that up.
places.access_detail: The listing mentions 'central AC', 'completely tiled, walk-in showers', 'Free parking on premises', and says each bedroom has 'a separate entrance onto the patio'. The interior photos show vaulted ceilings on one main level. The exterior has dormer windows, but I found no stairs mentioned and no Airbnb 'Must climb stairs' flag. I couldn't confirm how many steps are at the entry, whether the showers have grab bars, or how far the parking is from the door. None of the 120 reviews mention stairs, walking or mobility. Ask the host (Aide, Superhost, speaks English and Spanish) for the step count at the front door and the patio doors.
places.flood_note: The house is on TX-16 north of town, not beside a river. I found no flood exposure and no 2025 or 2026 flood impact.
sources: Airbnb reviews API for listing 809381898793046272 (120 reviews)
highlights: Everyone fits under one roof (14 beds), and more units next door can take a group of 25
Private fenced pool, walk-in tiled showers and central AC
2.8 miles from Main Street shopping and restaurants, so grandma has short rides
places.red_flags: It's a highway house: reviews mention traffic noise and a pool 'very close to the road', so it's not the 'step out to scenery' dream. It's the most expensive per night of these six (about $1,000+). The renter must be 21+. The entry step count isn't confirmed.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.94 from 120 reviews, with a Superhost who responds fast. Guests praise the pool, the space and having 4 baths. The complaints are highway and road noise (Dec 2023, May 2024, June 2023) and some tight bedrooms.

places.name: Walnut Canyon Cabins
places.town: Fredericksburg (503 Deer Rd, about 15 mi south of town near Old Tunnel State Park, toward Comfort)
places.price_note: The ResNexus booking engine on the official site blocked automated checks. I took prices from the property's own Airbnb listings with dates on 9/24/26. Those include Airbnb fees but not taxes. Oct 20-22 (weeknights): Siesta, Woods, Hideaway and Lookout were $212.50/night, Tree House $237.50 and Rocky Top $272.50. Nov 6-8 (weekend): $251.50, $271.50 and $322.50. Booking direct may cost less, so ask. Breakfast supplies are included (farm eggs, local Canadian bacon, coffee). Wi-Fi modem rental is $20 per stay. Pet fee applies in 5 cabins. The owners say you can rent the whole property for 'family reunions', but no price is published. Call +1 830-456-9326.
places.group_note: 7 separate cabins on 15 acres. Woods sleeps 2, Hideaway 3, Siesta 4, Lookout 4 (with a loft), Rocky Top 6 (2 bedrooms plus a loft queen), and Tree House, which is 2 stories. Milky Way's capacity isn't published. Rocky Top has the most room, but its third bed is in a loft. Group total is roughly 25-30.
places.scenery_what: The cabins sit on the rim of a canyon the owners call 500 ft deep, with private back decks looking up to 30-40 miles south and southeast. Deer feed right below (corn is provided), and there are foxes, turkeys and dark skies. Reviews say 'The view from our balcony was breathtaking' (Sept 2026) and 'magnificent views and wildlife' (May 2026). Some cabins sit close together: Tree House has 'two cabins very close'.
places.access_detail: It depends on the cabin. Woods: 'After parking, you wander down the graveled path to the cabin'. Its bath has a 'tiled shower combo', which means a tub edge to step over. Lookout: 'wander the pathway leading to the cabin tucked down among the tall trees'. Hideaway: 'assigned uncovered parking' and a 'covered deck off the back'. Milky Way: 'pull into the private driveway', which looks like the best drive-up candidate. Siesta's Airbnb page flags 'Must climb stairs' for its rooftop deck. Tree House: 'The stairs beckon'. Lofts in Hideaway, Lookout and Rocky Top are for 'a child or agile adult'. All cabins have a private bath, AC and heat. No review mentions steps or mobility either way. Before booking, call and ask which cabin has drive-up parking, a zero-step entry and a walk-in shower. Milky Way and Hideaway are the first to ask about.
places.flood_note: The cabins are on a canyon rim on high ground, not in a floodplain. I found no 2025 or 2026 flood impact, and reviews run through Sept 2026.
highlights: Real canyon-rim view of 30-40 miles from each cabin's deck, a good fit for 'step out and it's beautiful'
Deer feeding, big sunrises, dark-sky stargazing, and breakfast groceries included
You can rent all 7 cabins for a family reunion
Close to Old Tunnel State Park's bat flight and the Alamo Springs Cafe
places.red_flags: Several cabins involve a gravel path from parking to the door, lofts, or stairs (Tree House, Siesta roof deck), so pick the cabin carefully for grandma. Most cabins are small, sleeping 2-4 each. It's about 25-30 min from Fredericksburg over country roads. The whole-property price isn't published.
places.review_signal: All 25 reviews on the owners' site are 5 stars, the latest in Sept 2026. The 6 Airbnb listings score 4.94-5.0 across 72 reviews. Guests praise the views, the wildlife and hosts Carl and Rhonda. The only negatives are the drive to town and a shared hot tub at Tree House.

places.name: Garner State Park Cabins (book Cabin #18, the ADA cabin, for grandma plus neighboring cabins for the family)
places.price_note: The cabins without a fireplace, including #18, are $130/night, and the 13 cabins with a fireplace are $150/night. Tax is added. The rate covers 4 people, with a max of 6 at $10/night per extra person. Everyone 13 and older also pays the $8 daily park entrance fee; kids 12 and under are free. There's a 2-night minimum. A refundable cleaning deposit equal to one night ($130/$150) goes on a credit card at check-in. Cabins close for maintenance on the first Tuesday of each month, except June through August. Book through Texas State Parks reservations (texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com, park rating 4.5 from 2,149 ratings). I didn't check live cabin availability.
places.group_note: 17 cabins: 4 without a fireplace (including ADA #18) and 13 with one. Each has 2 double beds and sleeps 4 (6 with the surcharge). They're grouped in the Oakmont section of Old Garner, so a family can book #18 plus the cabins around it. No tents or RVs are allowed at the cabins, and no pets.
places.scenery_what: Single-story cabins spread across flat, grassy oak and pecan groves in the Old Garner (Oakmont) area, with picnic tables and fire rings under big live oaks. TPWD says both park sections are 'along the Frio River', and the swimming dam, dance pavilion and store are nearby in Old Garner. From the porch you see shade trees and lawn rather than a river or canyon view. The river and hills are a short walk or drive away.
places.access_detail: TPWD says: 'Cabin 18 in the Oakmont camping area is ADA compliant with a sidewalk leading from the parking space to the cabin.' The cabins page says 'Cabin #18 is equipped for special physical needs in the bathroom, doorways, and the entrance from driveway.' Every cabin has a private bathroom with sink, toilet and shower, 'Central air-conditioning and heating', a kitchen sink, a microwave, a fridge and a stove with no oven. The TPWD photos show low single-story cabins on level ground. There are no linens, blankets, towels, utensils or dishes, so bring all of it. Whether #18 has a roll-in shower or grab bars isn't specified, so call the park to confirm.
places.flood_note: Old Garner sits along the Frio River corridor. The cabins are in the oak grove back from the water, but I couldn't confirm whether they're in the floodplain. Current TPWD alerts: a burn ban since Sept 17, 2026 (no wood fires), a July 21, 2026 river advisory closing the Blinn River and White Rock Cave trails, and suspended construction at the Scenic Overlook. A nearby Airbnb guest mentioned 'recent flood closures' of roads in July 2026. No cabin closures are listed, and I found no 2025 flood damage notice on TPWD pages.
highlights: The most accessible pick for grandma: an official ADA cabin with a sidewalk from its own parking space, ADA bathroom and doorways, and central AC
Cheapest option at $130-150/night, so several cabins side by side for the family stay affordable
Classic Frio River park with the swimming dam, summer jukebox dance at the pavilion, mini-golf and paddleboats (seasonal)
places.red_flags: Bring everything: no linens, towels, dishes or utensils, and no oven. The porch view is shade trees, not a vista. The park gets crowded and books up (it recommends reserving even day use), and there are feral hogs. There's a burn ban as of Sept 2026 and a river advisory from July 2026. It's about 1h50 from SA and over 3 hours from Austin.
places.review_signal: 4.5 from 2,149 ratings on ReserveAmerica and 4.5 from 36 reviews on The Dyrt (park-wide). Campers mention a 'beautiful' river and 'totally fine' bathrooms. I found no cabin-specific complaints, but there are few cabin-specific reviews to go on.

places.name: Camp Riverview: ADA River Facing 2BR Cabin
places.town: Concan (1636 County Road 350, next to Garner State Park)
places.price_note: Official booking engine (booking.staylist.app/campriverview), checked 9/24/26 with 4 adults. The '2 Bedroom River Facing Cabin - Accessible' is $149/night for Oct 20-22, Oct 23-25 and Dec 31-Jan 2, and $169/night for Mar 12-14, 2027. It wasn't available Nov 6-8 or Nov 25-28. On Airbnb the same cabin is $186.50/night including fees (listing 1115230762218295536). Guests 5 and older beyond the base pay $8/night each, and extra vehicles are $5/night. Minimum stay is 2 nights in fall, winter and spring, 3 in summer, and 4 over July 4th. Refunds: cancel 31+ days out and you lose $125; 30-7 days out you lose the deposit; under 7 days you pay the full stay. No refunds for weather. Bring your own linens and towels. Summer rate not shown.
places.group_note: There's only 1 accessible cabin (2 queens plus a futon, sleeps 6). The listing says it's 'near to our other river facing two bedroom cabins'. Nearby options: 2 more River Facing 2BR cabins ($149), 1 River Facing 1BR ($132), 2 Small 2BR River Facing ($129), 4 studios ($119) and 13 Mountain View 2BR cabins ($139). That's enough for a family cluster of about 18-24 in river-facing cabins. There's also a group RV and tent site for reunions.
places.scenery_what: A small updated cabin with a railed front deck under oaks in a family campground with half a mile of Frio River frontage. The name says river-facing, but the listing photos show trees and grass in front and don't clearly show the water from the deck. The river bank, shady sitting spots and the camp's waterfall are a short stroll away.
places.access_detail: The official Staylist listing says 'ramped entry into the cabin' and is tagged 'Handicap Accessible'. Airbnb says it 'offers, a ramp and larger doorways for accessibility', with 'Free parking on premises' and air conditioning. The official cabins page says the river-facing cabins are 'air-conditioned and heated' with 'a private bathroom with a tile shower'. It has a cooktop but no oven. Two things aren't confirmed: whether the shower is roll-in or step-in, whether it has grab bars, and exactly where the car parks relative to the ramp. Airbnb also lists 'Heights without rails or protection' as a property safety note, probably the river bank. Call (830) 232-5412 about these.
places.flood_note: The river-facing cabins sit near the Frio River bank, so assume they're in the floodplain. A July 2026 Airbnb review of a nearby Frio cabin mentions 'recent flood closures' of roads, and Garner posted a river advisory on July 21, 2026. I found no 2025 flood damage notice. The camp is operating and taking bookings, with Airbnb reviews from Mar, May and Jun 2026.
highlights: A true ramp-access cabin for grandma, right on a Frio River campground about 5 minutes from Garner
Cheap: $149/night off-season for a 2BR that sleeps 6
Several river-facing cabins side by side for the rest of the family
Float and tube access, a waterfall, a camp store and a playground
places.red_flags: It's a busy family RV and tent campground: wristbands, strict quiet hours 10:30pm-8am, and one adult 21+ must be at the cabin. Bring your own linens and towels, and there's no oven. Refunds are nearly impossible. This specific cabin has only 4 reviews. Floodplain setting. The old URL riverviewcamp.com is an unrelated Alabama girls' camp; the real site is friocampriverview.com.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 5.0 from 4 reviews (Apr 2024 to Jun 2026). One guest said the cabin was a 'Perfect distance from the river'; repeat guests say 'it just continues to get better every year'. The host, Melissa, is a Superhost with 275 reviews averaging 4.72.

places.name: Frio River Cabins: River Terrace Cabins (4 units) and River Terrace House
places.town: Leakey / Concan area (6978 S Hwy 83; office 1.5 mi north of Garner State Park)
places.price_note: River Terrace Cabins, per the official site: $125/night for 2 guests from Oct to early March, $160 for late March-May and late Aug-Sept, and $240 for 6 in peak season (Memorial Day to early Aug). Each extra guest is $15/night, up to 6. Holidays run $240-290 with a 3-4 night minimum, and peak season has a 4-night minimum. River Terrace House: $245 for 6 guests off-season, $275 regular, $550 for 10 at peak, and $600 for Memorial Day, Labor Day and July 4th. Its extra-guest fee is $15 normally and $30 on holidays. The live booking system (Checkfront), checked 9/24/26: cabins at $125 and the house at $245 were open Oct 20-22, Nov 6-8, Nov 10-12 and Dec 12-14. All of them were sold out Oct 23-25. 2-night minimum off-season. Linens cost extra and aren't offered in peak season. Only 2 vehicles per cabin and 3 per house; extra cars $5/day. The cancellation policy is strict. Taxes and fees aren't itemized online.
places.group_note: 4 River Terrace cabins sit side by side in one clearing. Each is 1 bedroom and 1 bath, sleeps 6 (a queen and 2 twins in the bedroom, a real queen in the living room), and has a full kitchen. River Terrace House (3 bedrooms, 2 baths, sunroom, sleeps 10) is on the same river frontage. Booking all 5 fits about 34 people. The same operator's Original Cabins 1-6 ($145-295) and Shady Oaks house (sleeps 13) are nearby.
places.scenery_what: Small log and clapboard cabins under century-old oaks, each with a porch, picnic table, fire ring and hummingbird feeders. They sit on a terrace above a clear green swimming hole that the operator says Texas Monthly named 'Best Swimming Hole in Texas'. From the cabin doors you mostly see oaks and the gravel clearing; the river is a short mulch-trail walk away. The House's sunroom has picture windows that the site says look out to the swimming hole. Guests mention truck noise from US-83.
places.access_detail: Official site: 'All cabins and houses have air conditioning and heat', 'Only two vehicles are permitted to park at each cabin', and 'Our roads and parking have loose gravel'. The office lists a 'Shower Chair' among items available to guests. Photos show a gravel parking area next to low single-story cabins with a single step or stepping stones at the door. The House has 'Central heating and air conditioning' and 2 full baths. Reviews say 'the walk to the river is super short' (Apr 2026) and 'Easy to access' (Aug 2026). But a 2021 review said you 'have to climb down ladder for river access', and two 2021 reviews called the cabin wall AC loud. Grandma can get car to porch, but the river bank itself probably isn't reachable for her. Call (830) 232-5996 and ask which cabin has the fewest steps and whether the bath is a tub or a walk-in shower.
places.flood_note: The cabins sit right on the Frio River frontage, 'sitting above' the swimming hole on a terrace, so assume floodplain risk. A July 2026 guest review mentions 'recent flood closures' that blocked roads and highways. The property stayed open, and reviews from Aug-Sept 2026 are normal. I found no notice of 2025 flood damage, and the booking calendar is live for fall 2026.
highlights: The best budget family cluster: 4 identical riverfront cabins side by side plus a 10-person house, from $125/night
A famous clear swimming hole a short stroll from the porches, with tubing that ends at the property and shuttles available
Hummingbirds, deer and fireflies. A shower chair is available from the office
5 minutes from Garner State Park
places.red_flags: Paths and parking are loose gravel, and the riverbank reportedly needs a ladder. Bring your own linens (a paid add-on off-season, not offered at all in summer). There's highway truck noise and strict no-refund language. Fall weekends are already selling out (Oct 23-25 sold out). The site says 'about 90 miles west of San Antonio'; that's about 1h50 by car, not the 'one hour' the homepage claims.
places.review_signal: River Terrace Cabin 1 on Airbnb: 4.91 from 65 reviews through Sept 2026. Recurring praise for manager Veronica, the clear water and the 'super short' walk to the river. Complaints: loud wall AC (2021), a ladder down to the river (2021), highway truck noise (2026). The operator's site shows 5/5 testimonials, including one from a family with a grandson.

places.name: Frio River Cabins: Step Ladder Ranch Lodge / Buffalo Creek House (splurge tier)
places.town: Leakey / Concan area (Step Ladder: TX-337 about 3 mi from Leakey; Buffalo Creek: about 3 mi from Garner, 6 mi from Leakey)
places.price_note: Buffalo Creek House, per the official page: $355/night for 6 guests Oct to early March, or $425 on Fri and Sat nights. Late Aug-Sept is $495, or $550 on weekends. Peak (Memorial Day to early Aug) is $800 for 12, and Memorial Day, Labor Day and July 4th are $1,000. Extra guests are $30/night, up to 16. Linens cost extra and aren't offered in summer. Step Ladder Ranch Lodge: $395 for 4 guests Oct to early March. The detail page says $495 regular season, but the summary page says $425. Peak is $800 for 6, holidays up to $1,000, and extra guests are $30/night up to 12. It has a $500 refundable deposit (3.5% fee if paid by card), a $20 per pet per night fee, and luxury linens included year-round. Live Checkfront on 9/24/26: Buffalo Creek was $355 and open Oct 20-22 and Nov 10-12, but sold out Oct 23-25, Nov 6-8 and Dec 12-14. Step Ladder was $395, sold out Oct 20-22, Oct 23-25 and Nov 6-8, and open Nov 10-12 and Dec 12-14. 2-night minimum off-season, 4 in peak.
places.group_note: Each is a whole house for the whole family. Buffalo Creek House has 6 bedrooms, 4 full baths, a bunk room, 2 living rooms, a sunroom, a game room and three large patios, and sleeps 16. Step Ladder Ranch Lodge has 4 bedrooms and 3 full baths, sleeps 12, and comes with a game room, kayaks and canoes. The two are about 10 miles apart, so they don't work as a side-by-side pair. For more than 16 people, add River Terrace cabins.
places.scenery_what: Step Ladder: a mid-century ranch house on a rise above half a mile of private Little Frio Creek on a 100-130 acre ranch. A big flagstone patio and covered back porch look straight down on clear water lined with cypress and oak, with hills behind, and the master bedroom has a picture window facing the creek. Blackbuck, axis deer and turkey roam the ranch. This is a genuine step-out view (8). Buffalo Creek: a white stone farmhouse on a 75-95 acre ranch with three big patios looking out over Hill Country ridges and a seasonal creek close by. The Frio River frontage is a 3-minute drive or 25-minute trail walk away. Wide hill view but no water at the door (about 7).
places.access_detail: Both houses have AC and heat ('All cabins and houses have air conditioning and heat'; Buffalo Creek lists 'Central heating and air conditioning'). Neither page gives step counts, bedroom levels or driveway surface, and the operator notes 'Our roads and parking have loose gravel'. From photos, Buffalo Creek looks mostly single-level with a wide front porch near ground level, and its master bath has a 'separate oversize shower'. It has a dormer, so some space may be upstairs. Step Ladder is visibly two stories on a rise, with stone-terraced steps down to the creek. Its master bath has 'a tub and separate shower' and the master appears to be on the main floor facing the creek, but that isn't confirmed. The office lists a shower chair among items available to guests. Call (830) 232-5996 and ask which bedroom and bath is on the entry level, the steps from the parking spot, and the shower type. For grandma, Buffalo Creek is probably the easier house.
places.flood_note: The Step Ladder house sits 'nestled above' Little Frio Creek, elevated above the water, and the creek is described as flowing year-round. At Buffalo Creek the house is away from the river (3 minutes by car), near a seasonal creek. Neither house is on the Frio bank. July 2026 regional flooding closed roads, per a guest review at the same operator's River Terrace cabin. I found no 2025 flood damage notice, and both houses are bookable for fall 2026.
highlights: Step Ladder: a private creek-overlook patio and porch, luxury linens included, kayaks, and total seclusion near Leakey
Buffalo Creek: the whole extended family (up to 16) in one house, with 4 full baths, three hill-view patios and a game room
Off-season weeknights from $355 (Buffalo Creek) or $395 (Step Ladder), about a third of Casa Hacienda Agave's price for similar headcount
places.red_flags: Access for grandma isn't published, and Step Ladder is two stories on a slope with stone steps. Buffalo Creek's river is a drive away. Roads are gravel and cell service in the canyon is spotty. The $30/night extra-guest fee adds up (Buffalo Creek at 12 guests off-season is about $535 on weeknights). Several fall weekends are already sold out. The only reviews I found are testimonials on the owner's site; I couldn't check third-party reviews.
places.review_signal: The operator's pages show 5/5 testimonials. One Buffalo Creek family 'took my father for his birthday'; Step Ladder guests call it 'beautiful' and praise manager Veronica. I found no third-party review pages for these two houses in this pass. The same operator's River Terrace Cabin 1 has 4.91 from 65 Airbnb reviews.

places.name: Utopia River Retreat (formerly Utopia on the River)
places.price_note: Nightly rates are NOT published: every cabin page shows 'STARTING AT $___' with the number filled in by the ResNexus booking engine, and that engine returned a bot-block page to every check I made, so the price is unknown. Call 830-966-2444 for a quote. Policies: 35% deposit, paid in full 14 days out, full refund only if you cancel more than 30 days out. Minimums: cabins 1 night on weeknights, 2 on weekends, 3 on holidays. The Fortress needs 2 nights (3 on holidays). Extra guests and children over 5 cost more per night. Pets are $15 per pet per night. GROUP WARNING: if the group books 5 or more cabins, the rooms are non-refundable no matter when you cancel. The off-site River Park Lodge adds a $110 cleaning fee.
places.group_note: There are 9 cabins on the 22-acre estate: six 1-bedroom cabins sleeping 2-3, and three 2-bedroom cabins (Look Out, Hide Out, Robber's Roost) sleeping 4-5. The Fortress is a historic stone house that sleeps 12 (2 master suites plus 3 lofts upstairs). There is also a community pool, a gazebo and a barn event center. A family can spread across several cabins together, but booking 5 or more makes the stay non-refundable.
places.scenery_what: Cabins sit along the Sabinal River under very old cypress and live oaks. Look Out's back porch overlooks the river from a small ledge (the official photo shows the river through the trees). Tomahawk sits on a bluff above the river, Comanche faces it, and Kickapoo is closest to the water. The Hitching Post looks over a field. Other cabins are in sight, so it's not a no-neighbors panorama.
places.access_detail: Best pick for grandma is the Little River House, the only unit the site calls accessible: 'covered porch that is handicap accessible'. Its bathroom type isn't stated, and the photos show ducted central air vents. Kickapoo has an 'over sized tile walk in shower' (the photo shows a glass-door stall), but it's reached by about 5 wooden deck steps with a handrail. Comanche also has a walk-in shower. The Look Out photo shows a paved driveway right up to the cabin, and Look Out and Kickapoo have through-wall AC units (so 'at door' is confirmed only for Look Out). No cabin page says whether it has heat, though Look Out has a fireplace. The ADA page is generic ('contact us'). Call 830-966-2444 about steps at each cabin.
places.steps_to_enter: Varies by cabin. Little River House: handicap-accessible covered porch (per the site). Kickapoo: about 5 deck steps with a rail (official photo). Look Out: drive-up, step count unknown. Fortress: sleeping lofts are upstairs.
places.flood_note: This is riverside property on the Sabinal River, with several cabins at or near river level (Kickapoo is 'closest to the river'). The official site has no notice of 2025 flood damage or closure, and I couldn't confirm any 2025 impact on this stretch of the Sabinal. Ask about flood history and choose a bluff-top cabin like Tomahawk or Look Out.
places.review_signal: The site quotes short guest reviews from Facebook and Tripadvisor ('happiest place on earth'). Tripadvisor and Facebook review pages exist but blocked automated reading, so I found no independent read on access. Current owners bought the property in 2019. The old utopiaontheriver.com domain 301-redirects here.
highlights: Sabinal River frontage with cypress trees, 22 acres
Little River House has a handicap-accessible porch
Walk-in showers in Kickapoo and Comanche
9 cabins plus a 12-person Fortress for the whole family
Pool and event barn on site
places.red_flags: Price is not published, and online booking wouldn't load for me. Booking 5 or more cabins is non-refundable. No refund inside 14 days. Only one unit is described as accessible. The Fortress sleeping lofts are upstairs.

places.name: Neal's Lodges
places.price_note: Rates are not on the website. The WebRez booking engine loads prices only after a human-verification step, so the price is unknown. Call (830) 232-6118. Known fees and policies: 33% deposit, and final payment is charged 7 days before arrival. Canceling more than 30 days out refunds the deposit minus 20%; inside 30 days you lose the deposit; inside 7 days you pay in full. No refunds for weather. Extra people are $25 per person per night, and pets are $35 per pet per stay. One-night stays are by phone only. Minimum renter age is 21. Golf carts rent for $95 per 24 hours, but only Memorial Day through Labor Day.
places.group_note: There are 81 cabins, 10 lodges and 17 condos. Cabins sleep 4-16: for example, riverfront Cabin 21 sleeps 8, Cabins 27 and 28 sleep 4, and Buchanan Cottage sleeps 16. The lodges on Neal Ranch, about 1.5 miles from the river, sleep 12-22 and some have pools (Casa Santiago sleeps 22, Outback 21, Buckhorn 18). A family can easily book a cluster of cabins together.
places.scenery_what: This is a classic busy family river camp on the Frio. Riverfront Cabins 21 and 22 advertise the 'beauty of the Frio River right from the deck', and 27 and 28 are 'right on the Frio River'. Most other cabins look out on shady camp grounds and roads. The Outback lodge, 1.5 miles away, advertises '360 degree hill country views' from its pool and patio.
places.access_detail: Every cabin is 'furnished with: A/C', a kitchen and its own bathroom (1-3 baths). The site doesn't mention heat.
