It says nothing about parking at each unit, steps, ramps or ADA units. The tube page says guests 'walk up the hill' from the river. Golf carts rent only 'Memorial Day-Labor Day', and only for cabins on the store side of the river, so there's no rental cart for a fall trip. You can bring your own cart on the main property. You must bring your own sheets and towels (rentals $5 each). Call and ask for a ground-level cabin you can drive up to.
places.steps_to_enter: unknown (not listed for any cabin)
places.flood_note: The main camp is on the Frio River, with riverfront cabins at the swimming hole. The site has no 2025 flood or closure notice. It's operating normally and lists a Centennial Celebration Oct 9-11, 2026. I couldn't confirm any 2025 impact at Concan.
places.review_signal: Tripadvisor and Yelp blocked automated reading, so I found no review evidence about access. It's a long-running resort (since 1926) with big peak-season crowds.
highlights: Spring-fed swimming hole and 83-ft water slide (peak season)
Huge inventory: 81 cabins, 10 lodges, 17 condos
Riverfront cabins 21, 22, 27, 28 with Frio deck views
Neal's Dining Room on site
places.red_flags: You have to bring your own linens and towels. No golf cart rental outside summer. Price is not published. Strict cancellation rules with no weather refunds. Joe Jimmy's dance hall runs most summer nights. The Oct 9-11, 2026 Centennial weekend will be crowded.

places.name: River's Edge Cabin #3 at Oasis Resort
places.price_note: The official Frio River Escape rate table lists River's Edge Cabin 3 at $260-$430 per night. Rates vary by season, weekday and holiday. Fall is off-peak ('October-December'). There is a set cleaning fee per stay (amount not shown). Minimum stay is 2 nights off-season and 3 in peak season. 25% deposit, and canceling 30+ days out refunds the deposit minus a $100 fee. Dogs are $100 per stay. Airbnb adds its own service fee, so booking direct at 830-232-4600 may be cheaper. Nearby units: Oasis Cabins $200-$325, River's Edge Lodges 2-3 $460-$850.
places.group_note: Oasis Resort has 20 units run by the same manager: River's Edge Cabins 1-4 (sleep 8 each, side by side on the river edge), River's Edge Home 1-2 (sleep 10-14), River's Edge Lodges 1-3 (sleep 14-18), plus Oasis Cabins, Homes and Lodges. Their FAQ says groups can reserve several nearby rentals. Grandma plus 7 fit in Cabin 3, and the rest of the family can take Cabin 2 or 4 next door.
places.scenery_what: A large covered porch sits on the bluff edge directly above the Frio: green water, cypress and big live oaks below, with views of Mt. Baldy. The manager calls Cabins 2-4 'the best river views of any of our rentals'. Other resort cabins sit right next door, so it's a view, not seclusion.
places.access_detail: Airbnb amenities list 'Single level home - No stairs in home' and 'Free parking on premises'. The official page lists 'Central A/C' and 'Air Conditioning / Heating'. Bedroom 1 (king) has 'private en-suite bathroom' with a 'Master Bathroom - Stand up shower' (photo label). The bunk room has its own full bath (it also has a bathtub). The listing photo shows a concrete walkway on the street side leading to the entry, which looks at or near ground level. Rules say 'Parking is limited ... Park on driveways only.' Exact parking distance isn't stated, so confirm the driveway is next to Cabin 3. The river itself is reached by 'Private river access stairs', so grandma should enjoy it from the porch.
places.steps_to_enter: Looks like 0-1 step: a concrete walk to the street-side door (photo). Single level inside with no stairs. Stairs go down to the riverbank.
places.flood_note: Riverfront on the Frio at Mager's Crossing. The cabins sit on a raised bluff with stairs down to the bank (photo), but they're still on the river. The listing and site show no 2025 flood damage or closure notice, and the resort is taking 2026 bookings. I couldn't confirm any 2025 impact at this spot.
places.review_signal: Airbnb: 5.0 stars from 18 reviews (all 5-star; location and value both 5.0). The manager claims '650+ positive reviews' across its rentals. I couldn't read individual review text.
highlights: Covered porch hanging over the Frio with Mt. Baldy views
Single level, stand-up shower in an en-suite bath, central AC and heat
4 matching River's Edge cabins side by side for a family
Two resort pools, private riverbank, short walk to Mager's Crossing
places.red_flags: Parking is limited and on driveways only; distance to the door isn't confirmed. The river is only reachable by stairs. It's a 20-unit resort, so expect neighbors. Cell service is spotty. The cleaning fee amount isn't shown. Only 18 reviews on this particular listing.

skeptic.name: River's Edge Cabin #3 at Oasis Resort
skeptic.evidence: The manager's official page (frioriverescape.com, AAA Frio Property Management) confirms 'Central A/C', 'Air Conditioning / Heating' and 'Bedroom 1: King-size bed with private en-suite bathroom'. It also says Cabins 2-4 have 'The best river views of any of our rentals' and a 'Large covered front porch with sweeping river views'. Airbnb lists 'Single level home - No stairs in home'. The 'Rivers Edge Cabin #3' photo shows a flat concrete walkway to a side door at grade, so 0-1 step holds. The master shower photo shows a fiberglass stall with a low curb and a built-in seat, not a tub. The bunk bath has a tub. The official site plan puts Cabin 3 on the drive loop behind the River's Edge pool, but the exact parking distance is not stated. The FAQ says 'Parking is limited... park in designated areas only.' The river is reached by stairs (captions: 'Private river access stairs', 'Steps down to the private river bank area'). The porch photo confirms a green-water Frio view through live oaks. Caveats: it sits next to public Magers Crossing and campgrounds, and the listing says 'Many guests camp or stay in tents', so summer is busy. Some Airbnb reviews on this listing mention other cabins, so the review pool may be shared. Price was understated. Airbnb all-fees-included quotes were $352.67/night for Jan 11-14, $379.50 Jan 15-17, $385.50 Dec 6-8, $419.50 on Nov 6-8, Nov 13-15 and Dec 11-13, and $465.50 Apr 9-11. Easter and spring break are priced separately, with 2-3 night minimums. The calendar has wide availability Nov 2026 to May 2027. Reviews from Nov 2025, Dec 2025, Mar 2026 and Jul 2026 show it operating after the July 2025 floods.
sources: Airbnb StaysPdpBookItQuery and PdpAvailabilityCalendar API responses for listing 1147335959647656156 (queried 2026-09-24)

places.name: FoxFire Cabins
places.price_note: From the live 2026 availability calendar. Log cabins: $105 on fall weeknights, $125-$140 on early-October weekends, and $140-$160 from late October through November (fall color peak). Main House: $185-$260 (listed at $220 on Oct 2-4 and $260 from Oct 30 onward). Base rates cover 2 people in a cabin (+$10 per extra person, up to 6) and 4 in the Main House (+$25 per extra person, up to 10). Children 12 and under stay free. No cleaning or service fees. 2-night minimum on weekends and longer in peak. Deposit is 1 night, with $50-$200 of it non-refundable. The fall peak ('Mid October through November') is filling up: the Main House already shows many late-October and November dates as unavailable.
places.group_note: 7 identical 2-bedroom, 1-bath log cabins (sleep 6) plus the Main House (3 bedrooms, 2 baths, sleeps 10) share the same 5 acres, with a central pavilion, laundry and playground. The site says families and reunions book the Main House plus several or all of the cabins. Off-site homes are also available: Woodland House sleeps 10, and Hacienda del Sol sleeps 8 with a big hill-view deck but no river.
places.scenery_what: Shady live-oak grounds with hills in view. The spring-fed Sabinal River swimming hole with cypress trees and a limestone bluff is a short walk away. The Main House sits on the riverbank, with 'a view of the swimming hole and Sabinal River' from the living room and front porch. Lost Maples State Natural Area (fall maple color) is 1 mile north. Dark skies and fireflies, and no cell service.
places.access_detail: The property map shows gravel lanes running to every cabin, so you can drive up. The Brave Eagle photo shows a low stone porch about 1-2 steps up, with no rail visible. Log cabins have 'heat and cool window units', but the bathrooms 'have a shower/tub combination', so grandma would have to step over a tub edge. The Main House is the better grandma unit: the master bath 'has a shower only', floors are tile, and there's a fenced yard and a covered porch facing the river (step count not stated). The nearest hospital (Kerrville) is about an hour away. Ask for the Main House or the flattest cabin: (830) 966-2200.
places.steps_to_enter: Log cabins: low stone porch, about 1-2 steps, no rail seen in the photo. Main House: unknown.
places.flood_note: The property borders the Sabinal River, and the Main House is 'on the bank of the Sabinal River'. There's no 2025 flood or closure notice. The live calendar shows normal bookings through November 2026. I couldn't confirm any 2025 impact.
places.review_signal: Airbnb listing for a log cabin: 4.94 stars from 155 reviews (location 5.0). Testimonials run from 2023-2025, and the family has owned and run it for 40+ years.
highlights: Cheapest real-cabin option: $105 on fall weeknights with no cleaning fee
7 cabins plus a 10-person Main House on one property
Private spring-fed Sabinal swimming hole
1 mile from Lost Maples fall color
places.red_flags: The log cabins have tub/shower combos, not walk-in showers. No cell service. No TVs and no microwaves in the cabins. Late-October and November peak dates book up. It's about an hour to a hospital. ATVs and golf carts are not allowed.

places.name: A Peace Of Heaven Cabins and RV Park
places.price_note: Hipcamp list prices: log cabins (Cabin One, Two and Three) $185 per night for a base of 4 guests (max 7), plus a $75 cleaning fee and Hipcamp's service fee. Glamping tents (1-3) are $135 per night plus a $50 cleaning fee. RV sites are $40-$45. The minimum stay shown is 1 night. Weekend and holiday pricing isn't shown without dates.
places.group_note: There are 3 log cabins (2 bedrooms plus a daybed, sleep up to 7 each), 3 glamping tents for 2 each, and 3 RV sites on 10 acres. A family could take the whole place: grandma and most of the family in the cabins, and younger people in the tents.
places.scenery_what: A quiet hilltop property with creek and spring access. Photos show a big limestone-faced hill across from the entrance and open meadow and cedar grounds. Reviewers mention 'amazing' views, a 'hidden camp up on the hill', a 'decent view of the gorgeous stars', and a 'cute little bridge down to the creek'. What you see from each cabin door isn't documented.
places.access_detail: Cabins: 'All cabins have AC and Heat', with a full kitchen and one full bathroom with a shower (shower type not stated). Linens and towels are supplied. The listing gives no parking-to-cabin distance, step count, ramp or accessibility information. One RV review mentions 'little steps down to a charming creek'. The tents are NOT for grandma: they have a 'Chemical Toilet' and a 'Solar Shower'. I found no official website to check further, so message the host on Hipcamp before booking.
places.steps_to_enter: unknown
places.flood_note: The property has springs and creek access, but reviewers describe the camp as 'up on the hill'. I found no 2025 flood notice, and recent reviews (March 2026) show it operating. I couldn't confirm any 2025 impact.
places.review_signal: Hipcamp: 100% recommend, 11 ratings and 9 reviews. The most recent is from March 2026 ('cabin was immaculate', family-friendly). Everything is positive, but the sample is small.
highlights: True glamping tents with wood stoves for the younger crowd
Log cabins with AC and heat plus a private bath for grandma, all on one property
Dark skies, and 15 minutes to Lost Maples
Could rent the whole 10 acres
places.red_flags: Only 9 reviews. No details on parking or steps at the cabins. The tents have only a chemical toilet and a solar shower. No official site found. Cleaning and Hipcamp fees add roughly $80-$110 per stay on top.

places.name: Seco Ridge Campgrounds: The BunkHaus (shipping container)
places.price_note: Hipcamp list price for The BunkHaus is $100 per night with a 2-night minimum. No cleaning fee, and a Hipcamp service fee of about $17 per night, for about $123 per night total. Tent and RV sites are $40 per night; the Ridge Site (canvas cargo tent, no bed) is $61 with a 2-night minimum. Weekend and holiday variation isn't shown without dates.
places.group_note: There is only ONE air-conditioned unit, The BunkHaus (queen bed plus a bunk bed plus a cot, sleeps 4-5). The rest of the 42 acres is 8 tent/RV sites (up to 8 people each), the Ridge Site and a communal kitchen. A family could take over the property, but it's tent camping for everyone except the BunkHaus.
places.scenery_what: A private hill country ridge. Site 7 has a trail to an 'epic sunset view', and Site 6 has a 'wide open mountain view' for sunrises. It's named one of Hipcamp's best dark-sky sites. The BunkHaus itself sits by the common area, the outdoor kitchen and the owner's homebrew house, so the view from its door is not the ridge panorama.
places.access_detail: The BunkHaus has 'electricity and A/C' (heat not stated) and linens. Bathrooms are shared: guests use 'The Shower Haus (flushing toilets, sinks, and hot showers)'. The BunkHaus is 'Ideally located close to the bathrooms', and a reviewer says the restrooms 'not a far walk'. Most sites allow parking at the site, but 'Site 5 is hike in only'. Parking distance and the step into the container aren't stated. Not suitable as grandma's bed without a private bathroom.
places.steps_to_enter: unknown
places.flood_note: Ridge-top property with no river on site, so flood exposure is low. I found no 2025 flood notice, and reviews continue through September 2026.
places.review_signal: Hipcamp: 99% recommend, 1,293 ratings and 644 reviews. Recent reviews (Sept 2026) praise the clean bathhouse, privacy and stars. One April 2026 review complains about the owner's off-leash dogs and slow replies.
highlights: Cheapest AC bed in the set: $100 per night
Best dark-sky Hipcamp, with sunset and sunrise view sites
Very well reviewed, with a communal kitchen and hot showers
Between Garner and Lost Maples
places.red_flags: Shared bathhouse only, so it's a weak fit for grandma. Only one unit has AC; everyone else is tent camping. 2-night minimum. The owner's dogs roam (per 1 review).

places.name: Shadow Dance Ranch: 2000 Acre Private Ranch w/Lakes & 3/2 Guest House
places.kind: Airbnb/VRBO house (guest house on a working cattle ranch)
places.price_note: Airbnb shows all-in totals before taxes. For Oct 20 2026 to Jan 2027 dates the total was $868 for 2 nights ($434/night average, marked down from $954) and $1,273 for 3 nights (marked down from $1,402). That works out to about $405/night after the current discount, or about $448 undiscounted, plus roughly $58 for cleaning and fees. Weeknights and weekends cost the same. No listing came back for Oct 9-11, Oct 13-15, Oct 23-25 or Nov 6-8, so those dates are probably booked or blocked. No minimum stay is stated. You can't book the whole ranch: the main house and ranch manager's house are private.
places.group_note: One 3-bedroom, 2-bath guest house (4 beds) for up to 6. Only this one unit can be rented. The main house and the ranch manager's house are private, so only a small group fits.
places.scenery_what: A porch and patio on a rise looking over open ranch pasture and rugged hills. Reviewers mention watching the 'sun set over the hills', seeing deer, cattle and horses from the porch, and dark skies for stargazing. The spring-fed lakes and Hondo Creek are a short walk or drive across the ranch, not right at the door. The owner's and manager's houses are along the entry road.
places.access_detail: Airbnb lists 'Single level home', 'Central air conditioning', 'Free parking on premises' and 'Private backyard – Fully fenced'. The host says the ranch is reached 'via paved roads'. A 2020 review says the guest house 'sits on a hill away from the main road' down a 'long private drive/road', and a 2021 review warns off low-clearance cars. The master bedroom has an en-suite bath (2020 review). The listing doesn't say how many steps there are to the door or how far parking is from it. A July 2020 review says the AC 'has a hard time keeping up' on 100-degree afternoons (78-79F inside) but cooled to 70 at night.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The home is single level, but the entry step count isn't stated, so ask host Brian.
places.flood_note: The ranch includes 3 miles of Hondo Creek and spring-fed lakes, but reviewers say the house sits on a hill above the road. I found no 2025 flood damage reported. There are no reviews between late May and late November 2025 (cause unknown). Reviews resume from Nov 2025 through July 2026.
sources: Airbnb map-search price probes for Oct 2026 to Jan 2027 dates (airbnb.com/s/homes)
highlights: Rated 4.99 from 103 reviews (Superhost Brian, 7 years); latest review July 2026
Single-level home with central AC and a fenced yard; 2,000-acre ranch with lakes, a paddle boat and fishing
Among the cheapest options at around $405-448/night, with the same rate on weekends
About 1.5 hours from downtown SA, near Lost Maples and Garner
places.red_flags: It's remote. Cell service is AT&T only and 'spotty at best', so you rely on wifi calling, which matters if grandma needs help. It sleeps only 6. It's a working cattle ranch where horses and cattle roam. There's no dishwasher. AC can lag in peak summer heat. Some October dates are unavailable.
places.review_signal: 4.99 from 103 reviews. Reviews keep praising the views, the quiet and the cleanliness. The only negatives are AC lag in 100F heat (2020), poor cell service and dirty windows (2021).

places.name: Luxury Secluded Ranch, Stunning View, Fireplaces
places.kind: Airbnb/VRBO house (Step Ladder Ranch Lodge, run by Frio River Cabins)
places.price_note: Booking direct with Frio River Cabins: off-season (Oct to early Mar) is $395/night for 4 guests, regular season (late Mar-May and late Aug-Sept) is $495 for 4, and peak (Memorial Day to early Aug) is $800 for 6. Each extra guest is $30/night, up to 12. The minimum stay is 2 nights (3 on holidays, 4 in peak). Thanksgiving and other holiday weekends run $495-$1,000/night. On Airbnb (Nov 2026 to Jan 2027) it's about $474/night for 2 guests (discounted from $544) plus about $150 cleaning, or $789/night all-in for 10 guests on a 2-night stay. Direct is cheaper, about $515/night for 8 people. There's a $500 refundable deposit at check-in and a signed liability release. Don't leave a one-night gap next to another booking. Airbnb showed nothing for Oct 20-22, Oct 30-Nov 1 or Nov 13-15.
places.group_note: One 4-bedroom, 3-bath house for up to 12, so the whole family fits under one roof. Frio River Cabins also rents cabins and houses about 20 minutes away (Original Cabins, River Terrace and others), but none are next door.
places.scenery_what: A big back porch and deck above a bend of Little Frio Creek, with cypress and live oaks and a distant hill (2026 review). It sits on 100 private acres with no other houses on the creek. Deer come to the feeder, and there's good bird and wildlife watching.
places.access_detail: Airbnb lists 'Central air conditioning' and heating, plus 3 gas fireplaces. Downstairs: 'King master with on suite bathroom' (soaker tub and separate shower), a second king bedroom and a full bath by the kitchen. The upstairs bedroom and landing are reached by stairs. A 2022 review says 'Plenty of parking is available--be sure to park on the paved areas.' The number of steps to the door and the distance from parking aren't stated, and the house sits above the creek, so ask Veronica.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. There's a main-floor master suite, but entry steps aren't listed.
places.flood_note: The house has half a mile of Little Frio Creek frontage and sits 'above' the water. Creek-front land in the Frio basin carries flood risk in extreme storms. I found no 2025 flood impact: reviews continue through July to Sept 2025 (a July 24 2025 review describes fishing the creek normally) and on to Aug 2026.
sources: Airbnb map-search price probes for Nov 2026 to Jan 2027 dates
highlights: The whole family (up to 12) fits in one house with a main-floor king suite and en-suite bath
Creek-front porch on 100 private acres, 4 minutes from Leakey
Rated 4.98 from 50 reviews; latest review Aug 2026
Booking direct for off-season is $395/night for 4 guests
places.red_flags: A Jan 2026 review says the house is older, with a 'sensitive septic system' and 'sometimes low water pressure' for big groups, and no drawers or closets in the bedrooms. Check-in happens at the Frio River Cabins office a few miles away. There are many house rules and fines, a $500 deposit and a liability waiver. The upstairs bedroom needs stairs.
places.review_signal: 4.98 from 50 reviews (98% five-star). Reviewers praise the views from the deck, seclusion, wildlife and linens. The only negatives are the septic system, water pressure and the older house.

places.name: Miracle Lodge | Pool, Hot Tub & Scenic Views
places.price_note: From Airbnb probes (6 guests), with the $275 cleaning fee backed out: $625/night on weeknights (Oct 20-22 and Nov 3-5 2026), $688 on most weekends (Oct 30-Nov 1, Dec 4-6, Jan 15-17), and $813 for Nov 13-15. Examples: $1,525 all-in for 2 weeknights and $2,150 for 3. The base rate covers 6 guests, then it's $50 per guest per night (12 guests adds $300/night). Day guests are $25 each, pets $50 per pet per night, and a liability release is required. Taxes are extra.
places.group_note: One lodge with 4 bedrooms and 11 beds. The listing says it sleeps 20 in beds, or up to 25 with air mattresses, and reviews describe groups of 14-16 fitting. You rent the whole 754-acre ranch lodge, with a pool, hot tub and 2 lakes, but there are only 2 bathrooms.
places.scenery_what: The lodge sits high up. Its long front porch looks over two stocked lakes and the surrounding hills (2024 review: 'the expansive front porch looking over the lakes and hills'). There's a pool with a view and big stargazing skies. A 2025 review mentions the owners' house, a trailer and vehicles nearby.
places.access_detail: Airbnb lists 'Single level home', 'Must climb stairs: Front porch only' and central heating and AC. The King Suite has a 'Private En-Suite Bathroom' with a bathtub and steam shower. The other bedrooms share one tub/shower bath. The road in is a concern: the listing says 'Due to the road conditions from the recent rains, we are not allowing motorcycles to be driven down the hill to the property', and a 2021 review says 'drive going down and up in circles in a mountain... can be a little bit scary'. Reviewers suggest arriving in daylight. The distance from parking to the porch isn't stated.
places.steps_to_enter: Front porch steps only; how many isn't stated.
places.flood_note: The lodge is on high ground ('elevated in the high hills'). A guest there July 4, 2025 wrote 'It was a difficult week because of the rain and the tragic flood on the Guadalupe. We were completely safe.' The private access road down the hill has been rough after recent rains (see the motorcycle ban).
sources: Airbnb map-search price probes for Oct 2026 to Jan 2027 dates
highlights: Everyone under one roof (16-20), single level, porch steps only
Central AC, private pool, hot tub, 2 fishing lakes, canoes and kayaks
Panoramic hilltop views over lakes and hills; rated 4.96 from 46 reviews
Grandma can take the king suite with its own bath
places.red_flags: There were no Airbnb reviews from Aug 2025 to Jul 2026. The listing is now under property manager Backroads Hill Country, while older reviews name on-site owner-hosts, so management may have changed. The winding, steep access road is rough after rain. There are only 2 bathrooms for up to 20 people. Cell service is limited (a landline is provided). A 2024 review calls it 'worn but clean'. The pool is 16 ft deep and the owners' house is nearby.
places.review_signal: 4.96 from 46 reviews. Reviewers love the pool, views and space for big families. Recurring notes are the scary mountain road, no cell signal and worn furnishings.

places.name: Luxury Mountain Top Chalet On 10 Acres With Pool
places.price_note: From Airbnb all-in totals before tax (the price was the same for 4 or 10 guests): $1,552 for Dec 1-3, $1,692 for Nov 10-12 and $1,645 for Nov 3-5 (2 weeknights), and $2,120 for Nov 30-Dec 3 (3 nights). That's about $568-640/night after a current ~9-10% discount, or about $650-705 undiscounted, plus about $420 cleaning. Weekends seem to need 3 nights: Jan 8-11 2027 (Fri-Mon) was $2,204 all-in, while Fri-Sun dates returned nothing. Oct 30-Nov 1, Nov 13-15, Dec 4-6 and Dec 11-13 were unavailable. Pets are $100 each.
places.group_note: One 3,800 sq ft house with 6 bedrooms, 13 beds and 5.5 baths. It sleeps 16+ (the listing text says 20). A Sept 2026 review had 12 adults and 5 grandkids. Most bedrooms have their own bathroom, which suits several families.
places.scenery_what: A house on a hilltop on 10 acres, with a wall of windows and a covered deck looking toward Garner State Park, the Rio Frio valley and the surrounding hills. Deer feed on the property. There's a private pool, playground and fire pit, and the neighborhood is quiet.
places.access_detail: 'Four bedrooms are on the main floor', with Bedrooms 1 and 2 each having an en-suite bath. Only the 2 upper bedrooms and the game room need the 'custom-made marble staircase'. A Sept 2025 review says 'My mother must have walked so many laps with her walker... she loved it too.' A June 2026 review warns 'the driveway up is very steep' for low 2WD sedans, and a 2023 review says there is 'plenty of parking space'. There's central AC in the living area and window units in each bedroom (2026 review: 'no ductwork to the bedrooms... window unit... a little loud'). The number of entry steps isn't stated.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. The main floor is level enough for a walker, per reviews, but entry steps aren't listed.
places.flood_note: Hilltop, above the Frio floodplain, 5 minutes from the river. I found no 2025 flood impact, and reviews run continuously through summer and fall 2025.
sources: Airbnb map-search price probes for Nov 2026 to Feb 2027 dates
highlights: Best big-group fit: 6 bedrooms and 5.5 baths, with 4 bedrooms on the main floor
A 2025 reviewer's mother used her walker happily inside
Wall of windows and deck looking toward Garner State Park; private pool
4.89 from 140 reviews; Guest Favorite; latest review Sept 2026
places.red_flags: It runs on a private well: the host asks for no more than 2 showers at once. An Aug 2025 2-star review reported water pressure 'extremely low or completely unavailable', with toilets unusable at times, plus a broken fridge. The AC failed in a 2023 heat wave and the stay was cut short. The steep driveway is a problem for low cars. Bedroom window units are loud. There's a strict no-parties rule with noise monitors, and weekends need 3 nights.
places.review_signal: 4.89 from 140 reviews. Most praise the views, space and family setup. Negatives recur around well water pressure, plumbing, and AC or heat in the bedrooms.

places.name: Hill Country Dome | Stargazing + Private Escape
places.town: Hondo (401 County Road 2471, north of Hondo toward Bandera)
places.price_note: From Airbnb all-in totals before tax (the same for 2 or 4 guests): $403 for Tue-Thu (Nov 3-5), $555 for Fri-Sun (Oct 30-Nov 1, Nov 13-15, Dec 4-6, Jan 15-17), and $658-734 for 3 nights. That breaks down to about $179 per weeknight, about $255 per Friday or Saturday night (Monday priced about the same), and about $45 cleaning. A one-night stay (Nov 3-4) returned nothing, so there's probably a 2-night minimum. Pets need a $75 non-refundable deposit, and there's a $150 fee for smoking inside.
places.group_note: One dome with 2 bedrooms (queen beds) and 1 bath, for 4 guests, or 'up to 8 total' on request. It's on the Triple C Oasis Resort grounds, which also has Bell Tent Bungalows and primitive sites with shared bathrooms. Overflow family could book those through the resort (ResNexus or 210-570-6515), but I couldn't confirm how many units there are or the rates.
places.scenery_what: A 25-ft geodesic dome with a full-wall picture window and a skylight onto open brush country near Hondo. The land is flatter than the canyon, with a garden, trees and hammocks, sunsets and sunrises, and big starry skies. It has a view of the resort and its pool rather than a hill-country panorama.
places.access_detail: Airbnb lists 'Single level home', and under 'Must climb stairs' says '3 low-profile steps to enter the patio/deck area'. It also lists 'Free parking on premises', a 'Full private bathroom' (shower type not stated), air conditioning and central heating. The house rules mention 'portable AC units' alongside the main AC, and a 2026 review says 'we turned the portables on... The dome was cool by the time we got back.' The listing doesn't say whether there's a handrail or how far parking is.
places.steps_to_enter: 3 low-profile steps up to the patio/deck (listing); no mention of a handrail
places.flood_note: Not on a river and not in the flood-hit basins, and I found no flood note. Reviews mention intense thunderstorms felt inside the dome ('a little scary').
sources: Airbnb map-search price probes for Oct 2026 to Jan 2027 dates
highlights: The real glamping pick: a dome with its own full bath, kitchen and AC
Only 3 low-profile steps; single level
Cheapest private option at about $179-255/night; about 70 minutes from downtown SA
5.0 from 26 reviews; latest Sept 2026
places.red_flags: The host has only about 6 months on Airbnb, and the resort is still building out (its site says 'Final preparations underway', and guests were told about 'future plans' and new amenities). Some spaces are shared, including a pool and hot tub with no gate or lock. No carbon monoxide alarm is listed. One bathroom only. Cooling relies partly on portable AC units. The scenery is less dramatic than the canyon.
places.review_signal: 5.0 from 26 reviews, all 5-star (Mar to Sept 2026). Reviewers praise the stargazing, cleanliness and the host. The only watch-out is storms feeling intense inside the dome.

places.name: Garner State Park - Cabin 18 (ADA cabin), plus the other Old Garner cabins for the rest of the family
places.price_note: TPWD rates: $130/night for the 4 cabins without a fireplace (including ADA Cabin 18) and $150/night for the 13 with a fireplace. The base rate covers 4 people, and it's $10/night per extra person up to 6. There's also a daily entrance fee of $8 per adult 13+ (children 12 and under free) and a 2-night minimum. A cleaning deposit ($130 or $150) is taken by credit card at check-in. Book at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com or 512-389-8900. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 11 am. Availability for specific fall 2026 dates wasn't checked.
places.group_note: 17 cabins in the Old Garner / Oakmont area (13 with a fireplace, 4 without). Each has 2 double beds, sleeping 4 at the base rate and up to 6. The family can reserve several neighboring cabins and put grandma in Cabin 18. No tents or RVs are allowed at the cabins, and no pets.
places.scenery_what: On the Frio River valley floor inside Garner State Park. According to the park map, the cabins sit in the Oakmont camping loop near the CCC Pavilion and a bend of the Frio River, with limestone hills including Old Baldy around. It's pretty and wooded, with campground neighbors. TPWD doesn't describe a view from each cabin.
places.access_detail: TPWD accessibility page: 'Cabin 18 in the Oakmont camping area is ADA compliant with a sidewalk leading from the parking space to the cabin.' Cabins page: 'Cabin #18 is equipped for special physical needs in the bathroom, doorways, and the entrance from driveway.' Every cabin has an indoor bathroom (sink, toilet, shower), central air conditioning and heating, and a kitchenette with a stove but no oven. The shower type (roll-in or grab bars) isn't specified. The ADA restrooms and showers in Shady Meadows have handrails and a bench. Trails are 'rugged, rocky', so grandma's outdoor time is mostly the cabin area and ADA-parking spots like the Pavilion.
places.steps_to_enter: Cabin 18: none; it's ADA with a sidewalk from its parking space. Other cabins: unknown.
places.flood_note: The Oakmont / Old Garner area lies along a bend of the Frio River per the park map, so it's near the river floodplain. TPWD pages mention no 2025 flood damage to cabins. Current alerts: a river advisory dated July 21, 2026 ('Swimming is permitted on the river at your own risk', cause not stated) with the Blinn River and White Rock Cave trails closed; scenic overlook construction (sidewalk closed, parts of the Madrone and CCC Entrance Road trails closed); and a burn ban since Sept 17, 2026 (no wood fires, charcoal OK).
highlights: The only verified ADA unit: sidewalk from its parking space, and an accessible bath, doorways and entrance
Cheapest option at $130-150/night per cabin plus $8/adult/day entry
17 cabins together, so the whole family can book side by side
Central AC and heat in every cabin; inside Texas's best-known canyon park
places.red_flags: Bring everything: no linens, blankets, towels, dishes or utensils are provided, and there's no oven. The burn ban means no wood fires in the fireplaces or fire rings. The park is busy, with campground neighbors. Some trails are closed and river swimming is at your own risk. I didn't check reviews of the cabins themselves; this rests on TPWD's official pages only.
places.review_signal: No review source checked (search budget ran out); TPWD's official pages only.

skeptic.name: Garner State Park - Cabin 18 (ADA cabin), plus the other Old Garner cabins for the rest of the family
skeptic.evidence: The TPWD accessibility page confirms: 'Cabin 18 in the Oakmont camping area is ADA compliant with a sidewalk leading from the parking space to the cabin.' The cabins page confirms: 'Cabin #18 is equipped for special physical needs in the bathroom, doorways, and the entrance from driveway'; each cabin has a bathroom sink, toilet and shower plus 'Central air-conditioning and heating'. Rates are confirmed at $150/night with fireplace (13 cabins) and $130 without (4 cabins), plus the $8/adult/day entrance fee (under-13 free; 50% off for Texas residents 65+ with a Parklands Passport). The 2024 park map shows the cabin icons among the Oakmont/Pecan Grove loops by the Pavilion and a bend of the Frio, so the scenery description is fair. CAVEATS: each cabin has 'Two double beds', 4 people (6 max at $10/night extra), a 2-night minimum, no pets, and 'No linens, blankets or towels provided', so bring bedding for grandma. The shower type in Cabin 18 (roll-in or lip) is not stated. Current park alerts: burn ban since Sept 17, 2026 ('No wood fires are allowed'); as of July 21, 2026 the Blinn River and White Rock Cave trails are closed and river swimming is 'at your own risk'; Scenic Overlook sidewalk is closed for construction. There is no current cabin closure or flood closure. Booking: TPWD says 'Most overnight camping or lodging reservations may be reserved up to five months in advance', opening 8 a.m. As of 9/24/2026 fall 2026 dates are open, but spring 2027 (March and later) opens only 5 months out. Garner cabins sell out fast. Specific availability is unverified.

places.name: Hidden Oaks at Concan (Airbnb)
places.price_note: Airbnb only shows all-in totals (displayPriceStyle TOTAL_ONLY, which includes the cleaning and service fees but not taxes), so the base nightly rate is lower than these figures and I couldn't find it. Search totals on 9/24/26: Oct 16-19 (Fri-Mon) $951 = $317/night; Oct 19-22 (weeknights) $921 = $307/night; Oct 19-24 (5 nights) $1,396 = $279/night. The Airbnb calendar shows a 3-night minimum every month and open dates Oct 2026 through mid-March 2027. The main guest must be 25 or older. The pool is only open May to August, so it will be closed on a fall trip.
places.group_note: One house with 3 bedrooms, each with 1 queen, and 2 full baths (the master bath is attached; bedrooms 2 and 3 share the other). The listing says it sleeps 8, but a Dec 2024 reviewer said it really sleeps 6 and the extra spots are an air mattress. Parking fits 4 cars. That's too small for a big extended family alone. It could house grandma plus the core family, with others in Garner State Park cabins about 10 minutes away.
places.scenery_what: You pull in under a covered carport next to a mint-green house tucked into live oaks. Out back is a large raised deck, partly covered, that looks over oak woods, a small creek or water hole and the canyon hills. The host says 'breathtaking views of oak trees, hill country, and starry skies.' Reviewers watched birds from the porch (painted buntings, hummingbirds). It's secluded but in woods: you see treetops and hills, not a big open panorama, and the river isn't visible from the house.
places.steps_to_enter: 0. A listing photo shows a railed wheelchair-style ramp from the covered carport parking to the front door, and Airbnb lists 'Step-free access' for the guest entrance and parking. Airbnb's property info separately says 'Must climb stairs,' probably the back deck or yard (not confirmed).
places.access_detail: Airbnb accessibility feature: 'no steps, stairs, or curbs on the entire path' from arrival to the entrance. Amenity 'Single level home: No stairs in home.' Photos show a covered carport right along the house with a long ramp and handrails to the front door. The master bath has a shower and a separate tub. It's unconfirmed whether that shower is walk-in, and there are no grab bars listed. There's central heat and AC, but 2 reviews say the AC struggled in summer ('AC struggled a bit,' June 2026; 'Took overnight to cool off,' Aug 2025). That matters less in fall. You reach it on a gravel drive 'thru our neighbors property.'
places.flood_note: Not on the Frio floodplain. The house sits up on a slope above a small creek; the host says river access points are 5 minutes' drive. The listing mentions 'heights and drop offs.' I found no sign of 2025 flood damage: guests reviewed it in Aug 2025 and in June and Aug 2026, and the Wikipedia article on the July 2025 floods doesn't mention the Frio.
places.red_flags: (1) The drive in goes through a neighbor's property, which one Aug 2025 reviewer called 'very sketchy and full of trash.' (2) The AC struggled in 2 summer reviews. (3) There are 'Heights without rails or protection,' and Airbnb marks it 'Not suitable for children and infants.' (4) Well water and septic; one guest's toilet tank took hours to refill (Dec 2024). (5) Cell service is poor in the canyon (Wi-Fi calling works). (6) 3-night minimum. (7) Realistically sleeps 6. (8) 5 exterior security cameras.
highlights: Railed ramp from a covered carport straight to the front door, with a single-level interior
Big covered back deck over the oaks, good for birdwatching and stars; fire pit and grill
About 10 minutes to Garner State Park, 5 minutes to river access points, near Neal's in Concan
Superhost, 4.86 from 35 reviews, Guest Favorite
Open dates Oct 2026 through mid-March 2027

3 miles to Garner State Park, 2.5 miles to Leakey groceries

places.name: Garner State Park Cabins (incl. ADA Cabin #18)
places.price_note: From TPWD: $130/night for a cabin without a fireplace (4 units, including ADA Cabin #18) and $150/night with a fireplace (13 units). That rate covers 4 people; up to 6 are allowed at $10/night for each extra person. On top of that, park entry is $8/day per person age 13+ (12 and under free), and the cleaning deposit is $130 (standard) or $150 (fireplace), charged to a credit card. 2-night minimum. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 11 am. Reserve online or at 512-389-8900. Weekends often fill, so book Cabin #18 first.
places.group_note: There are 17 cabins, each with two double beds, sleeping 4 (6 max). The family can book several. The park map puts them together on one spur road in the Old Garner/Oakmont area, near the Pavilion and park store. Only Cabin #18 is ADA; put grandma there and the rest of the family in neighboring cabins.
places.scenery_what: The cabins sit along a wooded spur road in the busy Old Garner area, between the Pavilion and gift shop and the Oakmont camping loops. From the door you see trees, the park road and nearby campsites, with the canyon hills around the valley. They're not riverfront: the Frio is a few hundred yards east on the park map. TPWD says 'In the fall, the scenery is spectacular,' and reviews on The Dyrt praise 'stunning cliffs rising from the water.' The big views are a short drive or walk from the cabin, not at the door.
places.steps_to_enter: Cabin #18: none. TPWD says there's 'a sidewalk leading from the parking space to the cabin' and it is equipped for special physical needs at 'the entrance from driveway.' Step counts for the other 16 cabins are unknown.
places.access_detail: TPWD cabins page: Cabin #18 (no fireplace) 'is equipped for special physical needs in the bathroom, doorways, and the entrance from driveway.' The accessibility page adds 'a sidewalk leading from the parking space to the cabin.' Every cabin has a private bathroom (sink, toilet, shower), central AC and heat, and a kitchenette (sink, microwave, fridge, stove, no oven). The Shady Meadows restrooms have 'large, private shower facilities that have handrails and a bench.' Park rule: all vehicles stay on the pavement.
places.flood_note: The cabins are in the river-bottom Old Garner area, a few hundred yards from the Frio but not on the bank. I found no 2025 flood closure on TPWD's pages, and the Wikipedia article on the July 2025 floods doesn't mention the Frio or Garner. Current park alerts (checked 9/24/26): a burn ban since Sept 17, 2026 (no wood fires; charcoal and gas stoves OK). A July 21, 2026 river advisory says swimming is at your own risk and the Blinn River Trail and White Rock Cave Trail are closed (no reason given). An April 29, 2026 construction notice says the Scenic Overlook sidewalk is closed. There's also a statewide screwworm alert about pets and livestock, with no facility closures.
places.red_flags: (1) Only ONE ADA cabin (#18), so it has to be booked early. (2) You bring your own bedding, towels, dishes and utensils; nothing is provided. (3) Only two double beds per cabin. (4) Kitchenette with no oven. (5) Cabins are in the busiest part of the park, near the campsites and the Pavilion (known for summer jukebox dances), so it can be crowded and noisy in peak season. (6) Wood fires are banned right now. (7) Daily entry fee per person on top of the cabin rate. (8) The cleaning deposit is charged up front. (9) No pets in cabins. (10) The other cabins' steps are unknown.
highlights: Official ADA Cabin #18: sidewalk from the parking space, accessible bathroom and doorways
Budget price: $130-150/night per cabin, so a family can take 3-4 cabins for the price of one big house
17 cabins together, each with a private bath, central AC and heat, and a kitchenette
Frio River, Old Baldy hill and fall color in the park; about 10 minutes from Concan rentals

skeptic.name: Inn at Sunset Mill Ranch (book the Granary Room for grandma; a whole-property group rental is available)
skeptic.evidence: The Granary claims check out. The FAQ says 'the Granary Room has ground-level access, no curb large shower and wider doorways'. The Granary page lists 'Walk-in Shower | Ada Compliant' and 'Individually controlled heat and air conditioning system'. Cloudbeds describes 'a large, easy-access shower' and 'breathtaking views of the hills, valleys, and sunsets'. Parking is 'uncovered but conveniently located near all suites', with no distance given. The contradiction is real: the Accessibility Statement says the inn 'does not offer any handicap accessible accommodations' under the small-inn exemption, while listing an ADA ramp to the deck and Breakfast Room plus an ADA powder room. The FAQ also warns 'some outdoor terrain is naturally uneven due to our hilltop setting.' The claim missed several things. The Granary sleeps 2 max (Cloudbeds: MaxAdults 2, MaxChildren 0). The FAQ says 'we allow children 12 and older only. The only exception is for group rentals where all of the rooms are reserved.' The rest of the group rental is mostly stairs: the three Carriage House rooms are second-story, the Maggie suite is upstairs in the main lodge, the cabin has an upstairs loft, and the Glamper's large bathroom is outside. The whole-property rental sleeps 14 (+2-3 with the Maggie suite), and its price is unknown. Price was unknown in the claim. Google Hotels showed the official site at $259/night base ($275 with taxes) for Sep 28-29, 2026, and said the property 'typically costs between $202-$323 per night'. The Granary's own rate is not published. Rated 5.0 from 161 reviews, with live rates, so it is operating. It is on a hilltop, so no flood exposure.

skeptic.evidence: CONFIRMED: The ADA Spyglass listing has step-free access, a disabled parking spot, a single-level layout, a private walk-in shower and AC.
