places.price_note: Official rate table: river-view efficiency $219 weekday / $269 weekend / $299 holiday; 2BR riverside single-story $269 / $319 / $349; poolside 1BR $219 / $269 and 2BR $239 / $289; 2-story riverside 2BR $309 / $379 and 3BR $329 / $409. The table is headed 'Summer Rates 2026' while the policy text says 'Valid through September 15th - May 14th', so confirm fall rates by phone (830-964-3613). 2-night minimum, 3 nights on Thanksgiving/Christmas/New Year. No separate cleaning fee listed. Pets: $50 cleaning, cabins 6, 7, 21, 23 only. Book via Campspot (bot-protected, could not check availability) or phone.
places.group_note: Single-story cabins sleep 4; 2-story riverside cabins sleep 8. Individual cabins along 1/4 mile of river frontage, so several can be booked near each other. Total cabin count not stated (pet policy mentions cabin #23). Event hall and pergola can be rented for a family dinner.
places.scenery_what: River-view cabins have private decks with picnic tables facing the Guadalupe, with bluffs and big trees; the site says 'The best views of the Guadalupe River are from the Hill Country cabins'. It is also an RV park with neighbors, a big pool and tubing traffic in season.
places.steps_to_enter: Efficiency and 2BR cabins are single-story; steps to deck or door not stated. Avoid the 2-story riverside cabins (bedrooms upstairs, only a half bath up there on the 3BR).
places.access_detail: Site: efficiency has 'Full Bathroom with Shower', 2BR has 'Full Bathroom with Tub/Shower', all have 'Air Conditioning & Heating'. Policies: 'Resort property has rough and uneven terrain - please watch your step', 'Please do not park or drive on the grass', 'No ATVs or golf carts allowed'. No accessibility information; parking distance unknown. The efficiency's shower is easier for grandma than the 2BR tub.
places.flood_note: Riverside cabins sit in the Guadalupe floodplain on River Road below Canyon Lake Dam, and River Road low-water crossings close in high water. The site says nothing about July 2025 flooding (the deadly July 2025 flood was upstream of Canyon Lake); could not verify, ask when booking.
places.review_signal: Campendium 4.0 (6 reviews, RV guests, newest 2023). Site testimonials praise the river-view decks. No recent cabin reviews found; Yelp and TripAdvisor blocked.
places.red_flags: Renter must be 21+. No dishes or utensils in most cabins (bring your own). Rate table label conflict. Website has leftover template filler and a placeholder email. Floodplain. Uneven ground and no golf carts allowed.
highlights: Cheapest real river view with private bath and AC ($219 weekday)
Big pool, kayak rentals with shuttle, fly fishing
Closest of the six to San Antonio
Multiple cabins for family side by side

places.name: McKinney Falls State Park, Cabin 6 (wheelchair-accessible; book Cabin 5 next door for family)
places.town: Austin (5808 McKinney Falls Pkwy, 13 mi from the state capitol)
places.price_note: $86/night per cabin plus park entry $6 per adult per day (kids 12 and under free). 2-night minimum on weekends, 3 on holidays and special events. Book at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com. Bring your own linens. Check-in 3pm, out 11am.
places.group_note: 6 cabins, 4 twin beds each. Cabins sit in pairs (1-2, 3-4, 5-6), so Cabins 5 and 6 together sleep 8; 81 campsites nearby for extra family.
places.scenery_what: Cabins sit in woods near the campground loop, no view from the door. Onion Creek, bald cypress and the Upper and Lower Falls are a short drive or walk; the Onion Creek trail has a hard surface. Park is near the airport and city roads.
places.steps_to_enter: Cabin 6 has paved pathways designed for wheelchair use; entry details not stated.
places.access_detail: TPWD: 'Cabin 6 is wheelchair-accessible with an extended picnic table and paved pathways'. No restroom in any cabin; 'a restroom-shower house is a short walking distance away'. Big Cedar and Grapevine restrooms have ADA parking and accessible stalls. Park lends all-terrain wheelchairs (Grit Freedom Chair, EcoRover Trackchair) 9am-4pm by reservation, (512) 243-1643. Campendium reviewers call the showers 'older style big open bay for dressing' and bathrooms 'dated but fine'.
places.flood_note: TPWD: 'Onion Creek can flood after rainfall.' Current alerts (Sept 2026) are only a burn ban from Aug 11, 2026 (no wood fires) and a day-pass reservation notice; no flood damage notice.
places.review_signal: Campendium 4.0 (97 reviews, whole park): falls fun for kids, park convenient to Austin; complaints that it is 'close to the airport' and 'you can hear cars', bathrooms dated.
places.red_flags: No bathroom in the cabin, so night trips outside for grandma. Twin beds only. No pets. Bring linens. Wood-fire burn ban in effect. Weekend day passes sell out. Weakest scenery of the six.
highlights: Cheapest option by far: $86/night
Paved, wheelchair-designed path at Cabin 6
Loaner all-terrain wheelchairs to see the falls
20 minutes from downtown Austin

places.name: Rose Hill Retreat (Primrose Cottage is the accessible one; the Poppy House is a 3-bedroom house; you can also rent the whole property)
places.town: Stonewall (2614 Upper Albert Rd, about 15 mi east of Fredericksburg)
places.price_note: Live WebRez rate calendar for Oct-Dec 2026: every suite and cottage, Primrose included, is $199 Sun-Thu and $299 Fri-Sat; Poppy House $399/night every night (flagged phone booking only). Base rate covers 2 guests, +$50 per extra guest per night. 2-night minimum on weekends. Breakfast included (full hot breakfast Wed-Sun, pastries Mon-Tue). Cancel more than 10 days out: $20 fee. Groups of more than 4 rooms and whole-property buyouts by phone, 830-644-8488 (buyout price not published). Good availability in Oct-Dec (Primrose open 62 of 70 nights checked).
places.group_note: 18 suites and cottages on 38 hilltop acres plus the 3-bedroom Poppy House. Primrose (king) for grandma; family-friendly West Cottage has Purple Sage (king + queen bedrooms) and Hidden Hideaway (king + daybed, sleeps 3); Poppy House for a larger branch of the family. Children only 12+ on Friday and Saturday stays, so plan Sun-Thu if young kids come.
places.scenery_what: Hilltop country inn: Primrose has 'a wonderful deck in front with a fabulous view', and the Herb Garden cottages have 'big, panoramic views of the countryside'. Rolling ranchland, longhorns, Pedernales Cellars vineyard next door. Not canyon or water.
places.steps_to_enter: Primrose: wheelchair-accessible boardwalk ramp to the front door (site photo caption). Main House suites are upstairs with no elevator. Poppy House steps unknown.
places.access_detail: Site: 'This suite is handicap-accessible, except that the tub/shower is NOT a roll-in'; photo captioned 'Front entrance of the Primrose Cottage with wheelchair-accessible boardwalk ramp' (uploaded Aug 2026); private bath with tub and shower; king bed; 'enclosed heated and air-conditioned sun porch'. Rooms page: Main House suites 'upstairs... Please note there is no elevator.' Parking distance not stated.
places.flood_note: Hilltop property, not in a floodplain. No 2025 flood impact mentioned on the site.
places.review_signal: The TripAdvisor page the inn links (d270415) blocked scripted access, so no review snippets verified. Site says AAA Four Diamond.
places.red_flags: Tub/shower combo, grandma must step over a tub edge. Kids 12+ only on Fri/Sat. Poppy House phone-only. Farthest drive of the six. No pets.
highlights: Ramp entry cottage with a view deck for $199 weeknights
Breakfast included
Walk or short drive to Pedernales Cellars winery
Poppy House 3-bedroom for the rest of the family at $399
Whole-property buyout possible

places.name: Settlers Crossing (historic homes on one property; a whole-property 'Sanctuary' buyout is also offered)
places.kind: cabin (cluster of 8 restored 1787-1865 historic homes and log cabins on 35 acres)
places.town: Fredericksburg (about 5 min east-southeast of downtown, toward Luckenbach; listing pin approx. 30.216, -98.801)
places.price_note: Official 2026 OwnerRez listings, per home, per night, before fees: Indiana House $140-150, Kusenberger Log Cabin $175-300, Baag Farm House $175-300, Pioneer Log Cabin $200-300, Von Heinrich $225-300, Kusenberger Barn $300, Bohl Cabin $325, Richland Estate $450-800 (has a private pool). Fees and taxes are added at checkout. The manager's pages list a $200 cleaning fee per home, $25 per guest per night after 4 guests, and $35 per pet per night. 2-night minimum year-round, 3 nights on select holidays and event weekends. Cancellation: 50% refund only if you cancel more than 14 days out, nothing after that. Whole-property 'Sanctuary' buyout is $3,500-4,500/night (18 bedrooms, 10 full baths, sleeps 20-34, 2-night minimum).
places.group_note: 8 separate homes on one 35-acre property. Most homes sleep 2-4, Pioneer Log Cabin sleeps 6, and Richland Estate sleeps 7-10. A family can book several homes side by side or rent the whole place as the 'Sanctuary' (sleeps 20-34). Each home has its own kitchen or kitchenette and a grill. Pets are allowed. Renters must be 21+.
places.scenery_what: Pastoral Hill Country farm: big oaks, open fields and pasture, flower gardens, Settlers Creek, grazing farm animals, deer at dusk, and dark starry nights. The best view is from the Kusenberger Log Cabin, whose full-length stone porch with rockers looks out 'over the Hill Country beyond'. That cabin sleeps only 2. Most other homes look onto shaded oak grounds and gardens rather than a sweeping vista.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown number of steps. Every official listing says 'Wheelchair inaccessible'. Single-level homes: Indiana House, Baag Farm House, Kusenberger Log Cabin, Pioneer Log Cabin and Von Heinrich, though Von Heinrich is also tagged 'Requires Stairs'. Bohl Cabin and Kusenberger Barn are two-story. Richland Estate is three stories and tagged 'Requires Stairs'.
places.access_detail: The official listings (settlerscrossing.com, run on OwnerRez by Backroads Hill Country) say 'Free Parking', 'Air Conditioning' and one private bathroom per home. Indiana House, Kusenberger Log Cabin and Von Heinrich have a shower. Baag Farm House has a shower/tub combo. Every home, including the whole-property Sanctuary, is marked 'Wheelchair inaccessible', and nothing says how far parking is from each door. These are 1840s-1860s buildings, so expect porch steps, thresholds and stone floors. Kusenberger Log Cabin has 'original stone' floors. For grandma, the best bets are the single-level Indiana House or Baag Farm House. Call (830) 850-9011 and ask for step counts, how close you can park, and whether the shower is walk-in. No review found mentions steps, walking or parking.
places.flood_note: Settlers Creek runs through the property. The Pedernales River, which flooded in July 2025, is in the same area near Fredericksburg. I found no report of 2025 flood damage or closure here, and the listings are live and taking bookings with 2026 rates. Ask which homes sit highest above the creek.
places.review_signal: The new official site's review widget shows 'No reviews found'. Tripadvisor, Yelp and search engines blocked automated lookups. An archived March 2025 version of the old site had 5-star guest testimonials, e.g. 'Lovely stay with my husband and in-laws' and 'Absolutely magical! ... We loved the animals'. None mention access. The manager, Backroads Hill Country, is an Airbnb Superhost rated 4.85 across 5,636 reviews, but that covers its whole portfolio, not this property.
places.red_flags: Management changed hands between 2025 and 2026. The 2025 site was owner-run with its own phone and email. The 2026 site is run by vacation-rental manager Backroads Hill Country, so older reviews may not reflect how it runs now. No property-specific reviews could be verified. Every home is listed as wheelchair-inaccessible, and several are multi-story. The $200 cleaning fee per home adds up if you book several homes. Cancellation terms are strict. Richland's pool/jacuzzi is listed as 'No Fence'.
highlights: 8 historic homes on one 35-acre property; families can book side by side or rent the whole place for 20-34 guests ($3,500-4,500/night)
Budget-friendly single-level Indiana House from $140/night; most 2-bedroom homes $175-325
Farm animals, deer, creek and dark skies; the Kusenberger Log Cabin porch looks out over the Hill Country
AC, private bath and fireplace in every home; about 85 min from San Antonio

places.name: Palo Alto Creek Farm (Itz House farmhouse + Log Cabin; 4 guest houses total)
places.drop_reason: Could not confirm it is still bookable. All 4 of the site's online booking links (fbglodging.com/.../palo-alto-creek-farm-*) return 404. A search of the reservation service it names (Gästehaus Schmidt, 202 listings) finds no Palo Alto Creek Farm, only an unrelated 'Diamond Belle at Palo Alto Crossing'. Wayback Machine snapshots show those booking pages last working in Nov 2019. The farm's own pages and rates have not changed since 2018-2019. It also fits a family poorly: children under 12 are not accepted anywhere, and 3 of the 4 houses are 'not suitable for children' (couples-only units that sleep 2).
places.kind: inn/B&B (4 guest houses on an 1850s-1870s historic farm)
places.town: Fredericksburg (about 5 mi from downtown; exact address given only after booking)
places.price_note: These rates are from 2018 and may be out of date: Hideaway $160, Barn $225, Log Cabin $225, Itz House $350 for 1-4 people plus $50 per extra person (up to 6). Plus 13% tax. 2-night weekend minimum. Continental-plus breakfast included. Cancelling within 10 days means paying the full stay if the house can't be rebooked; $30 fee otherwise. No 2026 rate could be confirmed.
places.group_note: 4 houses. Only the Itz House takes more than 2 people (2-6, children 12 and over only). The Barn, Hideaway and Log Cabin each sleep 2 and are 'not suitable for children'. No pets. Poor fit for a multi-generation family group.
places.scenery_what: A quiet pastoral farm rather than a big vista: an ancient 'grandfather' oak, open countryside, Palo Alto Creek at the back of the property, donkeys and longhorns, and deer gathering at sunset. One old review mentions a 'breath-taking view of Palo Alto Creek'.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. Itz House has 'original, very steep' stairs to the upper floor, but there is a queen bedroom and bath downstairs.
places.access_detail: Every house has a private bath and central or room AC. The Hideaway has a 'walk-in shower of tumbled marble', which is the best bath for grandma, but it sleeps 2 and does not take children. The Itz House's downstairs bath is a claw-foot tub with a hand-held shower, so there is a tub wall to step over. The Log Cabin has a whirlpool tub plus a separate shower. The Barn has a whirlpool tub with a hand-held shower. The site's 'accessibility' page covers only the website, not the buildings. Parking and step counts are not stated.
places.flood_note: Palo Alto Creek runs along the back of the property; it is a Pedernales-area creek near Fredericksburg. No information found on July 2025 flood impact.
places.review_signal: The farm's own review page has only old testimonials, including an anniversary 'revisit' and couples' getaways. None are dated recently or mention access. Tripadvisor blocked automated access, so recent reviews could not be checked.
places.red_flags: Online booking links are dead, it no longer appears on the reservation service, and the website has not been updated since about 2019, so it may no longer be operating as a rental. Children under 12 are not accepted anywhere, and no pets.
highlights: Historic farm with deer, longhorns and a creek; breakfast included (per the 2018 site)
Hideaway has a walk-in marble shower (sleeps 2)
Not confirmed bookable in 2026

places.name: Hill Country Casitas & Retreat (La Benita, Casita #9, is the ADA unit)
places.kind: cabin (boutique casita resort: 11 casitas + off-site Ranch House on 13 acres)
places.town: Dripping Springs (7400 McGregor Ln, about 11 mi from downtown Dripping Springs toward the Pedernales River valley)
places.price_note: 2026 per-casita rates are only shown in the ResNexus booking engine, which blocked automated lookups. These figures come from the property's own rate sheet (version 7/23, labeled '2023-2024 Rates'), weekday / weekend per night: studios $229-249 / $289-309, La Benita (ADA) $319 / $399, CeCe and Polly Ann $339 / $429, The Pauline $359 / $449, The Retreat $339 / $399, 2-bedroom casitas $459 / $549, Ranch House $399 / $459. That sheet lists 6% state hotel tax and 'no other fees such as cleaning'. 2-night minimum, 3 on holidays. Dogs $50 per dog per night. Whole property (11 casitas, sleeps 44) was $3,500/night Sun-Thu and $4,300/night Fri-Sat in 2023-24. The current 2026 site says whole property plus Pavilion for 2 nights 'starts at $8000'. Cancellation: full refund minus $50 at 30+ days, 50% or credit at 14-29 days, nothing under 14 days. Call or text 512.829.1558 for current rates.
places.group_note: 11 casitas: 4 studios (sleep 2), 4 one-bedrooms (sleep 4, including ADA La Benita), The Retreat (sleeps 4), and two 2-bedroom casitas (sleep 8). Plus the Ranch House (sleeps 7), about 1/4 mile away off the main property. Up to 51 guests in total. You can book 2 or more casitas online or take the whole property. The site says 'We LOVE family reunions'. A June 2025 reunion testimonial covers 42 people aged '90 years old to 11 months old'. Shared pool, hot tub, fire pit, and a Pavilion with a full kitchen for group meals.
places.scenery_what: Hill Country ridge setting on 13 acres with dark skies. The studios sit 'high on The Ridge overlooking the hillside and valley below' (The Gina B. has the premium vista). The CeCe is on a cul-de-sac with 'unobstructed views of the natural landscape'. The Retreat and Los Amigos have 'expansive Hill Country views'. The Pavilion views are described by guests as 'stunning'. The Ranch House porch overlooks the Pedernales River Valley. La Benita (the ADA unit) is central, next to the pool and Pavilion, so its own porch view is probably more grounds than panorama. Each casita has a covered porch with rockers and a wood-burning fireplace.
places.park_at_unit: under 100 ft (the property map shows a parking spot right beside #8/#9 on The Mesa; the map is illustrated and not to scale)
places.steps_to_enter: La Benita (#9) is ADA accessible. The official FAQ says 'Only The Pauline, Casita #1, has steps', so the other casitas are step-free too.
places.access_detail: FAQ: 'La Benita (Casita #9) is ADA accessible' and 'Only The Pauline, Casita #1, has steps'. The one-bedroom page says La Benita 'is located right in the heart of our property and offers comfortable and convenient accessible accommodations. With close proximity to the pool/hot tub and the Pavilion.' Every casita has 'Air conditioning + heating', a private bath with a walk-in shower, and a kitchen. Self check-in with a keyless door code; there is no front desk. How far you park from each door is not stated, so confirm drive-up parking at La Benita when booking. A June 2025 reunion guest wrote that the property worked for a group 'ranging from 90 years old to 11 months old', and a 2025 blog post describes 'grandparents watching the little ones at the pool'.
places.flood_note: The casitas sit on a ridge, so floodplain risk looks low. The Ranch House overlooks the Pedernales River valley from its porch. There was no 2025 flood impact: the property was running normally in summer 2025, and its Aug 2025 blog says it took in a family reunion displaced by the July 4 floods in Hunt.
places.review_signal: Clearly operating in 2026: Feb 2026 retreat-host testimonial, June 2025 reunion testimonial, and an Aug 2025 blog post. The site's structured data claims 4.9 stars from 125 reviews, but the source is not named and the sample reviews look generic. Google and Tripadvisor could not be checked directly because automated access was blocked.
places.red_flags: Prices come from a 2023-24 rate sheet; 2026 rates are unconfirmed. It is a long drive from San Antonio: about 1h40 by routing, though the site claims 60 min. No restaurant on site, and the nearest HEB is about 15 mi away, so bring groceries. The Ranch House is off the main property. The pool is not heated. Casitas have no TVs. Dogs are allowed. Weddings or events may book the Pavilion.
highlights: True ADA casita (La Benita #9), step-free casitas except #1, and walk-in showers everywhere: the best grandma access of the three
Built for family groups: 11 casitas side by side plus a Pavilion kitchen for group meals; whole property sleeps 44-51
Ridge-top Hill Country views, pool, hot tub, fire pit, dark skies
About 55 min from Austin and 1h40 from San Antonio

skeptic.name: Hill Country Casitas & Retreat (La Benita, Casita #9, is the ADA unit)
skeptic.corrected_park_at_unit: under 100 ft (the property map shows a parking spot right beside #8/#9 on The Mesa; the map is illustrated and not to scale)
skeptic.evidence: The official FAQ confirms 'La Benita (Casita #9) is ADA accessible' and 'Only The Pauline, Casita #1, has steps'. The one-bedroom page says La Benita is 'right in the heart of our property' near the pool, hot tub and Pavilion. The amenities page lists 'Air conditioning + heating', and all casitas have walk-in showers. Whether La Benita's shower is roll-in is not stated. The official illustrated property map (hillcountrycasitas.com/property-map) shows a 'P' parking marker right next to casitas #8 and #9 on The Mesa, beside the Pavilion and firepit, so drive-up parking looks likely. Confirm the exact distance by phone (512.829.1558). Caveat on scenery: the best overlook ('Bella Vista') sits at the end of a hiking trail across Deadman's Creek, and Google describes '13 acres of wooded grounds'. Grandma's easy panorama is the Pavilion next to #9, which a June 2025 reunion review calls 'stunning'. Price: Google Hotels showed the official site at $207/night base ($219 with taxes) for Sep 26-27, 2026. Expedia rates for the same night were Standard Studio $256, Premium Studio valley view $269, Deluxe Studio $320, Honeymoon House $360 and 2BR Premium House $429 base. La Benita's own rate and the $549 top end were not verified. Google rates it 5.0 from 214 reviews and shows live availability, so it is operating. There is no sign of flood damage (it sits on a ridge). Whole-property booking sleeps 44-51, with a $1,000 retainer.

places.name: Casa Topo at Sparrow Bend River Retreat (Casa Avecita, the 1BR/1BA tiny home, is on the same property; you can also rent the whole property)
places.town: Lakehills / Pipe Creek (Medina River, just above Medina Lake)
places.price_note: Airbnb prices for 8 adults, checked 9/24/2026. Airbnb says 'Prices include all fees', so these include the cleaning and service fees but not taxes. Oct 20-22 (Tue-Thu): $743 for 2 nights ($371.50/night). Oct 16-18 (Fri-Sun): $966 ($483/night, marked down from $1,158). Nov 3-5 (weeknights): $485.50/night. Nov 6-8 (weekend): $1,240 ($620/night). Dec 4-6: $571/night. Free cancellation until about 5 days before arrival. For both houses or the whole property, the listing says 'contact us for rates' (no price posted). Casa Avecita (Airbnb 559287190181554279): $308/night Nov 3-5 and $493.50/night Nov 6-8, booked for Oct 16-18. Firewood is $7-9 a bundle, and kayaks and tubes are for rent.
places.group_note: Casa Topo is 4BR/2BA and sleeps 12. The dining table seats 12, plus 2 bar stools. The same 8 acres has Casa Avecita (1BR, sleeps 4, but Airbnb flags it 'Must climb stairs'), a vintage camper, 4-6 tent sites and 2 RV slots with hookups. A host photo caption says a third house, 'The Penny House' (1/1, sleeps 4), is 'coming soon'. A July 2022 reviewer booked the big house, the cabin and 2 RV spots for one family trip. Renting the whole property is by request.
places.scenery_what: A big wrap-around porch looking over the lawn and trees toward a private 300-yard stretch of the spring-fed Medina River, about 100 yards away, with limestone bluffs and coves. Reviewers mention great sunsets and very dark, starry skies. It is pretty river country, not a sweeping vista.
places.steps_to_enter: 0: a host photo caption says 'Entrance to Casa Topo is easy with ramp entering the wrap around porch.' Airbnb flags it 'Single level home' / 'No stairs in home'.
places.access_detail: The listing says 'Parking is onsite right next to Casa Topo.' The entrance is a ramp onto the wrap-around porch, and Airbnb lists it as a single-level home with no stairs. It has central AC and central heat. There are 2 full baths: one has a freestanding soaking tub and a separate shower with a curtain, and the other is a tub with a handheld shower head. There is no roll-in or walk-in shower. The river is about 100 yards away. A June 2026 reviewer said the walk down to the water was farther than the photos suggest, but 'we were able to drive down', so grandma can be driven to the riverbank. A June 2025 reviewer thanked the host for a wagon/cart.
places.flood_note: Riverfront (Medina River/Lake frontage), with the house about 100 yards from the water. Airbnb reviews continue straight through June-August 2025 (for example, July 2025: 'the river was awesome and it was a quick walk from the house'), and none mention flooding or damage. No official statement about the July 2025 floods was found, so damage is not confirmed either way. River levels swing a lot: 2022-2023 reviews complained about low, hot water, while 2026 reviews say 'The water was perfect.' Skip the riverbank if there is a flash-flood watch.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.96 from 148 reviews, newest August 2026 (six from August 2026). Hipcamp: Casa Topo 100% (5 reviews), Casa Avecita 100% (19). Families keep praising the views, the river, the dark sky and a very responsive host (Angela).
highlights: Ramp entry, single-level, parking right next to the house
Private riverfront on the Medina River, which you can drive down to
Whole property can be rented for a big family group
Central AC, a well-stocked kitchen, fire pit and pickleball court
places.red_flags: Other groups (campers, RVs, the other house) may be on the 8 acres unless you rent the whole property, and Airbnb notes 'Some spaces are shared'. The host warns that neighbors along the river sometimes play loud music. Neither bath has a walk-in or roll-in shower (both have tubs). Casa Avecita is not grandma-friendly ('Must climb stairs').
sources: Airbnb StaysPdpReviewsQuery (148 reviews) and StaysPdpBookItQuery prices for listing 52324171, pulled 9/24/2026

places.name: Sunset Ranch @ Medina Lake (Ranch House + Log House + Cabin; can be booked as one 3-house listing)
places.price_note: Airbnb prices for 8 adults, all fees included, before taxes, checked 9/24/2026. The 3-house listing (Airbnb 42707815) is a flat $565/night ($1,130 for 2 nights) on Oct 16-18, Oct 20-22, Nov 3-5 and Nov 6-8, and is booked for Dec 4-6. The Ranch House alone (Airbnb 32862159) is $617.50/night ($1,235 for 2 nights) on the same dates. Oddly, the whole ranch prices lower than the Ranch House alone, so confirm the price with the host (Sarah) before booking. Direct booking runs through ResNexus from sunsetflyinranch.com, where rates only show after picking dates. Booking direct is pitched as including access to Sunset Resort on the lake. Lake access at Sunset Resort otherwise costs a small fee ('($)').
places.group_note: The 3-house listing sleeps up to 22 (8BR, 5 baths), and with it 'you will be the only guests on our ranch.' The Ranch House (5BR/3BA, 3,000+ sq ft) sleeps 12 on its own. The Log House (2BR/1BA) and the studio Cabin sit about 150 ft apart, but the Ranch House is about 1/3 mile down the same driveway. A 2020 reviewer warned the houses are 'NOT within casual walking distance' of each other, so plan to drive between them. Put grandma in the Ranch House.
places.scenery_what: From the Ranch House's covered back patio you see Medina Lake and the dam over a big yard. The Log House patio is sold on 'views for miles' and sunsets. It is a 55-acre working longhorn ranch with deer and birds. The house is not on the water. The lake was 28.8% full on 9/24/2026 (TWDB), up from 5.9% a year earlier, so there is noticeably more water in view now than in recent drought years.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. You enter the Ranch House through a coded side door into the game room. Airbnb flags both listings 'Single level home' / 'No stairs in home'.
places.access_detail: Ranch House listing: 'Plenty of parking and yard to play in', behind electric gates. You enter 'via a code on the side door lock into the game room'. Airbnb lists it as a single-level home with central AC and central heating. The 'newly remodeled master bathroom features an oversized walk in shower, soaker tub and a double vanity', which is the best shower setup for grandma on this list after the hotel. The other baths are tub/shower combos. The exact distance from parking to the door and the number of entry steps are not stated.
places.flood_note: The houses sit up on a ranch above the Medina Lake dam, not in a river floodplain. No 2025 flood impact was found. Lake level changes the view (28.8% full as of 9/24/2026).
places.review_signal: The Ranch House has 4.98 from 51 Airbnb reviews, latest March 2026 and September 2025. Reviews repeatedly say 'Beautiful view' and 'breath taking view of the lake'. The combined 3-house listing is 5.0 but has only 10 reviews, the last in August 2021, so it rarely gets booked as a bundle.
highlights: The whole ranch is yours (up to 22 people) with no other guests
Walk-in shower in the Ranch House master bath
Covered back patio with a lake and dam view, fire pit and longhorns
Closest countryside option to SA (about 55 min)
places.red_flags: Not on the water: lake access is a 5-minute drive to Sunset Resort, for a fee. The houses are about 1/3 mile apart, so plan to drive between them. A 2020 review said the entry road needs work. There are 2 automatic gates, and longhorns roam free. Confirm the combined-listing price, since it is oddly lower than the Ranch House alone. No Ranch House listing photo shows the entry steps.
sources: Airbnb reviews and BookIt prices for 42707815 and 32862159, pulled 9/24/2026

places.name: The Lucky Dip (Private Medina River Retreat)
places.price_note: Airbnb prices for 8 adults, all fees included, before taxes, checked 9/24/2026. Oct 16-18: $471.20 total ($235.60/night, marked down from $642). Nov 3-5 and Nov 6-8: $563 ($281.50/night). Dec 4-6: $609 ($304.50/night). Oct 20-22 is not available. A refundable option runs about $36-46 more per stay. This is the cheapest whole house on the list.
places.group_note: 3BR/3BA and sleeps 10, and every bedroom has its own bathroom. It is one house on 4 gated acres, and there is room inside the gate to park RVs and trailers, so extra family could bring an RV. Reviewers mention 2 families with 7 kids, and a 'multi-generation crew' with grandparents.
places.scenery_what: The front porch has swings and looks over a pasture with deer. The back deck and living room look out on 'TX Hill Country and River', meaning a park-like lawn, a huge pecan and the Medina River with cypress trees about 150 yards away, and sunsets over rolling hills. Reviews keep saying 'the view was stunning'.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown for the front porch. Airbnb flags 'Single level home' / 'No stairs in home'. The steep stairs are only the optional route down to the river.
places.access_detail: The listing says 'Pull through the front gate and park directly in front of house.' It is single-level inside with 3 bedrooms, each with a private bath. Airbnb lists central AC, a window AC unit and central heat. A Sep 2026 reviewer said the house 'was nice and cool even during the heat of the day.' The river is 150 yards away 'by taking the staircase immediately off the backdeck', and a 2023 reviewer said those 'Stairs down to river are steep and wouldn't recommend for anyone with issues climbing', but you can 'drive down the private gravel drive which leads directly to the rivers edge.' Whether there is a walk-in shower is unknown.
places.flood_note: The house sits up above the Medina River (the back-deck stairs go down to the river, which is 150 yards away), and the river access is on a floodplain bank. There are no Airbnb reviews between January 2025 and September 8, 2026, and the reason is unknown. It could be host use, repairs, or effects of the July 2025 floods, so ask the host. The same host (John Paul) is still listed, and the latest review is positive.
places.review_signal: Airbnb 4.88 from 112 reviews. Latest is Sept 8, 2026 (5 stars); the one before is January 2025. Older reviews praise the views, porches and 'each bedroom had its own bathroom'. There were a few 3-star reviews in 2024 about maintenance.
highlights: Park right at the front door, single-level, a private bath for every bedroom
Cheapest whole house here (about $236-305/night with fees)
Porch swing and back-deck river and hill views
Private gravel drive down to the river's edge
places.red_flags: There are no reviews from January 2025 to September 2026, so ask why. 2024 reviews reported some rooms running hot while the master was cold, a fridge that was not cold, and kitchen flooring lifting ('wood lifting or wood caving in'). The Sep 2026 review sounds like this was fixed, but confirm. The stairs to the river are steep, so grandma should ride down the gravel drive. The river bottom is slick rock (the host recommends water shoes), and the river has run low in droughts.
sources: Airbnb reviews (112) and BookIt prices for listing 52114075, pulled 9/24/2026

places.name: Signia by Hilton La Cantera Resort & Spa (book a 'Hill Country View' room; there is a mobility villa with a roll-in shower)
places.town: San Antonio (16641 La Cantera Pkwy, far NW side)
places.price_note: Google Hotels base nightly rates, checked 9/24/2026. The 'Deluxe Room (Hill Country View)' was $434-435 on Nov 6-8 and Nov 10 and $650 on Oct 16-18. Mobility rooms: 'Deluxe Room, 1 King or 2 Queen (Mobility, Roll-In Shower)' from $409 (Nov 6-8). 'Villa, 2 Queen Beds (Mobility, Roll-In Shower)' was $507 (Nov 10) to $1,018 (Oct 16-18). Taxes and fees add about 18% (on Sep 28 the official site showed $645 base and $762 total). Some nights spike: the cheapest room on Oct 20-21 was $879/night. Parking costs extra (amount not confirmed, since the Hilton site blocked automated access). Club rooms include valet parking. Check-in 4pm, check-out 11am.
places.group_note: A large resort: book several rooms. Deluxe rooms have 2 queens, sleeping 4. Villas and suites are bigger. Everyone is under one roof with 6 restaurants, 5 pools and a spa. Separate rooms, not one shared house.
places.scenery_what: Hill Country View rooms look out over the golf course and wooded hills of NW San Antonio from a hilltop resort, and the restaurant advertises 'panoramic Hill Country views'. It is a pretty resort setting, but you are looking out a hotel window or balcony, not stepping out a cabin door, and the city is nearby.
places.steps_to_enter: Elevator and accessible entry. Google lists 'Accessible', 'Accessible parking', 'Accessible elevator' and 'Accessible pool'.
places.access_detail: Google Hotels room offers include 'Deluxe Room, 1 King Bed (Mobility, Roll-In Shower)', 'Deluxe Room, 2 Queen Beds (Mobility, Roll-In Shower)', 'Villa, 2 Queen Beds (Mobility, Roll-In Shower)' and 'Villa, 1 King Bed (Mobility, Roll-In Shower, Suite)'. Amenities list self and valet parking, accessible parking and elevator, and AC. The mobility rooms are not sold as 'Hill Country View', so ask the hotel whether you can get both. The walking distance from valet or parking to the room was not verified, and on a sprawling resort it could be long, so ask for a wheelchair or a room near the elevator. Google's review summary mentions a 'convenient shuttle service'.
places.flood_note: Hilltop resort, no river floodplain. No 2025 flood impact.
places.review_signal: Google 4.5 from 4,723 reviews, plus 7,315 reviews on other travel sites. Recent Google themes are pools, spa, fitness and 'beautiful views'. 57 Google reviews are tagged 'Accessibility', but their text was not readable in the fetch.
highlights: Roll-in-shower mobility rooms and villas, elevators, valet
Only 25 min from downtown SA, easy for a one-night splurge
5 pools, spa, restaurants on site, and nobody has to cook
Hill Country View rooms over the golf course hills
places.red_flags: The views are from a hotel room, not a cabin porch. Prices jump a lot on some dates (the cheapest room on Oct 20-21 was $879), plus about 18% in taxes and fees. There is a parking fee (amount unconfirmed) and possibly a resort fee. It is a big resort, so expect possible long hallway walks.
sources: https://www.lacanteraresort.com/ (301 redirect to the Hilton page)

places.name: Dixie Dude Ranch
places.price_note: Official 2026 rates, all-inclusive (lodging, 3 meals a day except Sunday dinner, 2 horseback rides a day, pool, fishing, evening entertainment). Priced per person per night: adults $190 each when two or more share a room, or $207 alone. Kids 13-16 $150, 6-12 $100, 2-5 $80, under 2 free. Per room that means 2 adults = $380/night and 4 adults = $760/night. Deluxe cabins are +10%, and Bunkhouse rooms are $5 per person less. Groups of 15 or more: adult double $185/day, kids $5/day less. Weekly adult double $1,295. Add 8.72% tax and a suggested 10% tip (optional). 2-night minimum (3 on Memorial and Labor Day weekends), no Sunday check-ins, deposit of one day's stay, full refund if you cancel 30+ days out. 4% discount for cash. There is no online availability calendar: call 830-796-7771.
places.group_note: 19 units (duplex cabins, cottages, lodge rooms, a two-story four-plex Bunkhouse), about 55 guests total. Most are family rooms with 2 or more beds, and Google says some cabins sleep up to 10. A family can take several units, and a group of 15 or more gets the group rate. Room requests are 'noted but not guaranteed.'
places.scenery_what: A 725-acre working ranch with longhorns, goats and horses. The site promises 'fine vistas of spectacular Texas Hill Country', sunsets and stargazing. From the rooms you see ranch grounds, pasture, the corral and the pool. Big views mostly come from trail rides.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. Skip the two-story Bunkhouse (Rope'n and Bunk'n are on its top floor).
places.access_detail: The official FAQ says 'All rooms/cabins are private with private bathrooms including tub and shower or shower stall', and the rooms have 'air conditioning, vented heat'. The Jan 2026 ranch map shows Rooms #2 and #3 (a suite) attached to the Lodge/Headquarters where meals are served, and the Casita duplex (#4/#5) and Stirrup nearby. Those are the rooms to request for grandma. Parking symbols on the map sit near the lodge and cabins, but distances, steps and ADA status are not stated. Paths are ranch grounds. Late arrivals get an unlocked room and a map.
places.flood_note: Not riverfront (fishing is in a pond). The official site shows normal 2026 operations ('89th year'), and no July 2025 flood impact was found.
places.review_signal: Google 4.8 from 375 reviews. Recent reviews rave about the family-style food, gentle horses and staff who 'treat you like family'. One review notes the accommodations are basic ('fine').
highlights: All meals and activities included, so nobody cooks
Lodge rooms attached to the dining hall, which is best for grandma
Every room has a private bath and AC
Grandma can relax on the porch while everyone else rides
places.red_flags: 'Most cell phones display No Service', with a landline and Wi-Fi only at the main lodge. You have to call to book, and room requests are not guaranteed. Standard rooms have no TV, and the 1940s-50s cabins are renovated but rustic. Per-person pricing adds up fast for a big family. No Sunday check-in and a 2-night minimum.

places.name: Hill Country State Natural Area - Group Lodge (1930s ranch house)
places.town: Bandera area (10600 Bandera Creek Rd, Hill Country State Natural Area)
places.price_note: $300/night for the whole lodge, plus the park's daily entrance fee ($6 per adult, children 12 and under free). Reservations by phone only at (512) 389-8920. No minimum stay is posted. No linens or cooking gear are provided, and you clean the lodge before leaving.
places.group_note: The whole house is yours: 4 bedrooms (2 queens + 5 twins) with beds for 9, up to 12 with cots. Up to 30 people total can use the site, including tents outside, and it has 5 water and electric RV hookups. That makes it the best fit here for a large extended family on a budget.
places.scenery_what: A white 1930s farmhouse on a mowed lawn under big pecan trees, with pasture, barns and corrals around it and West Verde Creek nearby (per the park map). The rugged canyons and overlooks are out on the trails, not visible from the porch. It feels quiet, ranchy and dark at night.
places.steps_to_enter: The TPWD exterior photo appears to show a slightly raised front porch with about 2-3 steps. Not confirmed, and no ramp is visible.
places.access_detail: TPWD lists an 'A/C unit' and 'Heater', '1.5 bathrooms' with a shower, and a full kitchen (fridge, stove and oven). The RV hookups at the lodge suggest you can drive right up, but parking distance and ADA status are not stated. The park is primitive: 'We do not have a park store, so bring everything you will need.' A TPWD alert from July 26, 2026 says 'road conditions are rough in some areas leading into the park.' The 1.5 baths are shared by the whole group inside the house.
places.flood_note: The park map places the lodge in the park's northwest area near West Verde Creek. No lodge flood damage from 2025 was found. As of the 7/26/2026 alert the whole park is open, but some access roads are rough. An 8/28/2026 burn ban means no wood or charcoal fires (propane stoves only), so the fire ring is off-limits for now.
places.review_signal: No lodge-specific reviews were found. TPWD gallery file names ('group-lodge-after') suggest a recent renovation.
highlights: Whole ranch house plus lawn for up to 30 people for $300/night
Room for tents and 5 RV hookups for overflow family
Very dark skies and a quiet state natural area
AC, a full kitchen and a shower
places.red_flags: Bring your own linens, towels, pots and dishes, and clean before you leave. There are only 1.5 baths for up to 12 people, and probably a porch step or two. Roads into the park are rough (TPWD alert 7/26/2026), and a burn ban is on (8/28/2026). It is the farthest from SA (about 85 min), with no store in the park.

places.name: Vintage Villas Hotel & Events
places.town: Austin (4209 Eck Ln, Hudson Bend, on a bluff over the Arkansas Bend of Lake Travis)
places.price_note: I pulled these prices from the hotel's own booking system (iqwebbook VVTX738) on 9/24/26. The Best Available Rate is $149 on most Sun-Thu nights from October to November 2026. Fri/Sat run $189-249: Oct 2-3 and Oct 9-10 are $209, Oct 16 is $249, Oct 17 is $189, Oct 30-31 is $189 and Nov 13-14 is $199. Some Mon-Wed dates in Nov and Dec jump to $299 (Nov 2-4, 9, 16-18, 23-24, Dec 2 and Dec 5), probably because events are booked. Sat Oct 24 and Nov 25-26 cannot be booked online, which likely means a wedding buyout. The 3 suites are $349 and show sold out online. The booking screen adds only a '6% Occupancy Tax', with no deposit, no resort fee and no minimum stay. Third-party sites on Google Hotels are cheaper: $75 base for Dec 20-21 (Super.com), $85 for King or 2-Queen on Hotels.com, $127 for Sep 28-29, and the finder saw $88 Sun-Tue and $134 Fri-Sun in mid-October. Breakfast is unclear: Google amenities list it as an 'extra charge', but a review says it is free. Ask when booking. No buyout price is published; ask events sales at 512-266-9333.
places.group_note: There are 44 rooms spread over 3 villa buildings: South Texas has 8, Central Texas 17 and East Texas 15. The booking system lists 21 rooms with 2 queens (up to 4 people), 16 kings with a private balcony or patio (up to 4), 3 queens, 1 ADA queen (up to 2) and 3 suites. The site says some rooms adjoin, and each villa has its own lobby, so a family can book several rooms next to each other in one villa. On most weeknights 2-Queen and King rooms showed as available. Weekends are often taken by weddings.
places.scenery_what: The hotel sits on a bluff above the Arkansas Bend of Lake Travis. The official site says every room has 'beautiful lake views', and king rooms have large private balconies looking at the lake. Google review highlights mention the sunset (14 times) and the lake (62 times), for example 'the view from the balcony is breathtaking'. The ground is event lawns and an arbor, not open wilderness. Other buildings and wedding guests are around. The one ADA room has no balcony (hasBalcony=false in the booking data), and its view is not described.
places.access_detail: The hotel does have one real ADA room. Its booking-system entry reads 'Single Queen Bedroom on the ground floor with roll in shower. ADA compliant.' It is 336 sq ft, sleeps 2, has no balcony, and the system flags it isAccessibleAda=true with numberOfRooms=1. Online it showed SOLD OUT on every date I checked from Sep 27 to Dec 5 2026, so it is either held back or already booked. Call 512-266-9333 to get it. Google lists the hotel as 'Accessible' with 'Accessible parking', free parking and air conditioning. Heat is not listed separately and should be the normal hotel system, but that is not confirmed. No elevator is mentioned anywhere. Suites are described as '2nd floor' and 'third floor', so the buildings have several stories and standard rooms may need stairs. On Google, 17 reviews mention accessibility: 71% unfavorable, 12% positive. 44% of bathroom mentions are unfavorable. Google's review summary also says 'half of the venue's air conditioning was not functioning' during one stay. The accessibility statement on the website covers only the website itself, not the building. How far the car parks from the ADA room is unknown.
places.steps_to_enter: The ADA Queen is on the ground floor and marked ADA compliant, so it should need no steps, though no one has independently confirmed that. The other rooms are on floors 1-3. Whether there is an elevator is unknown.
places.flood_note: The hotel is on a bluff high above Lake Travis, not down in a river floodplain. The official site and live booking system show it operating normally, and none of the sources I checked mention any damage from the July 2025 floods.
places.review_signal: Google gives it 4.5 from 663 reviews, and Tripadvisor 4.1 from 253 (shown on Google). Guests praise the lake views, sunsets and breakfast buffet. Complaints: beds and value ('motel 6... nicer bed'), 56% unfavorable on sleep, 71% unfavorable on accessibility, 44% unfavorable on bathrooms, and one report of AC out in half the venue. Google rates it a 2-star hotel with no pool, gym or spa.
highlights: The one ADA room is on the ground floor with a roll-in shower, but it has to be booked by phone
King rooms have large private lake-view balconies, which mom or the family could take
Direct rate is $149 on most weeknights in fall 2026 and about $85-134 on third-party sites
44 rooms, some adjoining, so the whole family can stay in one building
About 6 minutes to Mansfield Dam Park and about 35 minutes from downtown Austin
places.red_flags: There is only one ADA room and it cannot be booked online. Accessibility reviews are mostly negative. No elevator is mentioned. One stay reported AC out in half the building. It is a busy wedding venue on weekends (Oct 24 blocked). Rooms are antique-style and dated. It is a 2-star hotel with no pool. Breakfast may cost extra. Some weeknights jump to $299.
sources: https://us01.iqwebbook.com/VVTX738/ (official booking engine; api/roomtype/getall, /search and /ratecalendar queried Sep 24 2026)
OSRM routing (router.project-osrm.org): downtown SA 98 mi / 118 min, downtown Austin 20 mi / 34 min

places.name: Shaffer Bend Recreation Area - AMANI safari tent (LCRA)
places.kind: glamping tent (single safari tent in a public LCRA park)
places.town: Marble Falls area (706 CR 343A, Smithwick, on upper Lake Travis about 10 mi east of Marble Falls)
places.price_note: LCRA's park page says 'Starting at $349' a night. I could not get exact 2026 nightly or weekend rates from the LCRA/Campspot booking system: the page needs JavaScript and showed '0 Campsites Available' when loaded without dates. Pets cost an extra $50 (LCRA FAQ). The park entrance fee is $5 per adult, $2 for seniors 65+ or disabled visitors, and free for kids 12 and under; whether overnight guests also pay it is not stated. Cancellation: 30+ days before arrival gets a full refund minus transaction fees, 29-8 days gets 50%, and 7 days or less gets nothing. Minimum nights, taxes and booking fees are not stated.
places.group_note: There is only one AMANI tent, and it sleeps 2. The rest of the park is 23 primitive campsites (up to 8 people each, from $25) and 1 large group site (up to 16, from $35). Those sites have a picnic table, grill and fire ring, with flushing and non-flushing restrooms nearby. They sit by the lake, roughly half a mile and about 150 ft lower than AMANI on the park map. So AMANI could house grandma and one person, but the rest of the family would be tent camping far away. It does not work as a whole-family stay.
places.scenery_what: LCRA calls it 'Hilltop Glamping' and says 'If Hill Country views are your desire, then you've come to the right place.' On the park map, AMANI is the only structure on a hilltop at about 830-840 ft, in the middle of a 508-acre park with a Scenic Overlook just to the north. Lake Travis is about 0.5 mi south and roughly 150 ft below, so whether you can see the lake from the tent is unknown. There are no neighbors, and the site has a private heated cowboy pool. No LCRA text or review I found says what you actually see from the door.
places.access_detail: Confirmed by LCRA: 'Climate controlled', 'Private restroom with shower', a kitchenette, and a 'Heated Cowboy Pool and gas grill'. The page says 'climate controlled' but does not name AC and heat separately. It does not say whether the bathroom is inside the tent or in a separate private building. It gives nothing on parking, steps or ADA status. The official park map (SBRA-Map-1.14.2026.pdf) puts the AMANI icon about 700 ft west of the nearest mapped park road and about 1,400 ft from the entrance, with no driveway drawn to it. A drive-up spur may still exist that the map leaves out. The park map rules say 'Only authorized vehicles... must remain on designated roads and parking areas.' A 2019 Campendium review says the 'Park road is a mixture of gravel and blacktop and is rough in some spots.' I found no reviews of AMANI itself on Campendium, Google Hotels or the LCRA site. Call 512-473-3366 and ask whether you can drive and park at the tent, and how many steps lead up to it.
places.steps_to_enter: Unknown. LCRA does not say whether the tent sits on a raised deck or how many steps it has.
places.flood_note: On the LCRA map the tent sits at about 830-840 ft, well above Lake Travis's full level of about 681 ft, so the tent itself is out of the floodplain. The lakeside campsites (about 690-710 ft) are on the upper Lake Travis stretch of the Colorado River, below Starcke Dam, which passed the July 2025 Llano River floodwater downstream. Whether that flood affected the park is unconfirmed; I found no LCRA notice either way. As of 9/24/26 the park page shows no closure or flood alert, only a Burnet County burn ban. A 2019 review mentions the park 'still recovering from the flood' (the 2018 flood).
places.review_signal: I found no reviews of AMANI itself. The only park review I found was 4.0 on Campendium (1 review, 2019), which scored access 3/5 and noted rough gravel roads and about 10 miles to the nearest grocery store. It is not listed on Google Hotels.
highlights: Private bathroom with shower, climate controlled, kitchenette
Private heated cowboy pool and gas grill
Only unit on a hilltop in a 508-acre park, with no neighbors
Run by LCRA, a public agency, and booked directly through LCRA
Seniors pay a discounted $2 day entry
places.red_flags: It is one tent for 2 people, so it cannot house the family. Car-to-tent access is not documented, and the park map shows the tent about 700 ft from the nearest mapped road. Park roads are gravel and rough in spots. No reviews exist for AMANI. The price is only 'starting at $349' and could not be checked by date. The park is about 10 miles from a grocery store. A burn ban is in effect. The park is currently recruiting a park host, so staff may not always be on site. I could not confirm the booking system shows open dates.
sources: OSRM routing (router.project-osrm.org): downtown SA about 97 mi, and about 103 min to Marble Falls plus about 15-20 min on RM 1431/CR 343A

sections.heading: Best time to go
points: Short answer for a trip with grandma: late October through mid-December is best, then mid-March through April. Skip June to mid-September because of heat and summer flash floods. December to February works, but it's cold and wet, so book only heated, hard-sided units.

San Antonio average high/low in F (1991-2020 normals): Sep 90/70, Oct 82/60, Nov 72/50, Dec 65/42, Jan 63/41, Feb 68/45, Mar 74/52, Apr 80/58, May 87/66, Jun 92/73, Jul 95/75, Aug 96/75. Hill Country towns get colder at night than SA. (currentresults.com/Weather/Texas/Places/san-antonio-temperatures-by-month-average.php)

Freezes: the first freeze usually comes Oct 31 - Nov 6 around Kerrville, Fredericksburg, Leakey and Bandera, but only around Dec 1 in Austin. A tent or dome out west can get freezing nights from early November, so ask about heat as well as AC. (ksat.com, kxan.com first-freeze pieces)

THIS winter will probably be wetter and cooler than normal. On Sept 10, 2026, NOAA's Climate Prediction Center put the odds of a very strong El Nino through winter 2026-27 above 90%. In past El Nino years, fall and winter in South-Central Texas were about 30-40% wetter and a bit cooler, and San Antonio's December rain roughly doubled. Expect more rainy weekends, more flood-watch days near rivers and chillier nights. Book with flexible cancellation. (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov ENSO discussion; tpr.org; foxsanantonio.com)

Now through early October 2026: still hot (highs near 90) and every target county is under a burn ban. Crowd and price spikes: Oct 2-4 (Fredericksburg Oktoberfest plus ACL weekend 1), Oct 9-11 (ACL weekend 2), Oct 22-25 (F1 US Grand Prix in Austin AND Fredericksburg Food & Wine Fest).

November is the best month overall. Lost Maples fall color usually peaks mid-November. In 2025, TPWD started foliage reports Oct 9, weekends sold out, and the park closes when the lots fill. Wurstfest runs Nov 6-15. Daylight saving ends Nov 1, so it's dark by about 6pm. Thanksgiving week (Nov 26) costs more.

December to early January is holiday-lights season: Santa's Ranch drive-thru, Fredericksburg Marktplatz, Johnson City, Marble Falls and the SA River Walk. Weeknights are calm. Weekends and Christmas to New Year are busy. Cedar fever (mountain cedar pollen) starts mid-Nov to Dec, peaks around mid-January and tapers by late February. That matters if grandma has allergies or breathing issues.
January to February is the cheapest and quietest time, but it has the highest risk of hard freezes and ice. Only book heated cabins, houses or hotels for her.
March 2027: spring break is mid-March (check the local school districts) and SXSW runs Mar 15-21, 2027, so Austin prices jump. Easter is Mar 28, 2027.

April is the best-looking month. Bluebonnets usually peak from late March to mid-April, with the best odds in the first two weeks of April. Wildflower weekends in Burnet, Marble Falls, Fredericksburg and Llano book up early. The Burnet Bluebonnet Festival (a promoter lists Apr 9-11, 2027; the official site isn't updated yet) and Fiesta San Antonio (Apr 15-25, 2027) spike prices.

May to September: May averages 87 and July-August reach the mid-90s. Both deadly floods happened in July: July 4, 2025 and July 16-17, 2026. Not recommended for glamping with grandma unless she stays in a solid AC cabin or hotel.

sections.heading: Flood safety
points: What happened: on July 4, 2025, the Guadalupe at Hunt rose about 37 ft, the worst flood on record there. 136+ people died, 117 of them in Kerr County, including at Camp Mystic. Kerrville campgrounds like HTR TX Hill Country and Blue Oak RV Park were hit. The Llano (it hit 26.5 ft at Llano), San Gabriel and Lampasas rivers and creeks around Lake Travis also flooded. Travis County had 10 deaths and Burnet County 5. (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_2025_Central_Texas_floods; ksat.com)

It happened again on July 16-17, 2026, in Kerr, Kendall, Uvalde and Zavala counties (Guadalupe River, Quinlan Creek, West Goat Creek). At least 2 people died and Buckhorn Lake Resort RV Park near Kerrville was badly damaged. Any riverside unit in Kerr, Kendall, Real, Uvalde or Bandera counties carries real flood risk. (ksat.com, 2026-07-18)

What changed in the law: SB 1 (Heaven's 27 Camp Safety Act) and HB 1 were signed Sept 5, 2025. Youth camps can no longer be licensed with cabins in river floodplains, and camps and campgrounds must have weather radios, emergency PA systems and flood evacuation plans. SB 3 created a $50M grant fund for warning sirens and SB 5 put $28M into forecasting. None of this covers a private Airbnb or VRBO on the river, so you have to ask the host. (kut.org 2025-09-04; texastribune.org)

Sirens: the Kerr County river authority installed 6 new sirens, and 3 were used in July 2026. River Sentry installed 104 private sirens along the Guadalupe near RV parks and camps, and Comfort added sirens. Reporting from July 2026 said Kerr County's plan for when to sound the sirens was still being worked out, so don't count on sirens alone. (kut.org 2026-07-02; ksat.com)

How to check a place before booking: (1) FEMA Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov): enter the address and see if it's in a Zone A/AE floodplain or the floodway. (2) Texas Flood Information Viewer (map.texasflood.org, run by TWDB): live river gauges plus state floodplain maps. (3) water.noaa.gov: find the nearest river gauge and its flood stages. (4) Satellite view: a unit on the flat bottom next to the river with no hill behind it is the risky one. You want a bluff or hillside well above the water.

Alerts during the trip: turn on Emergency Alerts on every phone. After a CodeRED cyber-incident outage, Kerr County told residents to rely on these phone alerts (IPAWS/WEA). Also add the CodeRED Public Alerts app (it alerts based on where you are). For Travis, Hays, Blanco, Burnet, Llano and Williamson counties, register at WarnCentralTexas.org. Pack a NOAA weather radio. ATXfloods.com shows closed low-water crossings around Austin, and DriveTexas.org shows road closures statewide.

Rules for a group with grandma: when a Flood WATCH is issued, move her to high ground right away. Don't wait for the WARNING, because she can't move fast at 2am. Never drive into water over a road (Turn Around Don't Drown). When you arrive, drive the way out and note any low-water crossings. Pick a unit up the hill with a river view over one that's 'right on the water'. Flash floods here are most common in spring and in September to November, and this El Nino fall and winter leans wet.

sections.heading: Burn bans + fire pits
points: Right now: as of Sept 24, 2026, all of these counties have a burn ban: Bexar, Comal, Hays, Travis, Burnet, Llano, Blanco, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Bandera, Real, Uvalde, Guadalupe and Williamson. (burnbantexas.com, which mirrors Texas A&M Forest Service data)

The official place to check is the Texas A&M Forest Service county burn ban map at tfsweb.tamu.edu (Wildfire and Other Disasters > Burn Bans & Information). Each county's judge or commissioners court sets its own ban and can lift it after rain. Check the week of the trip and again when you arrive.

What a ban usually means: no wood fires in fire pits, fire rings or chimineas. Most county orders still allow cooking on propane or natural-gas grills or other enclosed cooking devices, but the wording varies by county, so read that county's order. Breaking a ban is a Class C misdemeanor with a fine of up to $500. (Texas Local Gov't Code 352.081; county.org)

State parks: Guadalupe River SP (since Aug 21, 2026) and Pedernales Falls SP (since Aug 25, 2026) allow no wood or charcoal, only propane stoves. Garner SP (since Sept 17, 2026) allows no wood fires, but charcoal and gas stoves are OK. (tpwd.texas.gov park alert pages)

For the fire-pit vibe, ask the host if the fire pit runs on propane. Gas fire tables are often still allowed, but get the host to confirm under the current county order. Otherwise plan on string lights, lanterns and a gas grill. A wet El Nino fall may lift the bans by November, but don't count on it.

sections.heading: Booking tips
points: Dates to avoid or book very early: Oct 2-4 (Oktoberfest + ACL weekend 1), Oct 9-11 (ACL weekend 2), Oct 22-25 (F1 + Fredericksburg Food & Wine), Nov 6-15 (Wurstfest, New Braunfels), Thanksgiving weekend Nov 26-29, Dec 19 - Jan 3, mid-March spring break, SXSW Mar 15-21 2027 (Austin), April bluebonnet weekends, and Fiesta Apr 15-25 2027 (SA).
Go Sunday to Thursday if you can. Hill Country rentals and glamping sites are usually cheaper midweek, and many have 2-night weekend minimums (often 3 on holidays). Check each listing.

Lead time: the few truly accessible units (ground level, parking at the door, private bath) go first. For October-November weekends and holiday-lights weekends, book as soon as dates are set. Lost Maples day passes open 30 days ahead and sell out on peak weekends.

Airbnb fees: Airbnb has moved nearly all US hosts to a ~15.5% fee the host pays, so the listed price is close to all-in. Some listings may still add the old guest service fee of 14.1-16.5%. Compare final totals with cleaning fee and taxes, not nightly rates. Vrbo still adds a guest fee of about 6-15%. Hipcamp adds a variable guest fee (minimum $3), shown at checkout. (airbnb.com/help/article/1857; vrbo help; support.hipcamp.com)
Taxes: Texas hotel occupancy tax is 6% state plus local tax, up to about 17% combined depending on the city. Airbnb collects it for you, and direct bookings charge it too.

Cancellation: Airbnb's standard policies are Flexible (full refund up to 24h before), Moderate (5 days), Limited (14 days) and Firm (full refund 30+ days out, 50% at 7-30 days, nothing inside 7 days). Bookings made 7+ days ahead get 24 hours to cancel free. With an elderly guest and a wet winter, choose Flexible or Moderate and skip the non-refundable discount. Ask each host what happens if a flood watch or burn ban hits.

Accessibility filters: Airbnb's accessibility filter (step-free entrance, step-free path to the bathroom, grab bars, accessible parking) narrows the list. Hosts report these themselves, so still ask for photos or a video of the path. Hotels and resorts must have ADA rooms; ask for the exact type (roll-in shower or tub with grab bars) and get it in writing.

Splitting cost: Airbnb's old split-payment option isn't generally available anymore, so one person books and everyone else pays them back. Use Splitwise or a shared sheet: lodging split by unit or by adult, food by household. Collect deposits BEFORE booking so the person who booked isn't stuck if someone drops out, and have everyone commit before the free-cancellation window closes.

Book direct when you can. Many glamping resorts and small lodges also take bookings on their own sites, which can skip platform fees and makes it easier to get the most accessible unit, closest to parking, held for grandma.
Look at trip insurance that covers cancelling because a family member gets sick, and read what it says about weather.

sections.heading: Heat + health for an elderly guest
points: Heat: older adults handle heat worse, feel less thirsty and often take meds that cut sweating (diuretics, sedatives, some heart and blood pressure drugs). Give her water on a schedule, not only when she's thirsty. Limit alcohol and caffeine in the heat and keep her in shade or AC midday. If she gets dizzy, confused, stops sweating or faints, get her into AC, cool her with water and call 911. (nia.nih.gov hot weather safety for older adults)

Glamping AC reality: canvas tents and vinyl domes soak up sun. Ask what cools the unit. A ducted mini-split is best; a portable or window unit in a canvas tent may not keep it comfortable on a 95F+ afternoon. Also ask about shade and backup power. From June to September, put grandma in a hard-sided cabin, tiny home or hotel room even if the rest of the family glamps.

Cold nights (Nov-Feb): ask what heats the unit. There should be no unvented propane heater inside a tent, and there should be a working CO detector. An electric blanket or heated mattress pad helps if the power supply is solid.

Night bathroom trips are the biggest fall risk. Insist on a private in-unit bathroom, a lit path from bed to toilet, motion nightlights and a normal-height bed (no floor platform, loft or bunk). If the only bathroom is a separate bathhouse, bring a bedside commode or urinal so she never walks outside in the dark.

Ground: Hill Country paths are often caliche, gravel, decomposed granite, grass or limestone steps. Walkers and wheelchairs bog down in them and toes catch. Ask for a paved, deck or boardwalk path and handrails on every step. A rollator with big wheels or a transport chair handles gravel better than small wheels.
Dark-sky country is pitch black at night. Whoever walks with her needs a headlamp, and there should be a lantern at the door and a lit route to the car.
Allergies: cedar fever runs from mid-Nov/Dec through February, peaking around mid-January, and oak and grass pollen come in spring. Pack her usual allergy meds.
Critters: fire ants in grass, scorpions around rocks and firewood (shake out shoes), mosquitoes near water. Bring repellent and closed shoes.

Medical access: canyon areas (Frio, Lost Maples, Pedernales) often have weak cell signal and long ambulance times. Before the trip, get the unit's exact address and GPS pin, find out which carrier works there and time the drive to the nearest ER. Bring all her meds plus extra days, a written med list and insurance cards.
Water: Guadalupe River SP asked visitors (July 2026) to bring their own drinking water. Rural rentals on wells can have low water pressure or limited hot water. Bring bottled water for her.

sections.heading: Park status + closures (fall 2026 into 2027)
points: Guadalupe River SP: under a burn ban. Closed to the public Nov 20 (8pm) - Nov 24 (noon) and Jan 11-15 for permitted hunts. Prairie Trail and overflow parking closed Oct 24 from 8am-2pm. After the flood the day-use area was closed until July 2026, and the parking-lot level has reopened with limited river access. (tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/guadalupe-river/alert)

Pedernales Falls SP: the water/electric campground is closed Oct 1-31, 2026 and Jan 1 - Feb 28, 2027 for construction. The whole park closes for hunts Nov 21-24, Dec 13-17 and Jan 18-22. Weekend day passes sell out. (tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/pedernales-falls/alert)

Garner SP (Frio): the Blinn River and White Rock Cave trails are closed, there are no lifeguards, and the Scenic Overlook sidewalk is closed to walkers. Under a burn ban. (tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/garner/alert)
Lost Maples SNA: closed Jan 5-7 for a hunt, and it closes when lots fill on fall weekends. (tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/lost-maples)
South Llano River SP (Junction): as of July 2026 the shoreline under the bridge is closed, and the river has changed course and may hold debris.

Scenic drives where grandma can stay in the car: Devil's Backbone (FM 32 between Wimberley and Blanco), the Twisted Sisters ranch roads (RR 335/336/337 around Leakey and Vanderpool) and the Willow City Loop near Fredericksburg in bluebonnet season. The Willow City Loop runs through private ranch land, so stay on the road. It gets packed on April weekends.

events_2026.why: Fun outing with 450 vendors, free entry, $10 parking. Wimberley lodging is tight on market weekends. Accessibility (shuttles, surfaces) isn't listed, so bring a wheelchair or rollator.

events_2026.name: Gruene Market Days
events_2026.why: Easy grandma outing with free admission and parking and about 100 artisan vendors in historic Gruene. Weekend crowds.

events_2026.dates: Oct 22-25, 2026 (Grand Tasting on Saturday at Marktplatz)

events_2026.name: Lost Maples fall foliage
events_2026.dates: Usually peaks mid-November. TPWD posts foliage reports from about early October (2025 reports started Oct 9)
events_2026.why: Best fall color in the region, but weekends sell out and the park closes when lots are full. Reserve day passes (they open 30 days ahead). Trails are rocky and not grandma-friendly; the scenic drive in is the grandma-friendly part.

events_2026.name: Wurstfest
events_2026.why: PRICE SPIKE for New Braunfels and Gruene lodging. Admission is FREE Mon-Thu (Nov 9-12) and free after 3pm on the last Sunday. Fri/Sun $15 online, Sat $25 online, kids 12 and under free. Shuttles available.

events_2026.name: Santa's Ranch drive-thru Christmas lights
events_2026.why: BEST FOR GRANDMA: everyone stays in the car, and there are restrooms on site. $37 + tax per car. No RVs, buses or vehicles over 8 ft tall.

events_2026.name: Fredericksburg Christmas Nights of Lights
events_2026.dates: Nightly Nov 24, 2026 - Jan 5, 2027: music from 5pm, 6pm narration and lighting countdown. Not held Dec 4 (Light the Night parade) or Dec 31
events_2026.why: Short (10-minute), flat, free town-square show with a 30-ft tree and 26-ft Christmas pyramid. Easy for grandma.

events_2026.name: Ford Holiday River Parade
events_2026.why: Reserved seating along the route, with ADA tickets sold in several areas. River Walk lights stay up into early January. Thanksgiving-weekend SA prices.

events_2026.name: Dickens on Main
events_2026.dates: Friday and Saturday after Thanksgiving: Nov 27-28, 2026
events_2026.why: Holiday street fair with fake snow, carolers and Friday tree lighting. Streets close at 4pm and parking is first-come, so drop grandma off close.

events_2026.name: Johnson City Lights Spectacular + PEC Holiday Lights
events_2026.dates: 2026 dates NOT yet published. 2025 ran Nov 28 - Jan 4, dusk to midnight
events_2026.why: Free, 2M+ lights around the courthouse square and PEC grounds. The FAQ says the displays are wheelchair accessible. Saturday nights get crowded.

events_2026.name: Walkway of Lights
events_2026.dates: 2026 dates NOT yet published. 2025 ran Nov 21 - Jan 3
events_2026.why: Lights along Lake Marble Falls, $2 donation in 2025. The city took it over from the Chamber in 2026 and approved 12 new themed display areas; the ice rink is cut this year.

events_2026.name: Wassailfest
