host_questions: How many feet is it from where we park to the door, and can we pull the car right up to the unit to drop grandma off and unload?
What is the path from parking to the door made of (pavement, deck/boardwalk, gravel, caliche, grass, stone steps)? Can you send a photo or short video of the whole walk?
How many steps are there from the car to the door, and inside from the door to the bed and the bathroom? Is there a handrail on every set of steps?
Is the bathroom inside the unit and private, or a shared bathhouse? If it's a bathhouse, how far is it and is the path lit at night?
What kind of shower is it (walk-in with no curb, tub/shower combo, or outdoor)? Are there grab bars at the toilet and shower, a shower seat and a handheld showerhead?
How tall is the toilet, and how tall is the bed from the floor? Is the bed a standard frame, or a floor platform, loft, bunk or futon? Is there a bed on the ground floor?
How wide are the doorways, and is there a raised threshold? Will a walker or wheelchair fit through the door and into the bathroom?
Is there lighting from the bed to the bathroom at night (nightlights, motion lights, a lit outdoor path)?
What cools the unit (mini-split, window unit, portable) and how cool does it actually stay on a 95-100F afternoon? Is the unit shaded?
What heats the unit in winter? Is any heater vented, and is there a working carbon monoxide detector?
What happens if the power goes out? Is there a generator or backup power? (Important if she uses a CPAP, oxygen concentrator or refrigerated meds.)
Is there an outlet by the bed and a fridge for medications?
Which cell carriers work at the unit, and is there Wi-Fi good enough for Wi-Fi calling? What exact address or GPS pin should we give 911?
How far is the nearest ER, and how long does an ambulance usually take to get to you?
Is the unit in a FEMA floodplain? How many feet above the river's normal level is it? Did it flood in July 2025 or July 2026?
What is your flood plan: do you watch NWS alerts, keep a weather radio, have a siren nearby? Is there a written evacuation route to high ground that doesn't cross a low-water crossing?
If a Flood Watch or Flash Flood Warning is issued for our dates, will you move us or refund us?
Is the road in paved? Are there low-water crossings or a steep caliche driveway that a regular car can't handle, or that closes in rain?
Is the fire pit wood or propane, and is it allowed under the county's current burn ban?

Can you put our group in units next to each other, with the most accessible one closest to parking for grandma? Is there a shaded common area with real chairs (with arms and backs, not just stumps or camp stools)?
Is there a golf cart or any help getting around the property? Can we borrow a wheelchair or shower chair?
Are there animals on the property (dogs, livestock) that roam near the units and could trip her? Any events or weddings on the property our weekend (noise, parking)?
Is the water drinkable, and how much hot water is there?
Do you treat for fire ants and scorpions around the unit?
What is your cancellation policy for a family medical emergency, bad weather or a flood watch?
packing_for_grandma: All her medications plus 3 or more extra days, in a pill organizer, with a written med list and dosages, her doctors' phone numbers, and copies of her ID and insurance cards
Insulated bag or small cooler with ice packs for any refrigerated meds
Her disabled parking placard, so she gets the closest spots at events and parks
Rollator with large all-terrain wheels, or a folding transport wheelchair for gravel, grass and events. A cane with a quad tip if she uses one
A sturdy folding chair with arms and a back (not a low camp chair), plus a seat cushion
Portable shower stool and a non-slip bath mat. Suction grab bars only for balance, never to hold her full weight
Toilet seat riser. A bedside commode or urinal if the bathroom isn't right next to the bed
Battery motion-sensor nightlights for the bed-to-bathroom path, a headlamp for whoever walks with her and a lantern for the door
Closed shoes with good tread and slippers with rubber soles. No flip-flops on caliche or rock
Layers: light breathable clothes and a wide-brim hat for heat, plus a warm jacket, beanie, blanket and an electric blanket for cold nights (Nov-Feb)
Insulated water bottle, electrolyte packets and easy snacks, so she drinks on a schedule
Sunscreen, sunglasses, a cooling towel and a small battery or neck fan
Bug repellent, anti-itch cream and a reminder to shake out shoes (scorpions, fire ants)
Her allergy meds and saline spray (cedar fever mid-Nov to Feb; spring pollen)
First-aid kit, thermometer, pulse oximeter and a blood pressure cuff if she normally uses one
Hearing aid batteries or charger, spare glasses, and phone charger plus a power bank
Incontinence supplies and wet wipes if needed
Printed card with the rental's exact address and GPS pin, the nearest ER's address and phone, and family contacts
NOAA weather radio (or at least Emergency Alerts turned on in every phone's settings) for flood alerts
Earplugs and an eye mask (canvas tents are bright at dawn and let in noise)
Small bills for market parking and vendors (for example $10 parking at Wimberley Market Day)
Bottled drinking water (some rural sites and parks ask you to bring your own)

activities.title: Old Tunnel State Park bat emergence (Upper Viewing Area)
activities.what: Watch Mexican free-tailed bats pour out of an abandoned railroad tunnel at dusk from a viewing deck. The park is in Kendall County, between Comfort and Fredericksburg. The upper area holds 100 people a night.
activities.access_note: TPWD says the upper area meets ADA guidelines. Dedicated ADA parking at the trail entrance, a very short hard-packed caliche trail, a ramp with handrails up to the deck, and wheelchair-friendly picnic tables on concrete pads. The left side of the deck has a curb, not a railing. No restroom is listed at the upper area. Tickets must be bought in advance online or at 512-389-8900; there are no on-site sales. The lower area (70 people, Thu to Sun) has 1 ADA spot, a gate drop-off and an accessible portable toilet, but it sells out about 2 weeks ahead. The park is not on a river, so the floods are not an issue here.
activities.cost: $2 per person for an upper-area ticket. The TPWD page also mentions a daily entrance fee, so confirm the total when booking.
activities.best_when: Bat season runs May 1 to Oct 31, so it is still running through October 2026. For emergence times call the recorded line (866-978-2287) and arrive about an hour early.

activities.title: Stonehenge II, Ingram
activities.what: A near-scale Stonehenge replica on the Hill Country Arts Foundation grounds. While the flood-damaged campus is rebuilt, it is being used as a temporary stage for Shakespeare and other shows.
activities.access_note: FLOOD FLAG: Stonehenge II was reported undamaged in the July 2025 flood. HCAF's black box theater, offices and studios were heavily damaged and are being rebuilt with Lake Flato. Ingram flooded again on July 16, 2026. TPR (Sept 2, 2026) reports Stonehenge II is still accessible and hosting shows. Parking distance and path surface are unconfirmed; call HCAF at 830-367-5121.
activities.cost: Unknown (not listed on the HCAF site)
activities.best_when: Daytime, or a performance staged inside the stones (check hcaf.com)

activities.title: Boerne Hill Country Mile + River Road Park
activities.what: A 1.1-mile historic Main Street with 80+ shops, galleries and cafes. River Road Park is just off Main Street on Cibolo Creek, with benches and creek views.
activities.access_note: There are benches and public restrooms along the Mile. Parking is free on Main St, behind buildings and at the Visitors Center, but it gets tight during events. The Cibolo Trail has just over 3 miles of ADA-accessible paved segments near downtown. Grandma can sit on a bench or at a cafe while others browse.
activities.best_when: Weekday mornings or afternoons, avoiding event weekends

activities.title: TX-16 Bandera to Medina river drive + Love Creek Orchards
activities.what: The shady two-lane stretch of TX-16 between Bandera and Medina runs alongside the Medina River and crosses it several times. End at Love Creek Orchards' apple store, bakery and patio cafe; the orchard says Texas Monthly voted its apple pie the best in Texas.
activities.access_note: The drive itself is all from the car. Love Creek's store/bakery is open 9am to 5pm daily and the patio cafe 11am to 3pm daily (14024 TX-16 N, Medina, 830-200-0302). Ramp and parking details for the store are unconfirmed. The Medina River was not named in the flood reports I found.
activities.cost: Free drive; food priced per item
activities.best_when: Now through October while fresh apples are in (late July into October). Daylight hours.

activities.title: Haby's Alsatian Bakery, Castroville
activities.what: A classic Alsatian bakery open since 1974 in historic Castroville on US-90 west of SA: pastries, strudels, breads. A good sweet stop for anyone driving west toward Hondo or the Frio.
activities.access_note: Storefront bakery at 207 US-90 E. Parking and ramp details are unconfirmed.
activities.best_when: Mon to Sat, 5am to 7pm; closed Sundays

activities.title: FLAG: Kerrville River Trail & Louise Hays Park (currently CLOSED)
activities.what: Normally the easiest paved Guadalupe River scenery in Kerr County. Listed only as a warning not to plan around it right now.
activities.access_note: CLOSED after the July 16, 2026 Guadalupe flood. About 6 miles of trail from Guadalupe Park to Kerrville-Schreiner Park are closed, with holes several feet deep, buried trail and a washed-out parking lot. As of July 29, 2026 there was no reopening timeline. The same stretch was also hit by the July 4, 2025 flood and had only reopened in Dec 2025. Hunt, Ingram, Center Point and Comfort also flooded in July 2026 (the Comfort crest was higher than in 2025), so avoid river-based plans along the upper Guadalupe.
activities.best_when: Not currently. Check kerrvilletx.gov before any trip.

activities.title: Gruene Hall + Gruene Historic District (free daytime music)
activities.what: A historic Texas dance hall with free live music. Weekend sets run roughly 11am to 5pm, the Friday Afternoon Club 4 to 7pm, and weekday shows 6 to 9pm. Examples: Sat Sept 26, 2026 has Dan Whitaker 11am to 1pm and Bo Phillips 1 to 5pm, both free. The surrounding Gruene district has shops and restaurants.
activities.access_note: Gruene Hall publishes no accessibility information and it is an old historic building, so call ahead. Parking is in Gruene district lots and can be crowded on weekends. It is next door to the Gristmill.
activities.cost: Free for daytime shows (evening headliners are ticketed)
activities.best_when: Weekday evenings or weekend late mornings for smaller crowds

activities.title: Gristmill River Restaurant & Bar, Gruene
activities.what: A restaurant built in the ruins of an 1878 cotton gin on the bluff over the Guadalupe River. Multi-level decks and patios look over the river.
activities.access_note: Listed as wheelchair accessible, but walkways are uneven and some seats require stairs. Reviewers say river-edge seating needs stairs. Call 830-625-0684 and ask for an accessible table that still has a view. There were no flood-closure reports for Gruene in what I found.
activities.best_when: Weekday lunch or early dinner; pair it with a free set at Gruene Hall

activities.title: Meadows Center glass-bottom boat tour, Spring Lake (San Marcos)
activities.what: A guided 30-minute glass-bottom boat ride over the crystal-clear springs of Spring Lake, the headwaters of the San Marcos River. A 45-minute extended tour runs on weekends.
activities.access_note: NOT wheelchair accessible: boarding takes two steps, the historic boats cannot be modified, and wheelchairs are left dockside. An accessible boat is only being researched. The boardwalk-based Wetlands tour add-on is temporarily closed for repairs. A parking permit is required (ticket kiosk or AMP Park app). The distance from parking to the dock is unconfirmed; call 512-245-7590. Seated ride once aboard.
activities.cost: $13 adult / $11 senior 65+ / $9 kids 3 to 12; extended tour $16 / $14 / $12
activities.best_when: Daily 9:30am to 5pm with departures every 30 minutes. Buy same-day tickets at the kiosk.

activities.title: Devil's Backbone scenic drive (RR 32, Wimberley to Blanco)
activities.what: A 23-mile ridge road between the Blanco area and just south of Wimberley. The Devil's Backbone stretch has a small rest stop and pull-out at the top of the ridge (north side) with an unobstructed view across the Blanco River valley, plus the ghost-lore Devil's Backbone Tavern.
activities.access_note: The view works from the car at the pull-out. Travel guides say the rest area has benches. It is a twisting two-lane road with a steep climb; drive gently if grandma gets carsick.
activities.best_when: Late afternoon light; spring wildflowers

activities.title: The Salt Lick BBQ, Driftwood
activities.what: A famous open-pit Hill Country BBQ place under the oaks near Driftwood, and a classic family group meal.
activities.access_note: Listings report a wheelchair-accessible entrance, parking lot, restroom and seating, with wide walkways. Confirm the parking-to-table distance for grandma: 512-858-4959.
activities.best_when: Mon to Thu 11am to 9pm, Fri to Sat 11am to 10pm, Sun 11am to 9pm. Weekdays are less crowded.

activities.title: Santa's Ranch drive-thru Christmas lights, New Braunfels
activities.what: A 1+ mile drive along winding country roads through about 3 million lights and animated displays, with homemade hot chocolate and kettle corn.
activities.access_note: Guests stay in their vehicles the whole time except to use on-site restrooms, so it is ideal for grandma. Vehicles are limited to 8 ft tall and 30 ft long; no RVs, buses, limos or trailers.
activities.cost: $37 + tax per vehicle (single pass); $74 + tax season pass
activities.best_when: Nov 6, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027. Sun to Thu 6 to 10pm, Fri to Sat 6 to 11pm, open every night including holidays and rain.

activities.title: Congress Avenue Bridge bats (Statesman Bat Observation area)
activities.what: Free sunset viewing of Austin's urban bat colony flying out from under the Congress Ave bridge. The flight can last up to 45 minutes. Watch from the grassy observation area on the southeast side of the bridge.
activities.access_note: The observation area is reported wheelchair accessible. Paid parking is at the southeast end of the bridge (305 S Congress) and fills fast on clear evenings. The bridge sidewalk gets very crowded, so the grass area is better for grandma; bring a folding chair. No 2026 construction closures of the viewing area were reported.
activities.best_when: Now through October (bats are present roughly mid-March to early November; late summer to early fall is peak). Arrive before sunset.

activities.title: Capital Cruises bat-watching cruise, Lady Bird Lake
activities.what: An electric boat leaves from the Hyatt Regency dock (208 Barton Springs Rd) about 30 minutes before sunset to watch the bats emerge from the water.
activities.access_note: A 2026 reviewer said the only route from Hyatt parking to the dock was down a flight of stairs, but staff walked their wheelchair users around the construction via the hike-and-bike trail to the dock. Call ahead at 512-480-9264 to arrange this. Onboard restroom and cover are unconfirmed. For grandma, the free Statesman lawn is the simpler option.
activities.best_when: Nightly March to early November; the operator says July through Sept/Oct is best. Nov to Feb shifts to 1-hour sunset tours with few bats.

activities.title: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
activities.what: Native-plant gardens, courtyards and an arboretum in southwest Austin. A calm, shaded garden outing.
activities.access_note: Free loaner wheelchairs at the Admissions kiosk (limited, first come first served). The Central Complex, Central Gardens, Luci and Ian Family Garden, Arboretum Trail and Roadrunner Trail are wheelchair accessible. The Observation Tower and the Woodland and Savanna Meadow trails are not. Parking is limited. The Family Garden is closed Sept 21 to Oct 1, 2026 for the Fortlandia install.
activities.cost: Mon to Thu $15 adult / $12 senior 65+ / $9 youth; Fri to Sun $18 / $15 / $12. Pre-purchase encouraged; cards only.
activities.best_when: Sept to May, 9am to 5pm (last entry 4pm). Spring is peak wildflowers.

activities.title: The Oasis on Lake Travis (sunset dinner)
activities.what: A huge terraced restaurant with 40+ decks built into a cliff about 450 ft above Lake Travis, famous for its sunsets.
activities.access_note: The Oasis says it is fully handicap accessible, with elevators to all dining areas including the upper decks. It takes no reservations (first come first served), so go at least 1 hour before sunset. Parking distance is unconfirmed. Food is secondary; the view is the point.
activities.best_when: Sunset. Mon to Thu 11:30am to 8pm, Fri to 9pm, Sat to Sun 11am to 10pm.

activities.title: Mozart's Lake Austin Festival of Lights
activities.what: A holiday light and music show on the Lake Austin waterfront decks of Mozart's Coffee Roasters, with shows starting at 7pm and a lit 'Enchanted Forest'.
activities.access_note: Mozart's states the venue is NOT ADA accessible. Ramps reach the main deck and cafe during regular hours, but moving around is hard on busy nights. Reserved upper-deck tables and see-through Overlook huts give a guaranteed seat, which is better for grandma.
activities.cost: $3 general admission in 2025; reserved tables cost extra
activities.best_when: The 2025 run was Nov 22 to Jan 3 (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas); 2026 dates not yet confirmed. Go on a weeknight.

activities.title: Hill Country Flyer vintage train (Cedar Park to Burnet)
activities.what: Restored historic railcars (diesel-pulled) make a 66-mile round trip over the South San Gabriel River trestle and through Short Creek Canyon, with a 2-hour layover on Burnet's historic square. Fall 2026 extras include the Texas Wine Flyer (Oct 11, Nov 8 and 22) and holiday North Pole trains.
activities.access_note: A wheelchair lift raises riders from the platform to the car door and can also be used by anyone who struggles with stairs. Doors are 27 in. wide. Wheelchair seating is only in the Buckeye Trail and Eagle Cliff cars, and a transfer chair is available; arrange in advance at 512-915-2340. The trip takes 6.5 hours total, which is long for an elderly rider.
activities.cost: Prices not posted on the event page; see etix.com
activities.best_when: Saturdays; the fall weather is pleasant

activities.title: Park Road 1C scenic drive, Bastrop to Buescher (Lost Pines)
activities.what: A hilly 12-mile, 30 mph road through the Lost Pines forest, recovering from past wildfires, between Bastrop and Buescher state parks. Scenery unlike the rest of the Hill Country.
activities.access_note: The whole experience is from the car. Bastrop SP also has an all-terrain wheelchair you can reserve (512-321-2101). Reservations are recommended because the park often reaches capacity. There is also a screwworm alert on the park page (not relevant to visitors in cars).
activities.cost: Bastrop SP day use $5 adult, free 12 and under. TPWD lists no separate road fee; one third-party guide mentions $3 per adult for a single drive-through, so confirm at the gate.
activities.best_when: Fall and winter daylight; the park is open 6am to 10pm

activities.title: Vanishing Texas River Cruise, Lake Buchanan
activities.what: A 2-hour Scenic Wilderness Cruise running year-round since 1981, from Lake Buchanan up the Colorado River to Fall Creek Falls: canyon walls, wildlife and birding. A 4-hour Ultimate Eagle Cruise runs Nov to Feb for wintering bald eagles.
activities.access_note: On board, the lower deck is fully climate-controlled with restrooms and tables and chairs; the top deck is covered but open. The catch is getting to the boat. Several reviewers say the walk from the hilly parking lot down the long walkways to the boat is steep. One got 90-year-old parents aboard with some difficulty, and an 83-year-old with a walker managed. Call 512-756-6986 to ask about drop-off or help. Check in 25 minutes early. Trips are cancelled for lake wind advisories. You can bring a picnic.
activities.cost: Not published on the site (booked through FareHarbor). No refunds after noon the day before.
activities.best_when: Year-round; Nov to Feb for eagles

activities.title: Blue Bonnet Cafe, Marble Falls
activities.what: A classic cafe since 1929 with breakfast all day, chicken fried steak and famous pies. Pie Happy Hour Mon to Fri 3 to 5pm (reported $4 for a slice plus a drink).
activities.access_note: No ramp information is published. It takes no reservations and the whole party must be present to be seated, which is hard for a big group at peak times. There are curbside parking spots near Birdie's Market (call ahead, 830-693-2344, and stay in the car), handy if grandma is worn out.
activities.best_when: Mon to Sat 7am to 8pm, Sun 7am to 1:45pm. Weekday 3 to 5pm for pie happy hour.

activities.title: Lookout Mountain overlook (RR 1431, between Kingsland and Granite Shoals)
activities.what: An overlook at 1,585 ft looking over Lake LBJ, best at sunset.
activities.access_note: 101 Highland Lakes calls it the easiest overlook in the area to visit, since you can drive right up to it. Pull-off size and any facilities are unknown. On the same list, Balcones Canyonlands, Inks Lake and Hidden Falls all need hiking or off-road vehicles, so they are not for grandma.
activities.best_when: Sunset

activities.title: Eagle Eye Observatory stargazing, Canyon of the Eagles (Lake Buchanan)
activities.what: Guided nighttime telescope sessions for nebulas, star clusters and galaxies on a hilltop above Lake Buchanan. The Austin Astronomical Society also runs periodic free public star parties here.
activities.access_note: Walking distance from parking, seating and ground surface are unconfirmed, and it is dark at night. Ask about closest parking when booking (512-473-3366). For the free AAS star parties the park charges $5 per adult, $2 for seniors and disabled visitors, and kids 12 and under are free.
activities.cost: $25 adult / $15 ages 5 to 12 / free 4 and under (guided sessions)
activities.best_when: Clear, moonless nights. Sessions usually start between 8 and 10:30pm, by reservation.

activities.title: Walkway of Lights, Lakeside Park, Marble Falls
activities.what: About 2 million holiday lights along the Lake Marble Falls waterfront downtown.
activities.access_note: This is a walk-through display, not a drive-through. Path surface, accessibility and parking are not published. The lakeside La Quinta's balconies reportedly overlook it, which could be an option for grandma.
activities.best_when: Late November to Dec 31

activities.title: LBJ Ranch driving tour (Stonewall)
activities.what: A 6-mile self-guided drive with 19 stops through LBJ's ranch along the Pedernales River: the Junction School, his birthplace, the family cemetery, and the Show Barn with ranger talks. It takes 30 to 120 minutes.
activities.access_note: Pick up the free driving permit at the LBJ State Park and Historic Site visitor center in Stonewall (8:30am to 4pm). Ranch entry is 9am to 4:30pm and you must exit by 5pm. The Texas White House complex (house, Hangar visitor center, JetStar, vehicle display) is CLOSED for rehabilitation. The Pedernales flooded July 16, 2026 (highest since 1979), but the NPS alerts page currently shows the driving tour open.
activities.best_when: Morning or late afternoon; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day

activities.title: Wildseed Farms, Fredericksburg
activities.what: A 200-acre wildflower farm and vineyard on US 290 with a half-mile trail through butterfly gardens and production fields. It also has an estate wine tasting room, the BrewBonnet Biergarten, a market and a nursery.
activities.access_note: Trails are wide and wheelchair accessible, with benches and shaded pavilions along the way. No loaner wheelchair or cart service was found. Grandma can also just sit in the biergarten or tasting room.
activities.best_when: Farm daily 10am to 6pm; tasting room Mon to Sat 11 to 6, Sun 12 to 6. Spring is peak bloom.

activities.title: Luckenbach, Texas
activities.what: The tiny song-famous town with a general store, bar and dance hall. There is free live music daily under the oaks.
activities.access_note: Listings report accessible parking near the entrance, an accessible entrance and accessible restrooms, but only limited accessible seating, so bring a folding chair to be safe. Fredericksburg officials said downtown and wineries kept operating through the July 2026 Pedernales flood.
activities.best_when: Afternoons. Mon to Wed 9am to 9pm, Thu to Sat 9am to 10pm, Sun 9am to 9pm.

activities.title: National Museum of the Pacific War + Fredericksburg Main Street
activities.what: A major WWII museum (Admiral Nimitz and George H.W. Bush galleries) right on Fredericksburg's Main Street, plus shopping and dining along Main.
activities.access_note: The museum lends wheelchairs free for touring the Bush and Nimitz galleries, and the galleries are wheelchair accessible. The outdoor Pacific Combat Zone has uneven terrain and closes at 3pm. Exhibits include flashing lights and loud gunfire and explosion sounds. Main Street shops stayed open after the July 2026 flood.
activities.best_when: Wed to Mon 9am to 5pm; closed Tuesdays

activities.title: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area (view the dome + dark-sky park)
activities.what: A giant pink granite dome north of Fredericksburg and an International Dark Sky Park with ranger-led star parties.
activities.access_note: The summit hike is steep and not for grandma; this stop is for looking at the dome from the park road and day-use area. No accessible viewing platform was confirmed (TPWD's accessibility page returned 404). Reservations are required on weekends and holidays, recommended other days, and the park sells out. The gate is open 6:30am to 8pm; the park is open to 10pm. It is closed to the public for hunts on Oct 12-16, Nov 2-6, Nov 30-Dec 4, Dec 18-21 and Jan 25-29. A burn ban is in effect.
activities.best_when: Weekdays; late afternoon light on the dome; ranger star parties (check the events page)

activities.title: Willow City Loop scenic drive
activities.what: A 13-mile rural road north of Fredericksburg through ranch land, granite hills and valleys. It is the Hill Country's most famous bluebonnet drive.
activities.access_note: Private ranch land is on both sides: stay on the road right-of-way and never cross fences (ranchers enforce this). The narrow road means viewing from the car is the plan anyway. Driving south to north, most of the flowers are in the second half.
activities.best_when: Late March to mid-April for peak bluebonnets; a pleasant drive year-round. Weekdays at golden hour.

activities.title: Johnson City Lights Spectacular + PEC headquarters lights
activities.what: Downtown Johnson City's holiday lights. The PEC headquarters has 1M+ lights on its oak trees plus themed displays. In 2025 there was also a laser show on the courthouse because its usual lights were paused for construction.
activities.access_note: The official FAQ says all local displays are wheelchair accessible to view. Street parking is along non-residential downtown streets and near the courthouse (101 E. Pecan Dr); arrive early on Saturdays. I could not confirm whether you can view it without leaving the car.
activities.best_when: The 2025 run was Nov 28 to Jan 4, lights on 5:45pm to midnight; 2026 dates not yet posted. Weeknights are less crowded.

activities.title: Garner State Park (Frio River)
activities.what: A cypress-lined Frio River park with a dam, dance pavilion, concessions and a hilly park road. This is the classic Frio canyon scenery.
activities.access_note: FLOOD FLAG: The park stayed open through the July 2026 flood (the Frio crested about 7 ft over the dam) and the river recovered quickly. Swimming is at your own risk with no lifeguards. Closed trails: Blinn River Trail, White Rock Cave Trail, and parts of the Madrone and lower CCC Entrance Road trails. Scenic Overlook construction is suspended with the sidewalk closed. A burn ban is in effect as of Sept 17, 2026. Accessible river-view parking is unconfirmed; call 830-232-6132. Reserve a day pass.
activities.best_when: Fall weekdays when it is quiet

activities.title: Twisted Sisters drive (RR 335 / 336 / 337)
activities.what: A 100 to 120 mile loop around Leakey, Vanderpool and Camp Wood through limestone ridges, river valleys and wide canyon views. It is the most dramatic scenery you can see from a car in the region.
activities.access_note: The roads are narrow with blind curves, including about 65 curves in one 15-mile section, so carsickness is a real risk for grandma. Drive one leg (e.g. RR 337 Vanderpool to Leakey) rather than the full loop. FLAG: the Lone Star Motorcycle Museum in Vanderpool shows as CLOSED on Yelp (May 2026).
activities.best_when: Daylight only. Late Oct to Nov pairs it with maple color near Vanderpool.

activities.title: Frio Bat Flight (Frio Cave near Concan)
activities.what: At dusk the operator says 10+ million Mexican free-tailed bats pour out of Frio Cave. You follow the guide 2 miles across the ranch in your own car, then take a short walk up a hill.
activities.access_note: Handicapped parking is available. If someone can't make the walk, tell a guide; the operator says someone may drive them up once the walkway clears. Meet at the gate 1/3 mile down FM 2690, the first gate right after the Frio River bridge.
activities.cost: $12 general admission / $10 kids 10 and under / free 5 and under (reported)
activities.best_when: The season runs mid-March through September with no October tours, so the 2026 season ends within days. Plan for spring or summer 2027; June to August is best.

activities.title: Lost Maples State Natural Area (fall color)
activities.what: Uvalde bigtooth maples in a narrow canyon near Vanderpool, the best fall foliage in Texas.
activities.access_note: The best color is along the trails. I could not find any accessible viewing spot that avoids walking (TPWD's accessibility page returned 404). Fall weekends and Thanksgiving week bring traffic delays and capacity closures, and lots close when full. Book a day pass up to 30 days ahead (512-389-8900) and go on a weekday. Treat it as a drive-by or scenic lunch trip for grandma, not a hike.
activities.best_when: Late October through November (check TPWD foliage reports)

activities.title: Lost Maples Cafe, Utopia
activities.what: A family-run small-town cafe open since 1986, known for homemade pies (coconut and lemon meringue, fudge pecan, buttermilk). A good lunch stop on a Frio or Lost Maples drive.
activities.access_note: Accessibility is not published. Hours were recently cut back for the school year, so call before going (830-966-2221). 384 FM 187 / Main St, Utopia.
activities.best_when: Daytime; confirm hours by phone
